Star can be a little shy and quiet at first whilst she gets to know you but does like a fuss. She is now starting to come out of her shell a little and can get giddy and excited at times. She loves her walks and can pull when she is interested in a certain smell. As she gets more confident and settles we do believe her cheeky terrier side will come out. She certainly has plenty of energy!

Due to her still being a little nervous Star may require multiple meets so she can get to know her new family before going home. Her new family will need to be patient and understanding whilst she is settling in and getting used to her new surroundings.

We think that it is best for Star to be rehomed with children who are 16 years and over – Subject to a successful meet.

Star has interacted well with other dogs whilst in our care so can potentially be rehomed with another dog of a similar temperament – subject to a successful meet.

We wouldn’t recommend Star to be rehomed with cats due to her breed.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3  months.

name: Kong
description:
Kong is a loveable and friendly giant who is always happy,  and maybe a little too enthusiastic, to say hello to everyone he meets. Kong is still only a young boy so doesn’t know his strength and size. Further training will need to be done to ensure he can be taught manners. Kong does currently like to jump up so a family with experience around large breeds would be beneficial. Kong is a sweet boy and always greets staff in the morning with a blanket in his mouth and a very waggy tail!

Kong came into our care as a stray from another kennels so we don’t have any history on him or know if he has lived in a home before. Due to this and his size, Kong is best to be rehomed to an adult only home.

Kong has interacted well with friendly dogs whilst in our care but can be very boisterous and over the top. He will need continuous socialisation to help train him to react appropriately around dogs. He could potentially be rehomed with another dog that has a calm and friendly temperament but it is preferred for him to be the only dog in the home so that he can get all of the attention to help with his training. This would be subject to a successful meet.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3  months.

name: Ebony
description:
Meet our gorgeous Ebony!  She was a little nervous and unsure at first, but it didn’t take her long to warm up and show us her lovely personality.  She is a very sweet and affectionate girl who really enjoys attention and being around people.  Once she feels comfortable, her giddy and playful side quickly comes out.  Ebony can sometimes forget just how big she is, especially when she gets excited, but it’s all part of her fun and loveable character.  Ebony knows her basic commands and is very keen to learn.  She is a very strong girl on the lead, so she will need someone who is confident and able to manage her strength while continuing her lead training.  She was also a very good girl during her visit to the vets and behaved brilliantly while having her vaccination.  Overall, Ebony is a big, affectionate, playful girl with lots of love to give.  Once she gets to know you, her sweet and silly personality really shines through.  She would benefit from a private secure garden. Previous experience with large breed dogs would be preferred.

Ebony has socialised well with other dogs whilst in our care so we feel she could potentially live with another dog of similar size and energy levels following a successful meet and greet.

As Ebony came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on her so would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Ziggy
description:
Ziggy is full of life  and energy as he is a young boy. He is a super friendly boy, with a big personality and absolutely loves playing in our enclosed area chasing balls around. At times Ziggy can get a little mouthy and will need his new family to continue helping him learn manners. With Ziggy still being young and high energy, he would need an active home who are able to give him the exercise he needs along with mental stimulation.

Whilst in our care Ziggy has socialised really well with other dogs and often enjoys his daily walks alongside them. For this reason, we do believe he could potentially live with another dog, able to keep up with his high energy levels – subject to a successful meet.

Ziggy wouldn’t be suitable to live with cat or any small animals.

Due to Ziggy coming into our care as a stray, we don’t have any previous history on him. Ziggy would be best suited to an experienced home, ideally having knowledge of his breed, with children no younger than 16 years old – subject to a successful meet.

name: Theia
description:
Meet Theia!  She can be very nervous and unsure when she first meets new people.  The world can feel like a scary place to her, and she needs time to get to know new people at her own pace.  But once she realises she is safe and she begins to trust you, a completely different side of her comes out.  Underneath those nerves is a very sweet, affectionate girl who absolutely loves a fuss and being around the people she trusts.  Theia already knows some basic commands and is keen to engage with you.  When she gets excited, she does tend to jump up to greet you, so will need some continued work on keeping all four paws on the floor.  Kennel life can be difficult for Theia and she does bark while in her kennel.  She also currently uses her bed as a toilet at times, so her new family will need to be prepared to work patiently on her toilet training and help her establish a good routine in a home environment.  What Theia needs most is someone who will give her time, reassurance and positive experiences to help her learn that the world isn’t such a scary place.  She will benefit from a private secure garden.

Theia has socialised well with other dogs whilst in our care and is very bouncy and playful.  We feel she could potentially live with another dog of similar size and energy levels following a successful meet and greet.

As Theia came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on her and as she can be quite timid and unsure we would like any children in the home to be 16+ years.

name: Lyra
description:
Meet Lyra!  This beautiful girl is looking for an active, experienced home where she can thrive.  She is a lovely, sweet-natured girl with a very giddy and playful personality.  Lyra absolutely loves attention and fuss and is always happy to be involved in whatever is going on.  She has lots of enthusiasm for life and certainly isn’t shy about showing it! Lyra can jump up quite a lot when she gets excited, so this is something her new adopter will need to be prepared to work on.  She is also very strong on the lead and will need someone confident and capable of handling her while they continue training.  As you would expect from a Malinois, Lyra is an active, energetic dog who will need plenty of physical exercise, mental stimulation and ongoing training and socialisation.  Due to the needs and characteristics of the breed previous knowledge and experience of the breed or similar high-drive working breeds is required. Underneath all that energy is an incredibly sweet girl who loves affection and companionship. She will need a private secure garden.

Lyra has socialised well with other dogs, and is very giddy and playful with them.  We do feel she could potentially live with another dog of similar size and energy levels following a successful meet and greet. (must be neutered).

As she came into the home as a stray, we have no previous history on her so would prefer any children in the home to be 16+ years.

name: Duke
description:
This lovely boy is Duke!  He is looking for a patient and understanding home where he can truly thrive.  When he first came into us he was very nervous, but given the time and space to build trust his friendly and affectionate nature shines through.  He can be quite vocal and will bark to let you know when he’d like some attention.  When he gets over excited or over stimulated he can become a little mouthy, so he will need owners who can calmly redirect this behaviour and continue his training and socialisation.  He already knows some basic commands and is eager to engage.  Being a large, strong boy, he does pull on the lead, so he will benefit from ongoing lead training and someone confident enough to manage his strength.  He is currently unsure around other dogs and would be happiest as the only dog in the home, where his new adopter can continue his socialisation with other dogs in a controlled environment with lots of positive reinforcement.  This handsome lad is looking for an active home, that can provide patience, consistency and plenty of exercise and mental enrichment.  He will need a private secure garden.

As he came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on him so would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Rosa
description:
Meet Rosa!  She is a beautiful and gentle soul who is searching for a calm, loving home where she can enjoy her golden years.  When you first meet Rosa, she can be timid and nervous around new people and unfamiliar surroundings.  She needs time to feel safe, so her new adopter will need to be patient and allow her to build trust at her own pace.  Once she knows you, Rosa’s sweet, friendly nature begins to shine through, and she forms lovely bonds with those who give her the time she needs.  Rosa would thrive in a quiet retirement home with a calm routine and understanding owners who appreciate that the best relationships are worth waiting for.  She will need several meet and greets before the adoption can take place to ensure she feels comfortable with her new adopter. She has socialised well with other dogs whilst in our care so we feel she could possibly live with another calm, older dog following a successful meet and greet. If you have a peaceful home, a kind heart, and the patience to let Rosa blossom in her own time, you will be rewarded with the companionship of a truly lovely girl who deserves to spend her retirement surrounded by love.

As she came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on her and as she can be a little timid around new people we would like any children in the home to be 16+ years.

name: Raven
description:
Raven is a gentle, sweet-natured girl looking for a patient and understanding home where she can build her confidence at her own pace.

She has been no trouble in our care and has no issues with feeding or cleaning. When she first arrived, she was extremely nervous and wouldn’t approach for attention. By day five she had made small steps, coming over for a sniff, but she is still very worried about being stroked and is understandably wary of new people, often keeping her tail tucked between her legs.

As Raven came into our care as a stray, we don’t know what she may have experienced in the past, but it’s clear she will need kind, committed owners who are willing to give her the time, patience and reassurance she needs to flourish.

Although she has coped around other dogs in our environment, she is very unsure of them and would be happiest as the only dog in the home, where she can have her own space and settle without added pressure.

With time, patience and plenty of love, Raven has every chance of growing in confidence and becoming a wonderful, loyal companion.

name: Marshall
description:
This handsome boy is full of life and absolutely loves people! Friendly, affectionate, and always ready for attention, he has a big personality and an even bigger heart.

He can be very excitable and still behaves very much like a puppy, so he’ll need owners who are committed to continuing his training. He is strong on the lead and pulls when walking, but with consistency and patience he is eager to learn. Once he settles, he enjoys being stroked and is happy to be handled all over.

He is looking for an active home that can give him the time, guidance, and love he deserves to help him become the best companion he can be.

Suitable for children aged 14+due to his size, strength, and bouncy nature.

name: Prism
description:
Prism is an ex racing greyhound that has come into our care after retiring. Prism is looking for a home to call her own after always living in kennels. Prism is a sweet and gentle girl who enjoys attention and a cuddle. Prism walks lovely on the lead but can still react to certain wildlife due to her prey drive. Prism has never lived in a home before so will need a patient family that is willing to give her time to settle and adjust to her new surroundings.

Prism has interacted well with dogs whilst in our care and has had a kennel mate previously. Due to this prism can be rehomed with another dog of similar size – subject to a successful meet. Prism isn’t yet spade so any male dogs would have to be castrated.

Prism has interacted well with staff and volunteers so we believe that she can be rehomed with children who are 12 years and over – Subject to a successful meet.

name: Elias
description:
Elias is a very sweet and friendly boy. He came into our care as a stray so we don’t have any background information on him. He has always been friendly with staff and volunteers whilst here. Elias can be a little strong on the lead due to his size so some basic lead training would be beneficial for him. We are looking for an active home for Elias as he has a lot of energy and would enjoy going on lots of adventures. Elias is a calm boy in his kennel and loves to have some down time with a tasty chew.

Elias is a friendly boy but due to his size we believe that it would be best for him to be rehomed with children over 14 years and over – Subject to a successful meet.

Elias has interacted well with dogs whilst in our care, he has a submissive nature around other dogs. We believe that Elias can be rehomed with another dog with the same energy levels.

name: Hunter
description:
If you’re looking for a loyal best friend, this handsome boy could be the one for you. He has a heart full of love and greets everyone with a wagging tail and a face that lights up with excitement. Affectionate, gentle, and eager to please, all he really wants is to be by your side.

He walks well on the lead, enjoys being groomed, knows basic commands such as sit, wait, and down, and is happy to be handled all over. He has also shown friendly, positive interactions with other dogs in our care.

Hunter could live with children aged 12 and over who confident and respectful around dogs. This sweet boy would thrive in a home where he can finally enjoy the love, attention, and companionship he deserves. In return, he’ll give you endless affection and be a wonderful, devoted companion.

name: Dakota
description:
Dakota is looking for her forever home, and she has so much love to give.  She’s an incredibly sweet, friendly girl who absolutely adores people.  If you’re happy to give her plenty of fuss, she’ll be in her element!  Despite her size, she is a gentle soul with a lovely nature and enjoys spending time with her favourite humans.  She already knows some basic commands and is very eager to please so would benefit from further training.  Being a young, strong dog, she can be powerful on the lead, so her new adopter will need to be confident and committed to continue her lead training.  Because of this, she will be best suited to an active home where she can enjoy plenty of exercise, adventures and mental stimulation.  If you are looking for a loyal, affectionate companion with a heart as big as she is, this lovely girl could be the one for you.  She will need a private secure garden.

She has socialised with other dogs whilst in our care, and is very playful and can be too much for other dogs as she does get in their face so for this reason we feel she would be best rehomed as the only dog in the home where she can continue to learn manners and boundaries around other dogs will the full support of her new adopter with lots of positive reinforcement.

As Dakota came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on her so would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Coco
description:
Coco came into our care as a stray so we don’t have any background information on her. She is a sweet but shy girl at times. She does get excitable once she gets to know you. With time and patience she will be a great companion for any home. She loves her walks and going outside for plenty of sniffs. As she came in as a stray, she would benefit from some basic training to help her flourish.

Coco can be rehomed with children 12+ – subject to a successful meet.

Coco has interacted well with dogs whilst in our care but can be a little nervous at first. We believe that she could potentially be rehomed with another dog of a similar size and with a calm temperament.

name: Daisy
description:
Daisy was previously a racing greyhound who has been brought up in kennels. She is a smaller girl in comparison to a typical greyhound but still does have quite a high prey drive. She makes up for her size with her big personality, she is a very sweet and loving girl but can be a little cheeky at times. As like most greyhounds, Daisy enjoys a good walk and sniff in the woods, with the occasional time off lead in an enclosed area to burn off energy but will equally spend lots time relaxing on a comfy cosy bed. Daisy is after someone that is looking to give a dog lots of love and companionship, which she hasn’t previously had in her life. She in return will give you unconditional love.

Daisy can be a little nippy at times so we feel that it would be best for her to be rehomed with children who are 14 years or older – subject to a successful meet.

Daisy is currently paired and used to living with another greyhound in kennels. She has also interacted well with other dogs whilst on walks so we believe that she could be rehomed with another dog of a similar size and temperament – again subject to a successful meet.

Due to Daisy being an ex-racer it wouldn’t be suitable for him to be rehomed with cats or small furries.

name: Treats
description:
Treats is a retired racing greyhound who has spent all of his life in kennels and is now ready to find his forever home. Treats is an affectionate boy who is after someone who wants to give him the life that he deserves full of adventures and love. Treats is an energetic boy who loves going for his walks and having off lead time zooming around the enclosed compound area. Once he has burnt off his energy he is ready to snooze away the day on his comfy bed.

With his out going personality and loving heart, he would fit into many different households that can offer him kindness, exercise, and plenty of cosy spots to curl up in. In return, this gorgeous soul will bring warmth, devotion, and endless companionship.

We believe that Treats can be rehomed with children who are 12 years and over – subject to a successful meet.

Treats is currently paired and is used to living with other greyhounds in kennels, he has also walked and interacted well with other dogs during his time as the home so could possibly be rehomed with another dog of similar size and temperament – again subject to a successful meet.

Due to treats being an ex-racer it wouldn’t be suitable for him to be rehomed with cats or small furries.

name: Eileen
description:
This gorgeous girl is Eileen.  She is searching for her forever home where she can enjoy all the fuss and attention she deserves.  She is an incredibly friendly girl who absolutely loves being around people.  Whether it’s cuddles on the sofa, a gentle scratch behind the ears, or simply spending time by your side, she’s happiest when she’s receiving attention from her favourite humans.  Out and about, she is a pleasure to walk and is good on the lead, making her an enjoyable companion for daily strolls and adventures.  Don’t let her laid-back Bulldog looks fool you – this girl has a playful side too!  Tennis balls are her absolute favourite, and she loves nothing more than a game of fetch or carrying her prized ball around with her.  As with many Bulldogs, we would prefer applicants to have previous breed experience and a good understanding of the breed’s specific needs.  Her new adopter should be committed to providing the care, companionship and lifestyle that will allow her to thrive.  This sweet natured girl has so much love to give and is ready to become a cherished member of her forever family.  She would benefit from a private secure garden.

Eileen has been rehomed previously but was returned to us as she wasn’t too keen on the man in the house but she was absolutely fine with the lady.  We are now looking for an all female home where we think Eileen would be most relaxed, where the new adopters can work with her issues surrounding males.  We have male staff here at the home and she has been absolutely fine with them.  She will need an experienced home with adopters that have previous experience with the breed.  She would be best suited to an adult only home.

Eileen has socialised well with other dogs and is very playful, so we feel she could be rehomed with another dog (must be neutered) of similar size and energy levels following a successful meet and greet.

name: Pudding
description:
This handsome boy is Pudding.  He is a friendly, affectionate lad who loves nothing more than a good fuss and plenty of attention from his people.  He is a big, strong boy with a bouncy personality and can be a little over-enthusiastic when meeting people.  He does have a habit of jumping up for attention and sometimes forgets just how big he is, so his new adopter will need to be prepared to continue working on his manners and help him channel his excitement appropriately.  On walks, he does sometimes rag his lead at first as he gets over excited, but does settle down and walk nicely and more calmly, he does enjoy getting out and about.  Due to his size and exuberant nature, we are looking for an adopter with experience of large, strong and bouncy dogs who can provide consistent guidance, ongoing training and plenty of exercise and mental stimulation.  In return, you will gain a loving, loyal companion who thrives on human interaction and is sure to bring lots of fun and affection into his new home.  He will need a private secure garden.

Pudding has socialised well with other dogs whilst in our care so we feel he could potentially live with another dog of similar size following a successful meet and greet.

As pudding came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on him so would prefer any children in the home to be 16+ years.

name: Scooby
description:
Meet our handsome boy Scooby, who is slowly learning that the world isn’t such a scary place after all.  When he first arrived with us, he was extremely timid and unsure around people. Since, then he has made lovely progress in the care of our kennel staff.  He will now happily take treats from familiar people and is beginning to enjoy gentle strokes and attention once he feels comfortable.  One thing that brings out his personality is playtime – he absolutely loves his toys.  Because of his nervous nature, he will need patient adopters who are willing to give him the time he needs to build trust.  Multiple meet and greets will be required before any adoption can take place so he can get to know his new family at his own pace.  He gains a lot of confidence from other dogs, so we feel he would thrive in a home with a calm and friendly resident dog who can help show him the ropes and continue building his confidence. He will need an experienced owner that has previously had very timid dogs.  With time, understanding and patience, this sweet boy has so much potential to blossom into a loyal and loving companion.  Scooby will need a private secure garden.

As Scooby came into the home as a stray, we have no previous history on him and as he is extremely timid we would prefer any children/visiting children in the home to be 16+ years.

name: Ivan
description:
This handsome lad is Ivan!  He’s a friendly, affectionate boy with a big personality and an even bigger heart.  Full of energy and enthusiasm, he’s always ready for fun and loves nothing more than chasing after tennis balls.  He’s a very excitable and giddy dog who doesn’t always realise his own size, so he can jump up when greeting people or when he’s excited.  He is also quite vocal at times, especially when he wants your attention.   He knows his basic commands and is eager to interact with people, but he will need continued training and guidance, particularly when out walking as he is very strong on the lead.  Due to his size and strength, he would benefit from an experienced and active owner who can continue his training and provide him with plenty of exercise and mental stimulation.  Ivan would benefit from a private secure garden where he can safely have off lead time to play fetch with his tennis balls.

Ivan has interacted well with other dogs whilst in our care so we feel he potentially could be rehomed with another dog of similar size and energy levels following a successful meet and greet.

As Ivan came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on him so would prefer any children in the home to be 16+ years.

name: Buddy
description:
This loveable boy is Buddy! He is the perfect mix of playful energy and affectionate companionship. He’s a friendly, easy-going lad who absolutely adores people and loves being the centre of attention.  Full of character, he’s excitable, giddy and always ready to make you smile.  Whether it’s cuddles on the sofa or a game in the garden, he just wants to be involved in everything you do.  He is bursting with energy and would thrive in an active home where he can enjoy plenty of exercise, playtime and mental stimulation.  Fetch is one of his favourite games, and he will happily keep you entertained for hours chasing after a ball.  Buddy is incredibly affectionate and loves a fuss, he will make a loyal, loving companion.  One thing to note : He is quite the escape artist, so he will need a private secure garden and owners who are mindful of doors, gates and fencing.  When Buddy came into us he had an Entropian (an eye condition) which has now been repaired and he is healing nicely.

Buddy has interacted well with other dogs whilst in our care so we feel he could potentially live with another high energy dog following a successful meet and greet.

As Buddy came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on him so would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Mercy
description:
Mercy came into our care as a stray, very shut down and scared. With time and patience staff managed to win her round and she slowly came out of her shell. Little by little we are seeing her lovely personality shine through. With those she trusts, Mercy has shown to be very affectionate and sweet lady.

She is still a little unsure, especially around men. However, this is something we are currently helping her with, and her new family must be willing to continue this.

With Mercy being nervous and unsure she is looking for a very patient and understanding adult only home, where she can develop and settle in at her own pace. Her new family must have the time to be able to come and meet her multiple times so she can get to know you before she goes home.

Mercy is currently also having socialisation training around dogs to build up her confidence. She is still unsure of other dogs so needs to be the only dog in the home.

name: Toby
description:
Toby is a very loveable bouncy boy. He is still just a puppy so is going to need all of the basic training to help him grow up to be a well behaved boy. Toby is bouncy and pulls a lot of the lead due to excitement. Toby needs an enclosed garden where he is able to spend time zooming around and playing with toys to help burn off all of the energy that he has. Toby needs a family who has a lot of time to put into his training and exercise each day, especially for the first few months. Toby will need to be with a very active family who can take him on lots of adventures to help burn off his energy and to help socialise him.  Toby is a loveable and friendly boy but needs training to teach him manners.

Toby can be rehomed with dog savvy children who are 12 years and over – subject to a successful meet.

Toby is a typical puppy around other dogs, always wanting to play and goes in feet first. Toby needs more socialsiation around other dogs to teach him how to appropriately interact. When toby meets a dog he is very friendly and just wants to play.  We think that he could be rehomed with another young dog of similar size and a dog who has a lot of energy and a high tolerance to dogs to keep up with toby’s playfulness.

Due to Toby’s breed, it is not advisable for him to live with cats.

Toby has lived in a home previously so we do have more information to provide to potential adopters.

Please do not apply for Toby if you are going on holiday within the next 3 months.

name: Cali
description:
Cali was a very nervous girl when she first arrived at the home, she came in as a stray so we don’t know much about her history. It has taken a lot of time and patience for Cali to show us her excitable, bubbly personality. Due to this we are after an experienced home that has the time to get to know Cali here before she goes home. Once Cali gets to know you she loves a fuss and attention.  She loves going out for woodland walks and gets very giddy for her lead, she pulls a little on the lead, due to her size, so would benefit from some on going training. Cali enjoys an offlead run in the enclosed compound where she can chase after a tennis ball.

Cali will need to live in an Adult only home with an enclosed garden where she has space to roam about at her leisure.  She used to be a little nervous and unsure around certain dogs, we have been working with her on this and introducing her to dogs which is helping her social interactions. She is now a friendly girl with most of the dogs on site and can say a lovely face to face hello and even tries to play with others. She will need continued training to help with her socialisation. We still feel that Cali will need to be the only dog in the house.

If you think you can give this gorgeous girl her forever home please apply!

name: Rue
description:
Meet Rue!  Rue was a little timid when she first came into us but it didn’t take her long to come around and show us her crazy and fun loving side.  Rue absolutely loves playing with toys especially her plastic ring, she will chase around the compound with it all day if she could.  She is a real character and will come over for some fuss and then she’s off again with her ring. When she’s not zooming around the compound you will find her going on long walks exploring and having a sniff about.  She is strong on the lead so will need continued lead training.  We are looking for an active home for Rue that have previous experience with larger boisterous dogs.  Rue would benefit from a private secure garden so she can safely have off lead time with her toys. Continued training and socialisation is a must for this gorgeous girl.

Rue has socialised with other dogs whilst in our care and although is very playful with them she is very boisterous and has no boundaries so for this reason we think she would be best rehomed as the only dog in the home and the adopter to continue her socialisation around other dogs so she can learn how to behave respectfully around them.

As Rue came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on her so would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Pearl
description:
This talkative girl is Pearl.  She is a very affectionate, confident and friendly girl that is always up for lots of fuss and strokes.  She can be very vocal when she wants your attention so probably not suitable for an apartment/flat.  She enjoys her walks everyday having a sniff about and saying hello to everyone she meets.  She is very strong on the lead so will need an experienced owner that is used to powerful dogs. Pearl would benefit from a private secure garden.

Pearl has socialised with other dogs whilst in our care, she can be a little unsure at first but does come around after a bit, so we feel she may be best suited as the only dog in the home where she can take her time getting used to other dogs with lots of positive reinforcement from her new adopter.

As Pearl came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on her so would prefer any children in the home to be 12+ years.

name: Mabel
description:
Mabel came in to our care as an ex racer, meaning she does have quite a high prey drive when out on her walks! She does walk beautifully until she sees a squirrel and then she’s off! She is a very chilled out girl in her kennel and does love to give you a scare when she’s under a blanket hiding!

This lovely girl is looking for a home where she can relax and enjoy her retirement years curled up in a bed or sprawled out on a couch! We do feel she could live in a home with another dog as she has interacted well with other dogs whilst being in our care. This would be subject to a successful meet. However shecannotlive in home with small animals such as cats, due to her high prey drive. We also feel she could potentially live in a home with a family where children are 12 years and older – subject to a successful meet.

Although Mabel does love being in her beds, she really does enjoy being out and about on her walks with her greyhound pals! So she would appreciate a home that would give her the best of both worlds – a lovely walk followed by snuggles with her favourite people! Please apply today to give her a forever home that she deserves so much!

name: Shadow
description:
Shadow is a very cheeky boy has been super friendly to our staff and volunteers since he came in to our care. With him being an ex racer, he does have a high prey drive so can try to chase squirrels whilst out for his walks! He was paired in his kennel prior to her going home and will walk well with other greyhounds. He does seem unsure around other breeds of dogs, especially smaller breeds and will be quite vocal towards them. The staff and volunteers have been doing socialisation training with him here and he is improving slowly, his new family would need to continue this to help with improve further.

Shadow will have spent most of his life in kennels with his racing background, so he may feel a little nervous going in to a home environment. We also do not know if he is house trained or toilet trained due to this. He loves to lie in his comfy beds after his walks – we sometimes catch him upside down showing his belly off!

We think Shadow would prefer to be the only dog in the home, with him being a little unsure around other dogs at moment. However, he could potentially live with another greyhound if a meet and greet with him went well and depending on the other dogs temperament. He could also potentially live with children 12 years and older – subject to a successful meet.

Shadow would love a home where he could relax and enjoy his retirement years and rest on a comfy bed (or couch) of his own!

name: Willow
description:
This stunning girl is Willow.  Willow was very nervous and unsure for the first few weeks she was with us.  She was very vocal when the staff went in her kennel and would hide in the back.  The staff have worked hard with her to gain her trust and she has come out of her shell now and is showing her playful friendly side.  We are looking for an experienced owner for Willow that have had nervous large breed dogs previously and will work with her on her confidence, doing this at Willow’s pace and not too rushed.  She is a very independent girl who will come to you when she wants some attention, her toys are her number 1 priority in life.  Willow is very food orientated and will sit nicely for her treats.  This said she is a little bit chunky at the moment so is on weight management food to help her loose a few pounds, and well done to Willow and the staff as she has managed to lose 3kg up to now!  She will need continued training and socialisation. Willow will benefit from a private secure garden where she can have off lead time to relax and have a sniff about.

Willow has socialised ok with other dogs whilst in our care but we feel she would be best rehomed as the only dog in the home as she does prefer her own space.

As Willow came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on her so would prefer an adult only household.

name: Bruce
description:
Bruce is a very active and playful boy who absolutely loves chasing around our compound with his toys.  He can be quite boisterous and bouncy when he is excited so would definitely benefit from continued training and socialisation. He can be quite a strong boy on his lead too.

He will need an active home where he can get all the exercise and mental stimulation he will need every day. Bruce would benefit from a private secure garden where he can have off lead time with his toys in between his walks.

Bruce has interacted well with most dogs whilst in our care but can be very dominant with them so we feel he would be best suited to be the only dog in the home.  The new adopter will need to continue his socialisation with other dogs to improve his interactions with them.

As Bruce can get nervous and overwhelmed meeting new people, especially men, we feel that it would be best for him to go to an adult only home. He will need time to get to know you before going home. His new family will need to be able to commit to multiple meets.

Bruce is a wonderful, vibrant boy with lots of love to give to his new family! He has spent a while in kennels now so would love to find his forever home and someone to be the person to throw his ball endlessly! Do you think this could be you?

name: Todd
description:
Todd is a super friendly, but very energetic boy! He can be quite vocal towards other dogs whilst out on his walks due to wanting to play so would benefit from further training and socialisation. He enjoys treats and toys and loves a good play around with the staff in his kennel and on walks. Todd is the happiest when he is outside in our enclosed compound area off lead and running around with his toys. He would happily stay there all day! We think that Todd needs a reasonably sized fully enclosed garden that he can spend a lot of time in burning off all of his energy in between walks. Todd needs a family that is around a lot so he isn’t alone in the house for too long. His new family will need to have the time to ensure he is getting a lot of exercise every day and be able to take him to extra activities such as agility or scent work to help engage his brain and keep it stimulated.

We believe that Todd needs to be the only dog in the home so that he has all of the focus on him whilst he still needs extra training. Todd loves other dogs but can be very over the top whilst out on walks.

Additionally, we think that Todd needs to be in an adult only home.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3  months.

name: Clover
description:
This gorgeous girl is Clover!  We are looking for an experienced owner for her.  Once Clover has bonded with you she shows off her loving side, it just takes some time for her to trust new people. Once she has got to know you she doesn’t leave your side.  Clover is a very boisterous and bouncy girl who does forget just how big she is when she is jumping up at you to say hello. She would definitely benefit from puppy training classes.  She can be very silly at times but in the nicest possible way and will definitely keep you smiling.  Her new adopter must give her all the support she will need whilst she gets used to new people and places and will have to commit to regular meet and greets before the adoption could take place.  Clover will need a private secure garden.

Please only apply for this gorgeous girl if you have the experience and can commit to the training and socialisation she will need.

Clover has interacted well with other dogs whilst in our care but we do feel she would be best rehomed as the only dog so she can get 100% of the training and socialisation she will need.

As Clover came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on her so would prefer any children/visiting children to be 14+ years.

name: Rosie
description:
Rosie is a 1 year old female cross-breed with unique and lovely markings. DOB 10/7/2023.

Abandoned in woodland with her siblings at a tender age, she found refuge in a foster shelter, where she currently resides.

Rosie, a good-sized medium dog, walks well on a lead, great with other dogs & older children.

This resilient pup has undergone thorough veterinary care, including comprehensive blood tests, ensuring her seamless integration into life in the UK.

Ideal for an experienced family well-versed in dog ownership, Rosie is best suited for a household with children over 8 years old, given her size.

She comes fully vaccinated, microchipped, and equipped with a pet passport and medical papers detailing her health history.

The commitment to her well-being extends beyond adoption, with the assurance of lifetime rescue backup and ongoing support from the dedicated rescue centre.

For households with feline companions, a cat test can be conducted to assess Rosie’s compatibility.

The rescue centre emphasises their dedication to the welfare of their dogs, offering not just a new family member but a guarantee of continuous support for Rosie’s lifetime.

name: Monty
description:
Monty is a 5-year-old male Cross-Breed. He is described as a medium-sized dog and is currently in foster care in Hartlepool. He arrived in the UK in September 2025 after spending three years in Romanian foster kennels.

When Monty first arrived, he was very nervous and shy in his new surroundings. Since then, he has grown greatly in confidence and has shown himself to be a wonderful and loving dog. He is now ready to find a caring and permanent home of his own.

Monty is a very cuddly dog who forms strong bonds once he learns to trust someone. He is described as having a soft nature and being full of love. He is especially affectionate with people he knows well.

He walks nicely on a lead, which helps make his daily exercise more manageable. Although he has made great progress, he can still be nervous when meeting new people and dogs while out on walks.

Because of this, he would benefit from an understanding adopter who can continue to build his confidence at his own pace.

Monty is good with other dogs and enjoys their company. He has not been tested with cats, and he has also not been tested with children. Any introductions in these areas would need to be handled carefully and thoughtfully.

He is up to date with his vaccinations and has been neutered. Full rescue backup is provided, offering ongoing support after adoption. Monty is currently based in Hartlepool but can travel to the right home.

name: Oliver
description:
Oliver is a 1 year old male Hound Cross, a medium to large sized boy weighing around 18–20 kilograms who is currently outside the UK.

Oliver, a handsome young hound mix is with a lovely black, brown and white coat and a wonderfully easygoing nature. He was found wandering alone before being brought to safety at the Residencia Garatuxa rescue in Galicia, northern Spain.

Oliver is a confident and friendly dog who enjoys the company of people and other dogs. He is social, relaxed and not nervous or dominant, making him an easy companion to have around.

At the shelter he mixes well with the other dogs and shows a gentle, affectionate character.

He is still a young dog, around one year old or possibly even younger, so he has his whole life ahead of him and will make a wonderful addition to a family willing to give him the love and stability he deserves. He can be cat tested and child tested if required.

Oliver will be fully prepared for travel — vaccinated, microchipped, neutered and with his passport ready — and can travel to the UK to the right home.

If you are looking for a young, friendly dog who will quickly become part of the family, Oliver could be the perfect match.

As with all of our dogs, he comes with full rescue back-up.

name: Pongo
description:
Pongo is a 1-year-old male Labrador Retriever Cross. He currently weighs around 25 kg and is described as a sweet and gentle dog with a sociable nature.

Although he may appear a little shy when first meeting new people, he gradually becomes more confident once he feels safe and comfortable.

Pongo’s early life began in Italy, where he was found as a very young puppy. When he was around two months old, he and his small siblings, along with other puppies, were captured and taken to a shelter.

Life behind the bars of a shelter was not the start any young dog deserves, but fortunately his story soon took a more hopeful turn.

A kind woman in Germany decided to rescue him and offer him a chance at a better life. Thanks to her, Pongo was able to leave the shelter and move into a foster home in Germany. There he is now patiently waiting for the loving family he truly deserves.

In his foster home, Pongo is continuing to grow and learn about the world around him. He is slowly becoming accustomed to everyday things such as walking on a lead and meeting new people.

While he still needs a bit of time to build confidence, he is making steady progress and learning that people can be kind and trustworthy.

Pongo has a naturally gentle and affectionate personality. Once he gets to know someone, his sweet and friendly side quickly appears. His sociable character makes him a lovely companion who enjoys positive interactions and calm encouragement.

He is also known to get along well with other dogs and cats. This shows that he has a friendly and tolerant temperament when around other animals. With continued guidance and a patient environment, he can continue developing his social skills and confidence.

What Pongo needs most now is a family willing to offer him patience, security, and love. A calm home where he can feel safe will help him continue blossoming into the confident dog he is meant to be.

With the right people beside him, his shy side will gradually fade as his trusting and affectionate nature grows stronger.

Adopting Pongo means giving a deserving dog the stable and loving future he has been waiting for. In return, he will offer loyalty, sweetness, and companionship to the family who welcomes him into their lives.

He is simply waiting for someone to give him the chance to belong.

name: Oscar
description:
Meet Oscar, a 2 year old male English Pointer Cross who is searching for a loving forever home.

When Oscar was found, he was so thin you could count every bone in his body, and yet his tail was still wagging.

Oscar is only about two years old, but life has already asked far too much of him.

This gentle boy was found wandering the streets of Cyprus, alone, starving, and heartbreakingly thin. When we first saw him, he looked almost like a living skeleton. Every bone was visible and every step was a struggle, and yet somehow his tail still tried to wag.

Despite everything the world had done to him, Oscar still believed in kindness.

Amazingly, after a vet check, all tests were normal. Since that day, Oscar has been slowly gaining weight and strength.

Day by day he is healing. He is still painfully underweight, and the road back to health continues.

What breaks our hearts the most is how gentle he is. Oscar is incredibly loving with people. He is calm, affectionate, and grateful for every soft touch.

He gets along beautifully with other dogs and simply wants to be close to someone who cares.

After everything he has endured, Oscar deserves a family to call his own.

A home with a secure garden where he can run and feel the grass under his paws.

People who will give him patience, guidance, and love as he learns what it means to truly belong.

He loves other dogs, but he could also be the only dog if he receives the attention and affection he longs for.

Oscar has survived the worst. Now all he needs is someone to see him, really see him.

Now he deserves the chance to love and be loved.

Could you be the one who finally gives Oscar the home he has never had?

name: Jester
description:
Introducing Jester, a 4 month old male Griffon Cross who is expected to grow into a medium-sized dog of around 18–20 kg.

Jester was born on 1 November 2025 as part of a litter of six boys. His mother is a Griffon cross, and he and his brothers have been raised at the Residencia Garatuxa shelter in Galicia.

During their time at the shelter, they have had regular contact with people and other dogs. This has helped them grow into confident, sociable puppies who are comfortable around activity and noise.

Jester is affectionate, playful, and curious about the world around him. Like all puppies, he will need a family ready to guide him through training and provide the love and stability every young dog deserves.

He has been tested for Mediterranean diseases and will be fully prepared for travel, vaccinated, microchipped, and with his passport ready. Jester will be ready to travel in April to his forever home.

As with all of our dogs, he comes with full rescue back-up.

name: Hamish
description:
Meet Hamish, a 4 month old male Griffon Cross who is expected to grow into a medium-sized dog of around 18–20 kg when fully grown.

Hamish is one of six lively brothers born on 1 November 2025 to a Griffon cross mum. He is currently nearly four months old and, like his siblings, is expected to grow into a medium-sized dog.

Hamish has had a good start to life at the Residencia Garatuxa shelter in Galicia, northern Spain. Growing up in the shelter environment means he is already used to people, everyday activity, and different sounds around him.

He is a very sociable puppy who enjoys interacting with both humans and other dogs.

As a young puppy, Hamish will benefit from a family willing to continue his training and give him the guidance, exercise, and affection he needs as he grows.

He has been tested for Mediterranean diseases and will be fully prepared for travel, vaccinated, microchipped, and with his passport ready. Hamish will be ready to travel in April to the right home.

As with all of our dogs, he comes with full rescue back-up.

name: Lupin
description:
Meet Lupin, a 4 month old male Griffon Cross who is expected to grow into a medium-sized dog of around 18–20 kg when fully grown.

Lupin is a charming young puppy born on 1 November 2025. He is one of six brothers born to a Griffon cross mum.

Lupin has spent his early months at the Residencia Garatuxa shelter in Galicia, where he has grown up surrounded by people, other dogs, and everyday shelter activity. This has helped him develop into a sociable and confident puppy.

He enjoys playing with his brothers and interacting with people, showing a friendly and open nature. Lupin will thrive in a home where he can continue learning, exploring, and becoming a much-loved family member.

He has been tested for Mediterranean diseases and will be fully prepared for travel, vaccinated, microchipped, and with his passport ready. Lupin will be ready to travel in April.

As with all of our dogs, he comes with full rescue back-up.

name: Bon Bon
description:
Bon Bon is a 1.5 year old spayed small to medium mixed breed currently in foster in Staffordshire. She is iElisa negative.

Bon Bon is a very sweet, shy-natured girl who is enjoying life in foster.

She is housetrained and sleeps through the night without issue.

Bon Bon gets along well with other dogs and could happily live with a canine companion or as the only dog in the home.

She can be a little shy at first and needs a family who will give her time and patience to build her confidence and bond with them.

Bon Bon accepts a collar and lead but will need further training to walk confidently outside the home. She has been walked in a field near her foster home and, although hesitant at first, soon enjoyed sniffing and exploring.

She enjoys time in the garden and then returning inside for snuggles on the sofa. At present she has a fairly low energy level and enjoys short play sessions followed by rest.

Bon Bon is currently more comfortable around women than men, although she shows no aggression and is simply shy.

Bon Bon would suit a quiet home with patient adopters who will allow her time to settle and continue building confidence.

name: Mylo
description:
Mylo is a 6 year old neutered small mixed breed currently in foster in Staffordshire. He weighs approximately 14kg and stands around 47cm tall. He has a distinctive stump tail and a confident little character.

Mylo previously spent a long period living as a stray before entering rescue. He has now settled well into foster care and is enjoying the comfort and routine of home life.

He is affectionate but independent and prefers interaction on his own terms. He enjoys gentle fuss, especially belly rubs, and likes spending time pottering around the house before settling down nearby.

Mylo is friendly with people but appreciates his personal space and will communicate when he has had enough attention. For this reason he would be best suited to an adult-only home.

He can interact well with other dogs he feels comfortable around but does not enjoy overly energetic behaviour, particularly from puppies. He may be happiest as the only dog, although he could potentially share with a calm and respectful companion. He can be protective of food around other dogs so feeding will need to be managed.

Mylo is housetrained and settles well in the home environment. He tolerates gentle handling but is sensitive about his tail being touched.

Mylo would suit a quiet household able to provide routine, companionship and respect for his boundaries. A secure garden would be beneficial for relaxed outdoor time as he enjoys pottering and lounging outside.

name: Roo
description:
Roo is a 1 year old spayed small mixed breed weighing around 10kg, currently in foster care in Staffordshire. She is iElisa negative.

Roo is a happy, energetic little dog with a gentle nature. She loves people and enjoys being around her humans.

She can initially be a little shy around loud noises but settles quickly with reassurance.

She is playful and lively and enjoys interaction with people and other dogs. Roo gets along well with dogs of all shapes and sizes.

Roo is housetrained with regular access to the garden and settles well in the home. She is not crate trained.

She accepts wearing a collar and lead and is beginning to get used to short walks around the garden area.

Continued lead training and confidence-building will help her become more comfortable walking outside the home.

Roo would suit an active household able to provide regular exercise, companionship and continued training as she matures.

name: Dolly
description:
Dolly is a spayed female mixed breed currently in foster care in Staffordshire. She is iElisa negative.

Dolly was rescued together with several members of her family group in Romania. The dogs were found living together in a field and clearly formed a close family unit.

She has recently arrived in the UK and is still settling into her foster home. At the moment she can be a little unsure around people but is gradually building confidence and beginning to come out of her shell.

She is becoming more comfortable around the people in the household and accepts gentle interaction.

Dolly enjoys the company of other dogs and would benefit from living with a friendly resident dog who can help her continue to gain confidence.

Dolly enjoys relaxing on the sofa and spending time near her foster family once she feels safe. She also enjoys her food and settles well into the home routine.

She will sometimes join in barking when other dogs bark.

name: Elsa
description:
Elsa is a 1.4 year old spayed female mixed breed with Husky-type characteristics, currently in Oxfordshire. She is iElisa negative.

Elsa is an affectionate and energetic young dog with a curious and intelligent nature. She enjoys human company and likes to be involved in daily activities.

She has a playful and enthusiastic personality and benefits from regular physical and mental stimulation. Although lively, she settles well after exercise and enjoys resting alongside other dogs in the home.

She is continuing to build confidence and can show assertive behaviour during energetic play.

Elsa is friendly with adults and enjoys attention. Due to her size and excitable nature, she would be best suited to a home with older children.

She enjoys rough-and-tumble play with other dogs and would benefit from living with a confident, energetic dog who matches her play style. She does not show food guarding.

She is not suitable for homes with cats or small animals due to a strong chase instinct.

She may bark at unfamiliar visitors and can appear anxious initially, but settles with calm, positive introductions.

Elsa’s housetraining is still in progress and she will require continued consistency and supervision.

She is not crate trained and becomes distressed if confined in a crate, particularly in the car, although she travels well once settled.

She walks well on a harness and collar but is strong and energetic. She may become overexcited on grassed areas.

Her recall is good in secure enclosed spaces, and she is more confident walking alongside another dog than alone.

name: Rebecca
description:
Rebecca is a beautiful black Greyhound, thought to be around 5 years old (possibly a little older), currently fostered in North Lincolnshire.

She arrived from Ireland in search of her forever home here in the UK, after an incredibly sad past. Rebecca was rescued in a terrible condition and was clearly used for breeding.

Despite everything she has endured, she has the most gentle and loving nature.

Since settling into foster, Rebecca has adapted wonderfully to home life. She adores her cosy bed, enjoys her daily walks, and gets very excited at mealtimes.

After breakfast and a walk, she’s more than happy to spend the rest of the day snoozing peacefully.

Rebecca is a calm, gentle soul who is lovely around children and has been great with the dogs she has met. She walks beautifully on the lead, although she can show a little strength when squirrels grab her attention!

Rebecca has no ear markings, so her exact age cannot be confirmed, but she is ready now to find the loving home she truly deserves.

name: Percy
description:
Percy is a large, affectionate young crossbreed aged just over 1 year old with a loving and playful nature.

Percy is incredibly people-focused and thrives on human companionship. He forms strong bonds and enjoys being close to his family, often following his people around the home and seeking affection.

In the home, Percy is calm, clean, and well behaved. He is crate trained, settles well when left, and shows no destructive behaviour. He enjoys his comforts, along with playtime, toys, and plenty of cuddles.

Percy is still learning about the world and can sometimes feel unsure in new situations or around unfamiliar dogs. However, he is making great progress with positive training and is growing in confidence every day.

He can live with another dog of a similar size following careful introductions, as he has shown he can build positive relationships. However, he would not be suitable to live with cats or small animals.

Percy walks using a halti and continues to improve with guidance. At this stage, off-lead exercise is best suited to secure fields while his training develops further.

Percy would suit a patient and committed home that can continue his training and provide a calm, supportive environment. He is a young dog with huge potential who will thrive with consistency and encouragement.

Percy is a loyal and loving companion who, once bonded, will be a constant and devoted presence in your life.

name: Brisbane
description:
Brisbane is a young, large crossbreed aged just over 1 year old with a gentle and affectionate nature.

Brisbane is a loving and people-focused dog who forms strong bonds with his humans. He enjoys being close and will happily follow you from room to room, always wanting to be near his people.

Brisbane is a double merle and has some sensory impairments, including limited vision in one eye and reduced hearing. Despite this, he navigates his environment well and lives a happy, full life.

In the home, Brisbane is calm, clean, and well behaved. He is non-destructive, settles well, and can be left alone without issue. He adapts well to everyday life and has shown he can cope in busier environments such as shops and cafés when supported correctly.

Brisbane is dog friendly and has shown he can live alongside other dogs. He is also gentle with children, although due to his sensitivity, a home with older or dog-savvy children would be more suitable.

Brisbane can become overwhelmed in new or busy situations. When this happens, he may become overexcited and struggle to regulate himself. This is not aggression, but a response to feeling unsure, and with calm handling and structure, he settles well.

He walks nicely on the lead and responds well to guidance. With consistency and a calm approach, he continues to grow in confidence.

Brisbane would suit a patient and understanding home that can provide structure, routine, and a calm environment. He needs owners who are willing to manage introductions carefully and allow him time to decompress and feel secure.

Brisbane is a gentle, loyal dog who, in the right home, will form a deeply devoted bond and become a constant companion.

Brisbane is crate trained, clean, and quiet in his crate overnight. He is not destructive at home but does need access to chew toys to keep himself entertained.

He especially enjoys filled Kongs, raw bones, and a game of tug. While he can struggle to self-settle at times, he’s learning the concept of “quiet time” and developing an off switch.

He enjoys accompanying his foster carer to work and confidently navigates busy public spaces such as shops and town centres. Brisbane is calm in loud environments and loves interacting with people. He can be left alone without issue, often just sleeping or chewing his toys.

As a Double Merle, Brisbane comes with some genetic considerations. He can both see and hear, although his left eye, which has a starburst pupil, may have some visual limitations.

Due to his lack of pigmentation, he is sensitive to the sun and can burn easily, so he requires sun protection and careful management.

name: Dorris
description:
Dorris is a 3 year old female American Bulldog Cross with a loving and playful nature who has sadly been waiting in rescue for over 2 years.

In the home, Dorris is calm, clean, and well behaved. She is non-destructive and enjoys a quiet, settled environment where she can relax, play with her toys, and spend time with her person.

She is affectionate and enjoys both playtime and cuddles, forming a strong bond with those she trusts.

Dorris is a fun and engaging dog who brings personality and joy into the home. She is happy to entertain herself with toys or chews but equally enjoys interaction and affection from her humans.

Dorris does struggle around other dogs and will need to be the only pet in the home. Walks and environments need to be carefully managed to ensure she feels safe and comfortable.

Due to her needs, Dorris requires an experienced and understanding owner who can provide structure, calm handling, and appropriate management of her environment.

Kennel life can be particularly stressful for Dorris due to the presence of other dogs, and she is often kept in a quieter area to help reduce this stress.

Dorris would suit a calm, structured home where she can feel safe and settled. She needs an owner who will advocate for her, manage her surroundings, and allow her to live a peaceful life without unnecessary pressure.

When given the right environment, Dorris is a loving, loyal, and joyful companion who simply wants to play, cuddle, and belong.

If they have been around children, what ages were the children?

How does the dog walk on the lead?She does focus on other dogs and will lunge at them, so will need to be walked in quieter areas or exercised in a secure field on her own. When she’s on her own, she’s generally well behaved on the lead, no excessive pulling. She’s quite nosy and likes a good sniff around.

How long can the dog be left at home without issue?7 hours plus. She was left for longer periods when I had to stay at work and was absolutely fine when I got home. No destruction or accidents. My neighbour did say she barked a bit when left, so she may be sorted to shorter periods or a house without many neighbours.

Is the dog destructive at home?Not at all, she is extremely well behaved girl in the house. Fully housetrained and doesn’t chew anything she shouldn’t. She was provided with a variety of chew toys though as she constantly likes to chew or play with balls etc.

Whats are they fed?I fed her raw and she loved it

name: Kalli
description:
Kalli is a young, athletic crossbreed aged just over 1 year old with a loving and energetic nature.

Kalli is very people-focused and forms strong bonds with her humans. She thrives on interaction and enjoys being close, often seeking reassurance and connection from those around her.

She is an intelligent and eager-to-please dog who is already showing great potential. Kalli knows basic commands such as sit and wait and is continuing to learn, responding well to training, especially when food rewards are involved.

Kalli is still very much a young dog and can become easily overstimulated, particularly around other dogs. She can struggle to regulate her excitement and may not always communicate appropriately, which can lead to misunderstandings. For this reason, she will need to be the only pet in the home while she continues to build confidence and develop her social skills.

She walks well on the lead in calmer environments but can become strong and determined if something catches her attention. With consistent, one-to-one training, she is continuing to improve.

Kalli can become bored if not mentally stimulated, so she will require enrichment and an active home that can meet both her physical and mental needs. She may also jump up when excited but is already learning that calm behaviour is rewarded.

Kalli would suit a home that is committed to training, structure, and consistency. She will thrive with owners who understand how to guide a young, energetic dog and are willing to invest time into her development.

Kalli is a loving and loyal dog with huge potential, and in the right home, she will grow into a deeply rewarding and devoted companion.

name: Roxy
description:
Roxy is an 18 month old female Caucasian shepherd located in Spain

This beautiful, medium-sized Caucasian Shephard is Roxy, still young at 18 months, she has the traditional dark, tan semi coat and black masked face, who has recently been saved by us from the streets.

Roxy is a very sweet girl, still a youngster, she can be nervous around new dogs to begin with until she knows they are friendly, but generally once introduced correctly she’s very playful and good with the dogs, but she can be a bit of slow burner.

Roxy walks very well on her lead and we think that she is suitable for a family with older children with or without another friendly dog as she can be a bit excitable.

Roxy is a no to cats we think, it’s not that she’s aggressive, but she chases them.Roxy is ready to travel now for the right family.

Great with people and dogs. gentle nature, and is obedient, happy to play and a pretty girl.

name: Roo
description:
Elegant Roo is a 5 year old female Greyhound. She is a friendly and gentle girl with a sensitive side. She enjoys being with her people, receiving affection, and playing with her toys.

She is social with other dogs but can be worried of some, so she will need her owner to help build her confidence and provide her with reassurance and guidance when needed.

She would love a home where she could snuggle up on the sofa after a day of sniffy adventures and enjoy the wonders of being a much-loved family dog. This gorgeous girl will make an extremely rewarding companion for anyone lucky enough to adopt her.

Roo can live in a flat as long as there is direct access to a private garden. She can live with sensible junior or secondary age children that will give her space when needed.

She could also potentially live with a calm, large-breed adult dog, subject to a successful meet at Mayhew. Roo has a very subtle lameness in her right foreleg, especially after intensive exercise.

It is possible that she has an underlying injury from her previous work as a racing greyhound. She is on long-term anti-inflammatories for this and doing very well.

Roo has been microchipped, neutered, and vaccinated and is up to date with flea and worming treatment. She has also been health checked and behaviourally assessed. Lastly, every dog adopted from us will go home with 4 weeks free pet insurance.

name: Cleo
description:
Cleo is a stunning 2 year old Cane Corso with a loyal and affectionate nature.

Cleo is a gentle and sensitive girl who forms strong bonds with her people. She is very people-focused and loves to be close, often sitting beside you or resting her head on you for comfort and reassurance.

In the home, Cleo is calm, clean, and well behaved. She is crate trained, settles beautifully, and shows no destructive behaviour. She enjoys her comforts, including relaxing with her family and playing with her favourite toys, especially her squeaky ball.

Cleo walks nicely on the lead and regularly checks in with her handler, showing a willingness to learn and stay connected. She mixes well with other dogs, particularly when introductions are handled correctly, and has shown she can live with a dog-savvy cat.

Cleo is a sensitive soul who can be wary of unfamiliar men or sudden movements. However, with calm and patient introductions, she builds trust well and relaxes into her environment.

She is currently receiving behavioural support and continues to make positive progress.

Due to her breed and temperament, Cleo requires a knowledgeable home with experience of guardian breeds. She thrives in a calm, structured environment with clear guidance and consistency.

Cleo would suit an adult-only home or one with older, dog-savvy teenagers who understand her needs and can give her the time and space to settle.

Cleo is a devoted and loyal companion who, in the right home, will become an incredibly rewarding and loving addition to the family.

name: Joey
description:
Joey is an adorable three-legged, 8-year-old French Bulldog who came into rescue due to his owner’s housing situation. He’s in an Oldies Club foster home in north-west Leicestershire, near the Derbyshire border.

He was briefly rehomed, but didn’t get along with the resident female dog, so is back at his foster home, waiting for a lovely retirement home.

Summary: Joey is a happy-go-lucky charmer who takes almost everything in his 3 legged stride. He doesn’t like cats and needs to be an only dog at home. Resident teenagers should be fine for him but not very young children.

He wants a retirement home where he usually has human company, has an hour of walkies a day, someone to watch what he eats (because he’ll try to wallop down anything!) and lots of toys, lap time and fusses.

Settled quickly in foster: Joey, also known as “Big Joe”, settled at his foster home within one day! He’s a confident dog and once he knew where the garden was, who would be feeding him and that he was allowed on the sofa, he was right at home.

Can be left sometimes: Joey does love being with someone, preferably on their lap, so he does need a home where there is usually someone around. When you do need to go out without him, he should just settle down and snooze until you’re home.

His foster carer has left him for 3 hours and watched him on a camera having a lovely sleep. He wouldn’t want this to be a daily occurrence though because he does need plenty of people time.

Needs to be the only dog at home: Joey gets on OK with other dogs when out and about and, as you can see, he’s fine with the two resident Sighthounds in his foster home.

However, this blissful state or affairs is the exception not the rule and Joey has a history of not getting on with other dogs in his home (both male and female, even after nice introductions).

As he’s already had both a foster home and an adoption fall through because he took against the resident dogs, it’s now thought he should be the only dog in his retirement home.

That way, he can be assured that all toys, food and attention are rightfully his.

Needs a cat-free home: Joey doesn’t seem to like the cats next door and his foster carer thinks he would chase them if given the opportunity.

Could live with teenagers: We were told that Joey used to live with a teenager and was happy. There are no children at his foster home but we think he should be OK to live with sensible teenagers.

Great on walks: Joey’s missing leg does not hold him back on walks at all. He walks pretty well on the lead and has good recall when off lead in enclosed spaces. He does have a tendency to eat things he shouldn’t, so he needs to be watched.

He ate some vegetables which were growing in the garden when his foster carer wasn’t looking, and would eat cat poo if he had a chance. There are cats living next door so daily vigilance in the garden is needed!

Joey munched a whole cucumber in seconds so he doesn’t need long to steal something he shouldn’t and guzzle it. For walks, he goes once or twice a day and needs about an hour of exercise each day.

Great in the car: Joey is very good in the car and he has taken the bus a few times too. He especially likes going to the pub as he’s sure to get lots of attention.

Joey’s favourite pastimes: Eating, walking, sleeping and hugs.

Joey’s ideal home: He would love a home where he can have loads of fuss and sofa snuggles. He is quite a lapdog and would rather sit on you than near you.

He doesn’t bother himself with personal space and he wants to be around people as much as possible. Daily walks and tasty food are his favourite things. He’s pretty easy to please. He needs to be your only dog.

Health notes: Joey is neutered, vaccinated, microchipped, wormed and flea treated. Joey lost his leg when he was younger and this really doesn’t impact him very much at all. He has a poultry allergy, so eats a mainly fish-based diet.

As long as he isn’t stealing anybody’s food this is easy enough to manage by just avoiding any poultry.

name: Leo
description:
EVERYONE loves Leo! If you’re looking for a real character – a dog who will give you lots of laughs, lots of fun and cuddles…this little one-eyed lion is your boy.

Leo, born in 2023 is a lively, cheeky terrier mix and as with all terriers, needs firm and consistent boundaries. People with terrier experience in particular, will love this boy’s intelligent, lively and hugely fun personality.

Leo can live with other dogs (he lives with 3 others of all ages and sizes in his foster). He hasn’t got a nervous bone in his body so can sometimes be full on, liking rough and tumble vocal play.

He might be a little domineering for a very quiet, older or nervous dog, but a great buddy for an enthusiastic kindred spirit (any size… Leo thinks he’s a Lion!).

Leo likes his dog pals but he’s more of a people’s-dog than a dog’s dog. He adores people, he adores men; he’s been lovely with his fosterer’s 7-year-old grandson. His loves are food, cuddles and walks…. dog friends come after.

So, Leo would also be perfectly happy as an only dog if he kept up regular socialising with other dog friends.

Leo is clean in the house, crate trained, can be left alone for short periods, travels beautifully (he loves a long car journey) and has behaved very nicely in a care home (where everyone fell in love with him of course).

Leo has learnt to live in a home and now knows the difference between his own toys and other objects where chewing is concerned.

Originally, Leo came from Bosnia. He came to our rescuer’s attention when he was hit by a car. Unfortunately, his eye was found to be badly damaged and had to be removed.

Leo really doesn’t mind that he only has one eye and his cheeky jaunty look suits this loveable boy perfectly!

Please note – we do not rehome dogs to families with children under the age of 10.

Leo is super adaptable and can live just about anywhere, as long as it has a garden. He loves chasing about. A busy household would be fine. A large household would be fine.

Leo will need a good amount of exercise, play and stimulation.

Leo chases cats so a household without cats would be best unless they are extremely dog savvy.

Please read about our Adoption process. We really appreciate it when potential adopters have read our advice, and these are the people who are most often successful at application stage!

Our adoption donation is £325. This includes travel to the UK, their vaccinations, pet passport, microchip and all preparation for travel. They also come with 5 weeks free insurance (excluding The Channel Isles & Isle of Man).

name: Jess
description:
Jerss is a 1 year old male medium size Labrador Retriever Cross, a little shy but very good.

Jess is a very playful, and sweet puppy, rescued with his siblings, he was in a kennel for few months and now he’s in a foster home.

He loves human people, he is a little shy at the beginning but after a while he comes close to you asking for cuddles.

He has the character of the lab, very balanced and respectful of your spaces.

His foster mum is very happy with his progress; he is really gaining confidence day by day.

Jess is learning how to walk with the leash, following the other dogs of the family. He is a really good boy.

Would you like to adopt Jess and love him forever?

Jess will be the best part of your life, he will fill your life with joy and happiness.

name: Alfie
description:
Alfie is a 2 year old neutered small mixed breed currently in foster care in Lincolnshire.

Alfie is a sensitive dog who builds trust slowly. He is cautious around new people and needs time and space to approach interactions at his own pace. Once he feels safe, he forms strong bonds and shows an affectionate and playful side.

He enjoys spending time with his foster carers and will seek out attention when comfortable. He is curious, enjoys exploring the garden and benefits from a calm and predictable routine.

Alfie can become overwhelmed if approached too quickly or if expectations are placed on him too soon. He requires patient handling and a consistent environment to help him continue building confidence.

He is housetrained and crate trained and settles well overnight. He walks well on lead and enjoys regular walks.

He is currently working on accepting the removal of his harness and will require continued support with this, as he can still be sensitive during handling around his head.

Alfie enjoys food and is motivated by it, although he prefers to eat undisturbed. He is still learning to tolerate grooming and will benefit from gentle, ongoing desensitisation.
