name: Marcus
description:
Marcus is an 8 month old neutered male small to medium mixed breed currently in foster care in Lincolnshire. He is iElisa negative and measures approximately 35cm.

Marcus was previously living in a shelter environment in Romania where he shared space with several other dogs.

He is settling well into foster life and is described as friendly and non-dominant with other dogs. He mixes well with his foster siblings and shows appropriate social behaviour.

Marcus enjoys human interaction and will come for affection, but is not overly demanding. He has a calm and balanced nature and is not highly energetic.

Marcus is expected to remain small to medium in size.

He would suit a home able to continue his development and provide routine, companionship and ongoing training as he matures.

name: Courtney
description:
Courtney is a 6 year old female Mastin cross breed located in Spain.

Pretty Courtney is a big, beautiful girl, with a smooth, soft, tan coat, and soulful eyes. Our Courtney is a Mastine Cross, she stands at medium to large size, and she came to the rescue in 2023, so now its well overdue for her to find a loving home.

She has always been part of the ´front´ pack & gets along with other dogs. She only ever once clashed with another dominant female, but otherwise she enjoys being in a pack. She walks well on her lead & enjoys attention and cuddles.

Courtney is a calm, gentle girl with confidence to fit into many situations so she would thrive in a home with or without another friendly dog and older children over 12. She is not cat tested.

The rescue where Courtney is living is closing and so she is one of 35 dogs looking for a home quickly. Can you help Courtney with a loving forever home?

Great with people and dogs. gentle nature, and is obedient, and a pretty girl.

name: Hovis
description:
Hovis is a 4 year old male medium cross breed currently in the East Midlands.

He was born at the shelter on 20 March 2021 after his mother, Rosie, was rescued heavily pregnant from a public shelter. Sadly, Rosie later passed away.

Hovis has grown up in a rescue environment and is described as friendly. He has been child tested and is comfortable around children.

He lives with other dogs and is good with them. He walks on a lead and manages routine handling well.

Hovis weighs approximately 25 kg and stands around 52 cm tall. He is neutered and travel ready.

Hovis is looking for a committed home willing to support him as he transitions from shelter life into a family environment.

name: Lasi
description:
Our extra special girl Lasi is approximately two years old and a very splendid cross breed at the bottom end of medium. Lasi weighs just fourteen kilos and measures twelve inches from shoulder to paw.

Having been found abandoned on the streets, Lasi has been in our Cyprus shelter for four months.

Lasi has been described by our shelter manager as calm, sweet, eager to please and will make a fabulous family dog.

Her appearance is breathtaking with a light tan coat and a graduated darker tan along her back. Gorgeous hazel eyes and beautiful ears are showstoppers.

Lasi will fit into her forever home so well and will bring years of joy and happiness to her very fortunate adopters.

Lasi walks nicely on her lead and enjoys her time in the car. She seems to mix perfectly well with children, cats and other dogs.

name: Carmel
description:
Our special pretty girl Carmel is approximately three years old and a sublime cross breed at the bottom end of medium. Carmel weighs a perfect thirteen kilos and measures eleven inches from shoulder to paw.

Having been found abandoned on the streets, Carmel has been in our Cyprus shelter for three months.

Our shelter manager describes Carmel as quite adorable with a submissive personality. She has a natural kindness and empathy about her and will prove to be very low maintenance.

Carmel thoroughly enjoys human companionship and savours a cuddle and a lap. Her manners are impeccable, and she is far too good for shelter life.

Carmel is longing for her forever home with a loving family and gentle routine. With so much love to give, Carmel will be treasured for her entire life.

Carmel walks really nicely on her lead and enjoys her time in the car. She seems to mix perfectly well with other dogs, cats and children.

name: Bert
description:
Bert is a 4 year old large male Labrador Retriever Cross.

Bert is Black and White in colour and his coat is short in length.

Bert is a Labrador Cross and has been at the shelter a few years through no fault of his own. He was found on the street and was most likely abandoned at around 1 year old. Despite his bad start in life he is a lovely, sweet boy.

Bert is quite a busy boy who likes to keep active. He loves his walks although can be a bit strong and needs to learn some manners.

However, with regular daily exercise we are sure this will improve. Bert has probably never had a home of his own but we think he will adapt quite quickly.

Bert gets on well with other dogs, both male and female, and he would be better living with another dog for company. He also needs someone home most of the day.

Poor Bert is getting fed up of being in the shelter and really deserves his own forever home.

name: Marley
description:
Marley is a 5 year old large male Labrador.

Marley is Golden and White in colour and his coat is medium in length.

Marley’s nature is sweet, friendly and clumsy.

None of us can understand why Marley is still in the shelter waiting. He is the most friendly, loveable dog.

He has the typical Labrador mentality although he is probably not pure. He loves his walks, he loves attention and loves belly rubs.

Marley gets on with most dogs and we believe would be great with children. He could be a family dog, couples dog or a one person dog.

He can live with other dogs but possibly better suited to females and to dogs that are not dominant. He could also be an only dog.

Marley has been with us about 4 years sadly, through no fault of his own, so may take time to adapt to the outside world.

Who will give this gorgeous boy a chance at happiness?

name: Luna
description:
Luna is a 3-year-old female Cross-Breed. She is described as a medium-sized dog and weighs approximately 14.5kg. She is currently in Croatia while she waits for a permanent home to call her own.

She is a happy and energetic dog who clearly enjoys being around both people and other dogs. Luna loves to run, jump, and play, showing that she has an active and lively personality.

She is expected to become a loyal and loving companion in the right home.

Luna has already learned to walk nicely on a lead, which is a great foundation for her continued training. She is friendly with other dogs and has the potential to live in a home with them.

She can also live with children over 8 years old, making her suitable for families with older children.

She has not yet been tested with cats, but this can be arranged if needed. Luna is not fully house trained at the moment, though it is noted that she is likely to learn quickly with guidance and routine.

With patience and consistency, she should continue to make good progress in a home environment.

Luna has received extensive veterinary care to prepare her for adoption. She is microchipped, vaccinated against rabies, and has been vaccinated twice against infectious diseases.

She will also receive the Bordetella vaccine before transport, has been castrated, and has tested negative for Mediterranean diseases and Brucellosis. In addition, she will be given a kennel cough nasal vaccine before travel.

name: Molly
description:
Molly is a 1 year old large female Cross Breed.

Molly is Black in colour and her coat is long in length.

Molly’s nature is fun loving and she loves to cuddle.

The gorgeous scruffy Molly was found abandoned by a couple who took her in but then decided they couldn’t look after her so she came to the shelter.

Molly was a little nervous at first but soon got to know everyone. Molly loves charging around the compound playing with the other dogs. She adores playing with the hose so will most likely love water and swimming.

She’s a lovely, friendly, happy girl who would probably be a very good family dog or can live with just adults.

She gets on fine with the dogs she shares a kennel with and would be happier living with another dog. Needs someone home most of the day.

name: Camel
description:
Camel is an 8-year-old male Cross-Breed. He has recently returned to care due to his previous owner’s health and is currently in Leicester.

Camel is described as a gentle giant who brings joy to everyone he meets and loves nothing more than cuddles on the sofa.

He has a calm, affectionate nature and enjoys sunbathing, paddling in the pool, and eating, showing that he takes pleasure in simple comforts.

Camel has struggled with kennel life, often appearing lost and lonely, but he responds well to time, care, and enrichment.

He would be happy with garden exercise in a home that can provide love, attention, and opportunities for mental stimulation.

Camel can live with children aged 10 and above, but he is not suitable to live with cats or other dogs.

He would benefit from walks where he could meet friendly dogs in a controlled environment.

name: Reuben
description:
Reuben is a 2 year old male Hound Cross-Breed. Reuben, a gentle boy, needs a loving home.

There are few rescue stories for dogs in Cyprus that start well. It is a story of sadness and neglect. Hunting on the island means many beautiful dogs are treated like trash — neglected and starved under the misconception it will make them better hunting dogs.

Often abused physically and terrorised mentally, Reuben is sadly a classic example of this.

Found in Lefkara village, terrified and emaciated, his hip bones visibly showing. He was extremely skittish and on edge when rescued.

Once at the shelter, Reuben was allowed to decompress in a safe place, with small meals gradually building him up under veterinary instruction. What he has been through, we don’t want to imagine.

Reuben is likely a hunting dog that wasn’t performing. We’ve since discovered what a gentle, sweet, and kind boy he is — hunting is not in his nature.

He was discarded in the mountains in the hope he would perish. Somehow, this tired, skinny boy made his way down into the village, showing incredible resilience despite how terrible he must have felt.

Reuben is settling well into shelter life. He has a shy nature but is ever so kind and gentle. He is inquisitive and shy with children but friendly, and always sweet and loving with the other shelter dogs. Not cat tested.

Reuben is naturally wary of new people on first meeting, but he manages to be brave — coming forward for sniffs and fuss. He trusts and adores his rescuer, Lin Ova. With time and patience, Reuben can learn to trust.

He wants affection and loves kisses and cuddles, regardless of the terrible things he’s been through. Dogs are incredible for continuing to trust humans even after humans do horrible things to them

Reuben would be best sharing his home with another dog or two to help him settle and build trust. He could live in a home with older children aged 12+.

Reuben has a lot of learning to do but is very keen to please, very bright, and eager to learn.

Rescue backed by Saving Souls Animal Rescue, a UK-registered charity.

Please message if you think you can show Reuben what it’s like to be truly loved.

name: Breeze
description:
Breeze is a 5 year old German shorthaired pointer. She is large in size at approx. 23kg and is currently in Croatia.

Breeze is good with other dogs, likes to play and run and is very loving.

She currently lives in kennels so may need some house training. She walks well on a leash.

Breeze can live with other dogs and children over 8 years old. She cannot live with cats.

Breeze is microchipped, rabies vaccinated, infectious diseases two times vaccinated, bordatella vaccine will be recieved before transport, castrated, Mediterranean diseases tested-negative.

Brucellosis tested negative and Kennel cough nasel given before travel.

Adoption fee and home check applies, and full rescue backup is provided by Ninas Haven.

name: Minty
description:
Minty is a 6-year-old male Cross-Breed. He is described as a beautiful boy with a charming personality that has clearly helped him through some tough times. His affectionate and fun nature shines through in everything he does.

He previously spent six months in Lancram and narrowly escaped with his life, which makes his gentle and loving temperament even more special.

Despite his past, he has remained friendly and people-focused. He truly enjoys being around his humans and building a close bond.

Minty loves his walks and being outdoors, making him a great match for someone who enjoys an active lifestyle. Time spent exploring the outside world is one of his favourite things. He is happiest when he can share these moments with his special person.

At home, Minty would prefer a situation where his keeper is around for much of the time. He forms strong attachments and thrives on companionship and routine. A household where he is not left alone for long periods would suit him best.

Although he can get along with other dogs while out on walks, Minty would like to be the only dog in the home. He enjoys social moments outside but prefers a calm and focused environment indoors.

Having his humans all to himself would help him feel settled and secure.

He would be an especially good match for a retired but active person who enjoys regular walks. Someone with time, patience, and affection to give would help him truly flourish. In return, Minty offers loyalty, warmth, and plenty of loving companionship.

Minty is neutered, immunised, microchipped, and has been treated for fleas and worms. He has also been blood tested for Brucella canis and comes with a Romanian passport. A home check and adoption fee will apply as part of the adoption process.

name: Bilbo
description:
Calling all dog lovers – meet the very handsome Bilbo. Bilbo is a 5 year old male Spaniel Cross-Breed currently in Surrey, U.K., and he is looking for an adoptive or foster home.

Can live with a small dog after correct introductions.

Cat-free home, as he is not used to cats.

Bilbo is a 5 year old rescue boy who is searching for his forever (or foster) home. Currently located in Surrey, Bilbo likes his own space and will settle quite happily in his bed. He sleeps through the night and is calm and quiet.

Bilbo thrives in peaceful home environments and loves relaxing the most.

Bilbo is toilet trained, lead trained, and can be left for short periods in the house. He is non-destructive.

On walks, Bilbo shows lead frustration towards other dogs. He may pull and react out of frustration and fear. He shows no reaction towards people or strangers.

Bilbo is definitely food-motivated and will do anything for a tasty treat; this will help with his training going forward.

With correct introductions, Bilbo could live with another small dog, but he is still learning social cues and boundaries, so a patient canine companion would be ideal.

Bilbo could live with older, dog-savvy children of teenage age, as long as he has his own child-free space to go to. Bilbo likes his own space and does not like too much fuss when he is resting. He especially does not like being touched on the top of his head.

Rescue support in the U.K. Meadow of Hope Dog Rescue. Application and checks apply.

Vaccinated and blood tested.Flea and worm treated.Neutered and microchipped.

name: Dexter
description:
Dexter is a 6 year old male German shepherd cross located in Spain.

This loveable chap is Dexter, a medium to large size, 6 year old, GSD mix who has a tan, short coat and black masked face.

Dexter is much smaller than a traditional GSD, as you can see by the videos and also the videos show how friendly he is and how popular in a group of dogs that live together.

Dexter is our priority, he’s not pretty or cute but he’s handsome and has a big, loving heart so we are desperate to help him find a new home.

Unfortunately, he is one of three dogs we are helping urgently, because he has had his ears cruelly cut, so it’s crucial we bring him to the UK as soon as possible before the laws change to ban dogs with cropped ears.

Dexter is great with male and female dogs and loves all people. He is quite independent and not the type of dog to want cuddles all of the time.

He has a fantastic character. He would not be good with cats due to how fixated he is with them. Children we think over 12 years.

Dexter has been tested as having low level Leish and is responding very well to his inexpensive treatment. A packet of tablets for one month is just £3 and of course Leish is not transferable to dogs or people.

Dexter is neutered, chipped, vaccinated, and has his passport, so he is ready to travel as soon as he is offered a foster place or an adoption. Dexter is a happy and playful chap and can also be calm and gentle. Good on lead.

name: Calvin
description:
Calvin is an 8 year male old German shepherd cross located in Spain.

Calvin is a medium to large size, 8 year old GSD mix who has tan semi long coats and black masked faces.

Long overlooked Calvin is a the star of the shelter, and everybody loves him, so you have to ask why the hell has he been there 7 of those 8 years? It’s just tragic and now it’s his turn to find a warm sofa and treats and loving cuddles.

He is great with people and dogs. He is neutered, chipped, vaccinated, healthy and has such a wonderful, gentle nature and is obedient, loving and all-round good dog.

He is used to hiking with the volunteers, spending time in crowds of people and lots of dogs, and isn’t nervous or shy. He is also used to children and is very gentle and calm around them.

He is great with male and female dogs and has no problem with cats, as he ignored them at the shelter.

Calvin, born around January 2017, arrived with his brother Murray in 2018. He is very good-natured, obedient, calm, and sociable. He enjoys human contact.

He is healthy and weighs about 36 kg. He has long hair. Calvin’s ears are naturally small – he could be part Chow, we don’t know!

Calvin weighs 35kg, with neck 53cm, a chest of 84cm and height to withers .56cm. We think children we think over 10 years only because of their size. Will split for the right home.

Happy Calm but playful can also be gentle. Good on lead – wonderful temperament.

name: Murray
description:
Murray is an 8 year old German shepherd cross located in Spain.

Murray is medium to large size, 8 year old GSD mix who has tan semi long coats and black masked faces. Long overlooked, he is a star of the shelter, and everybody loves him, so you have to ask why the hell he been there 7 of those 8 years?

It’s just tragic and now it’s his turn to find a warm sofa and treats and loving cuddles.

He is in the shelter with h8s brighter Calvin. Both are great with people and dogs. They are neutered, chipped, vaccinated, healthy and they have such wonderful, gentle natures, and are obedient, loving and all-round good dogs.

They are used to hiking with the volunteers, spending times in crowds of people and lots of dogs, and aren’t nervous or shy.

They are also used to children and are very gentle and calm around them. They are great with male and female dogs and are no problem with cats, as they ignored them at the shelter.

The videos and photos show them walking nicely on leads and out for the day, walking in the hills with the volunteers.

Murray, a male born around January 2017, arrived with his brother Calvin in 2018. He is very good-natured, obedient, calm, and sociable. He enjoys human contact. He is healthy and weighs about 36 kg. He has long hair.

Murray: Weight 37 kilos, Neck 50cm, Chest 85cm, Height to the withers: 68cm.

We think children we think over 10 years only because of their size. Will split for the right home.

name: Willow
description:
Willow is a 9 month old female Cross-Breed.

Willow and her 3 siblings arrived with their mum when they were 6 months old, having been confiscated from their owners. Now they are all 9 months old and ready for their forever homes.

Willow is a lovely, friendly girl and is patiently waiting for her forever home, still unaware of what it truly means to be a puppy.

She should be living in a loving home, cared for, cherished, and warm at night, not shivering through the cold Cyprus evenings.

Confiscated from her home she now curls up with her three siblings on a hard concrete floor, huddled together for warmth.

She’ll need some training and time to get used to walking on a lead, but she’s already great with other dogs and children. She’s far too young to spend her days in a shelter, missing out on such an important stage of learning and exploring.

Her ideal home would be with either a single person, couple, or a family with a secure garden. She can be cat tested for a serious enquiry.

She has been tested for infectious disease and will travel with a passport, be vaccinated, including rabies, and will have received regular flea and worm treatment.

Full rescue back-up is provided by Saving Souls Animal Rescue, a UK-based registered charity.

name: George
description:
George is a 2-year-1-month-old male Pointer cross Vizsla. He is an exuberant, intelligent, and boisterous young dog who is still settling in and being assessed. George is full of energy and thrives on both physical activity and mental challenges.

He is housetrained, travels well, and would love a secure garden where he can burn off energy and play. His active and clever nature means he will need adopters who can keep him engaged and stimulated daily.

Without enough to do, he may become restless.

George is confident, cuddly, and bouncy with adults. He enjoys affection but can be excitable, especially in new situations. He would do best with people who appreciate lively, working-breed types.

An adult-only home would be ideal, though he could live with sensible teenagers aged 14 and over who are used to large, energetic dogs.

George must be the only dog in the home. He is not suited to living with cats, small animals, or livestock due to his chasing instincts.

Adopters will need to understand the needs of his active breed mix and be ready to commit to ongoing training and structure. A home with previous experience of working breeds would be beneficial.

George would prefer a semi-rural or rural setting rather than a busy urban area.

name: Koko
description:
Koko is an approximately 10 months old setter/ pointer mix male located in Cheshire UK.

Super happy and handsome Koko is a medium height, rough coated, liver roan Setter x Pointer mix boy, an unusual mix! but a very nice combination and handsome looking boy with a very happy disposition.

He lives in foster in a multi dog situation and loves to play with them.

He’s an adorably sweet dog, very friendly, good on his lead, mixed in with our residents dogs well and just seems to love people. Koko has a cheerful happy demeanour.

Very attentive to people and likes fun with other dogs. Walks well on lead.

name: Livia
description:
We are looking for a calm, kind foster home for our beautiful girl, Livia, a 3 year old female Cross-Breed. Currently based in Wiltshire, U.K.

Livia had a tough start to life. She was sadly dumped outside our shelter in Bosnia. Thankfully, she was rescued and shown the love she deserves.

In January, Livia travelled to what we hoped would be her forever home in the UK. Unfortunately, one of her adopters has become seriously unwell and is currently in intensive care, leaving the remaining adopter struggling to manage her care.

This has been very hard on everyone, especially Livia.

We are now searching for a peaceful, understanding foster home where Livia can reset, decompress, and feel secure again.

If you can offer Livia the time, patience, and love she needs to heal and blossom, please reach out. She truly deserves a second chance at happiness.

name: Zara
description:
Zara is a 3 year old female Cross-Breed who measures 40 cm and is on the smaller side of medium.

Zara was found abandoned in Romania as a tiny puppy and was taken to a private shelter where she has remained for the last three years.

She spends her life in a very cold kennel with two other dogs. The volunteers all work, so the dogs only get a visit twice a day where they are let out for a run, then back into their kennels again.

Zara is very lonely and would love a home. She is always so happy to see the volunteers. In the picture, you can see Zara’s pen after the snow had melted.

It lacks a full roof as the rescue cannot afford good kennels for all the dogs. They have around 160 dogs and only 40 of them have proper kennels.

Zara is spayed and vaccinated, and she will be tested for Brucellosis. The test is now sent to the UK prior to travel and, if negative, a dog must travel within 30 days of the test.

She will also receive further blood tests in Romania, will be microchipped, and will have a passport.

If you can offer this absolutely lovely girl a forever home, please get in touch. She will make the most wonderful companion and light up your life. A home check is required and her adoption fee is £550. She will be transported to your home.

name: Reggie
description:
Reggie is a 10 month old male small Cross-Breed.

Reggie (was Chance) is looking for a new home. Sadly this boy, not quite a year old, finds himself looking for a new home.

This gorgeous boy came to our care in August 2025 in Romania, and the vet didn’t think he’d survive 48 hours. But he proved us all wrong, and we named him Chance, as he was fighting for a second chance!

He was so excited to be adopted in the UK December!

He was renamed Reggie, and has been loving his walks, cuddles and is such a friendly boy. But sadly Reggie and the resident dog did not gel. So he is now on the hunt for another home.

Reggie is 10kg, and medium sized. He is good with people but can be boisterous. A typical teenager, he can be vocal and can try to test boundaries!

Reggie is such a clever boy, and even though he’s only been in the country for a couple of months, he has already nearly completed his Bronze Kennel Club training!

Reggie would be happy as an only dog or living with other medium or large size dogs.

Reggie is in Thatcham, near Reading, Berkshire.

name: Noodle
description:
Noodle is a 1 year old male Cross-Breed. He is described as a lovely and energetic dog with a very friendly nature. Every person he has met so far has been greeted warmly and positively.

He gets along well with all other dogs he has encountered. His sociable personality makes him a pleasant companion in shared spaces. He clearly enjoys interaction and company rather than being solitary.

Noodle is comfortable wearing both his collar and harness. However, he has not yet learnt proper lead manners and can pull during walks. Continued training and guidance will be important for improving his walking behaviour.

Despite being excitable, he also enjoys affection and closeness. He happily settles down for cuddles and even thinks of himself as a lapdog. Quiet bonding time is just as important to him as active time.

His ideal home would include a good garden and plenty of opportunities for walks. Having other dogs around to play with would suit him well. After activity, he would love nothing more than relaxing on the sofa for a snuggle.

Noodle is currently in foster care in Southampton. He is looking for a home that matches both his energy and affectionate side. With structure and companionship, he should settle nicely into family life.

name: Hueso
description:
Hueso is an 8 year old male Sabueso Hound currently in foster care in Kent, UK.

Hueso is a quiet, nervous boy who needs a special person to give him time and patience to settle. He loves female humans and is more comfortable with them but he will get used to men over time.

He is not aggressive but he will avoid and try to make himself invisible.

Hueso would benefit from a kind dog to live with to help him, especially when humans need to go out, as Hueso does have separation anxiety. Ideally he needs someone who is home a lot or works from home.

He loves his walks. He is not scared of traffic or people on walks but he might sometimes bark at people. So someone who loves to go walking a couple of times a day would be great for this boy.

Hueso has luxating patella so he needs to be on supplements like YuMove and he does need some good walks at a good distance to keep him mobile plus to keep his weight at a good level.

Hueso is a scenthound and can pull on the lead after scents at times.

name: Zar
description:
Zar is a 6-year-old male Sabueso Hound. He was born on 03/06/2019 and is currently waiting in the north of Spain for a permanent home.

He had to be urgently rescued because he was not suitable for hunting. Being in the hands of a hunter placed him in danger, so rescue intervention was necessary for his safety.

Zar is described as a very obedient dog. Despite this, he is extremely shy and clearly frightened by people due to whatever experiences he has previously endured.

He is sociable with other dogs and feels more comfortable around them. However, he still needs to learn that humans can be trusted and will not harm him.

Because he is a scenthound trained for hunting, his recall may be unreliable. His instincts are strong and secure handling will be important in everyday life.

Zar needs patience, love, and time to properly adjust to a family environment. What he truly requires is a home that will finally give him the dignity and kindness he has never known.

Full rescue back up will be provided to ensure both Zar and his adopters receive support. With understanding and consistency, he has the potential to become a devoted companion.

name: Buddy
description:
Buddy is a 1-year-old male Jura Hound. He was born on 06/01/2025 and is currently in a shelter in the north of Spain waiting for a forever home.

He was surrendered because he was not suitable for hunting. Despite his rough start, he is still very young and capable of learning quickly.

Buddy is nervous around people but has already shown noticeable improvement since arriving at the shelter. With time and reassurance, he continues to build confidence.

He gets along well with other dogs. However, he is fed separately because he becomes anxious around food and is very enthusiastic at mealtimes.

Buddy is an active and playful dog who enjoys running around and exploring the garden. He loves using his nose and investigating scents in his surroundings.

He will need an active household willing to provide both exercise and guidance. A patient family prepared to teach him and spend quality time doing activities will suit him best.

As a scenthound with hunting training, his recall may be unreliable. Secure outdoor spaces and careful handling will therefore be important.

He would benefit from structure and routine to help him feel safe and settled. Given consistency and kindness, he should continue gaining confidence and become a loyal companion.

Full rescue back up is provided to support both Buddy and his adopters throughout the process.

name: Seona and Luigi
description:
Seona is a small mixed-breed around 4 years old and Luigi is a small mixed-breed around 7 years old.

Seona and Luigi are fostered together in Staffordshire. Seona is spayed and Luigi is neutered. A reduced adoption donation applies if they are adopted together.

Their journey began with heartbreak when their elderly owner sadly passed away and they were left without care. Thankfully, a rescuer stepped in and they are now safe in foster — but they are looking for a loving forever home together.

These two are completely bonded and it would break their hearts to be separated. They truly are joined at the hip.

Both are gentle, affectionate, and well-mannered. They are housetrained, sleep soundly through the night, and greet each morning with wagging tails. They both love their food and treats.

They are comfortable walking on lead and would benefit from continued confidence-building in new walking environments. A secure garden is essential for their new home.

They are good with other dogs and play nicely with their chosen companions. They are also good with cats.

Seona is the more confident of the pair and often keeps a watchful eye over Luigi. Luigi is more submissive and sweet-natured, happily following Seona’s lead.

They adore sofa snuggles, watching television, and sitting on the windowsill observing the world.

Their foster believes they would thrive best in a quiet home with a secure garden, ideally as the only dogs where they can enjoy peace and attention together.

If you are ready for double the affection and companionship, Seona and Luigi are waiting to meet you.

name: Rolly
description:
Rolly, known as Neeko, is a 6–7 year old neutered male medium mixed breed currently in Lincolnshire.

Neeko is a gentle and affectionate boy who thrives on human company. He enjoys being close to his people and likes to be involved in daily life. Once he feels settled and secure, his loyal and loving nature becomes very apparent.

He is great with children and enjoys their company. Neeko is good with other dogs; however, he can feel overwhelmed in large groups. He would be happiest either as the only dog in the home or living with one or two calm, friendly companions.

Neeko is not suitable to live with cats, as he will chase and reacts strongly to them when out on walks.

He walks nicely on a lead when focused. If he becomes excited by other dogs or people, he responds well to guidance and can be asked to stop, sit and refocus before continuing calmly.

Neeko does not cope well with being crated and becomes stressed, so he will need a crate-free home. He settles well once he feels safe and part of a consistent routine.

Neeko would suit a loving and stable home looking for an affectionate companion. He enjoys an active lifestyle and would thrive with adopters who can offer reassurance, structure and plenty of companionship.

name: Bolt
description:
Bolt is a 7 year old neutered male large mixed breed currently in foster care in Lincolnshire. He stands approximately 57 cm tall.

Bolt is a gentle and affectionate boy who enjoys human company. Since moving into foster care, he has settled well and formed a strong bond with his foster carer.

He is described as calm, attentive and loving. Bolt walks beautifully on the lead and handles everyday life in the home well. He is clean in the house and will indicate when he needs to go outside. He is generally quiet and does not bark excessively.

Bolt lives around other dogs and tolerates them well. If he feels overwhelmed, he may adopt a dominant posture but does not escalate the behaviour.

He has no food aggression and is calm in the home environment. He does not jump up and has a steady, gentle manner. He enjoys relaxing on the sofa and being close to his people.

Bolt has some sores from spending a prolonged period in kennels and feels the cold easily. He would benefit from a warm and comfortable home environment where he can continue to recover fully.

Bolt is iElisa negative and ready to meet his forever family.

name: Snowdon
description:
Snowdon is a 3 year old neutered male medium mixed breed currently in Lincolnshire. He weighs approximately 20–22 kg and is iElisa negative.

Snowdon previously lived in a family home in Romania and is familiar with a home environment. He is described as very friendly and affectionate, with a strong focus on people.

He enjoys attention and physical closeness and will actively seek out affection.

He is playful, curious and enjoys exploring his surroundings. He is confident within the home environment and keen to interact with those around him.

Snowdon is currently unsure about walking on a lead and finds it intimidating. He is accepting of being carried and will require continued patient lead training.

Access to a secure garden will be important while this training progresses.

He is good with other dogs and shows friendly interest, although he has not yet been observed engaging in active play. He is also good with cats.

Snowdon would suit an adopter willing to continue his lead training and provide reassurance and structure as he builds confidence.

name: Hermione
description:
Hermione is a 7 year old female mixed breed currently in foster care in Lincolnshire. She was rescued from a public shelter and is now looking for a quiet, stable home.

Hermione is an affectionate and people-focused girl who enjoys close companionship. She is happiest when receiving attention, going for walks and exploring new scents. In the home, she enjoys relaxing and will often greet you with gentle, sleepy stretches.

She walks well on the lead, although she can occasionally be strong-willed about the direction she prefers. Her recall is good when motivated by treats, and she travels well in the car.

Hermione currently lives with other dogs in foster care. While she does not initiate conflict, she can lack boundaries around other dogs, particularly around food.

She has previously been attacked following an interaction over a treat and required surgery. She has fully recovered physically, but since this incident she can be reactive towards some dogs and other animals, including cats.

For this reason, Hermione would be best suited as the only pet in an adult-only home.

She can take a few days to warm up to men and to new environments, but once settled she forms strong bonds and enjoys affection and reassurance.

She shows natural guarding tendencies around her home and people, so a quieter household with limited visitors would suit her best. Slow and structured introductions to regular visitors will be important.

Hermione is eager to learn and responds well to positive reinforcement using treats and praise.

She would thrive in a calm, rural or quiet home environment where she can feel secure and enjoy being someone’s close companion.

name: Sophie
description:
Sophie is a 2 year old spayed female mixed breed currently in foster care in Lincolnshire. She weighs approximately 15 kg and is described as short-legged, sturdy and long-bodied. She is iElisa negative.

Sophie is a sweet-natured and affectionate girl who forms strong bonds with her people. She enjoys close companionship and will happily curl up nearby. She is gentle in her interactions and adapts well to new situations.

She is good with other dogs and enjoys their company. She can occasionally be a little bossy with smaller dogs but does not show aggression. She would also be happy living as an only dog.

Sophie is comfortable being handled and is very good at the vet. She travels well in the car and is clean in the house, sleeping through the night in her own bed.

She accepts wearing a lead but will benefit from continued lead training to build confidence and consistency when walking. She responds well to positive reinforcement and routine.

Sophie is slightly underweight at present but is steadily improving in foster care.

Sophie would suit a calm and stable home willing to continue her lead training and provide companionship and structure as she settles.

name: Macsen
description:
Meet Macsen (pronounced Maxon), a 3 year old male Cross-Breed. He is a beautiful, slender black and white boy who was rescued in October 2022 when he was just a puppy.

He was born and lived on the streets of Muscat until he was about 2 months old, when his mother was cruelly shot and killed. Macsen and his siblings were then rescued off the streets and taken to safety.

Macsen has always been a nervous/ wary character especially with people he doesn’t know. He is however friendly with the volunteers who he knows and trusts.

Macsen is currently living in a boarding facility and gets along really well with the other dogs there. He has one best friend in particular (Kaito) who he loves to play with.

For this reason, we think Macsen would be better suited to a home with at least one other dog for him to play with and learn from.

Due to Macsen’s nervous nature, he would be best suited to a quieter home in a rural/ semi rural area. He has very little experience around children so either a child free home or with older, dog savvy children would be best.

We don’t know what he is like with cats now, but he was fine with the cat in the previous boarding facility he resided at.

Macsen has never lived in a home environment but we would endeavour to find him a foster home in Muscat before he leaves Oman. He is leash trained though and will go for a walk with his doggy friends.

Although he is nervous, he has never shown any signs of fear aggression/ reactivity towards any of the volunteers or boarding staff. He will just need a lot of patience to help him adjust to his new life.

He is a healthy boy who is fully vaccinated, microchipped, neutered and titer tested (so he is ready to travel to the UK now). We will also test him for Brucellosis before he leaves for the UK (and any other test if required).

name: Sam
description:
Sam is an approximately 11 year old male medium mixed breed currently in Lincolnshire.

Sam is described as affectionate, intelligent and playful. Despite his age, he still enjoys bursts of energy and interactive play. He forms strong bonds with his primary carer and thrives on close companionship.

He is fully housetrained and is used to having free run of the home. He walks well on a harness and sits calmly to have his lead attached. He can be left alone for reasonable periods and enjoys learning new tricks and engaging in mental stimulation.

Sam currently lives alongside calm foster dogs and coexists well; however, he prefers not to share food, toys or personal space. For this reason, he is best suited as the only dog in the home.

He can be reactive towards unfamiliar visitors entering the house and shows protective behaviour around his home and primary person.

Slow introductions and clear boundaries are important. Once he trusts someone, he is affectionate and loyal.

Sam would be best suited to a quiet, adult-only home with limited visitors. A calm, rural or low-traffic environment would help him feel secure and settled.

He is looking for a committed adopter who understands his need for structure and consistency and can provide a stable retirement home.

name: John
description:
John is a 7 year old neutered male mixed breed weighing approximately 30 kg, currently in foster care in Scotland.

John has had a difficult start in life. He was previously kept chained and later lived as a stray before being rescued. After spending three years safely with his rescuer, he travelled to the UK and is now ready to find a permanent home.

He is described as affectionate, sociable and steady-natured. John enjoys human company and has met children aged 10 and over, interacting positively with them. He is confident, playful and enjoys attention and companionship.

John shares well with other dogs and is polite and easy-going in canine company. He currently lives with a cat and budgies in foster care without issue inside the home.

However, when out on walks he can show interest in cats and may attempt to chase, so ongoing management will be important.

He is fully housetrained and accepts wearing a collar and lead. He walks well but can pull at times due to excitement, particularly at the start of walks.

Continued lead training will help him progress further. He enjoys regular exercise and benefits from access to good walking areas.

John is intelligent and responsive and has good manners within the home. He would suit an active household able to provide structure, routine and companionship.

name: Rhea
description:
Meet Rhea, a 1 year old female Cross-Breed. She is a medium-sized girl weighing approximately 15 kg and is full of life just waiting to be lived.

Rhea was rescued just in time from an overcrowded shelter, but what she truly needs now is not just safety; she needs a home that understands her heart and her energy.

Rhea is incredibly sweet and loving. When she is beside you, she is calm, gentle and quiet. She leans into your hands, closes her eyes when you stroke her and soaks up affection like she has been waiting her whole life for it.

Rhea is actually more energetic than the photos show. She loves to run. She loves to move. She loves a bit of action and fun. She is young, healthy and full of spirit.

She would not be suitable for a family looking for a dog just to sit quietly on the sofa all day.

Rhea needs exercise. She needs walks. She needs play. She needs a family who enjoys being active and including their dog in their life.

She is friendly with dogs and loves attention from people. She would likely enjoy another friendly dog to share life with, but she also bonds strongly with her humans.

Imagine her running across a field, ears flopping, then coming back to you, tail wagging and ready for cuddles. That is Rhea.

She deserves a home where she can burn off her young energy and then curl up safely at the end of the day knowing she belongs.

Rhea is not broken. She is not difficult. She is simply young, alive and ready for a life she has never had the chance to live.

She can travel to the UK as soon as a home is offered.

name: Koi
description:
Koi is a medium English Setter who was originally bought by a hunter from a breeder but later abandoned to make space for another puppy.

The hunter even threatened to kill him if the rescue didn’t take him. Despite this harsh start, Koi remains cheerful, playful, and affectionate.

He is excellent with children, allowing them to pet him and enjoy the experience while staying calm and patient. Koi loves cuddles and human attention, and he is friendly with other dogs and people alike.

His medium-length coat is soft and well cared for, adding to his charm. Koi can live in a home with or without resident dogs and could also be cat tested for the right family.

He is a social, loving dog who will thrive in a home that offers affection and activity.

name: Nova
description:
Nova – 2–3 year old female Whippet Cross (Medium/Large, slim build)ova is a 2–3 year old spayed female Whippet cross currently in foster care in Doncaster. She has a slim, athletic build and enjoys running and open space.

Nova is affectionate, intelligent and sensitive. She thrives on routine and bonds closely with her primary person, often choosing to stay nearby. She enjoys fuss and interaction but benefits from calm, predictable handling.

She is friendly with people and dogs. She may bark briefly when visitors first arrive but settles quickly with reassurance and positive guidance. She has not shown aggression.

Nova plays well with other dogs and would benefit from living with a calm or playful resident dog for companionship and confidence. If she feels unsure, she will give herself space rather than escalate.

She is housetrained, crate trained and understands basic commands.

She walks well on a lead and harness without pulling and is calm around other dogs when out. She travels well in the car and prefers quieter walking environments, as busy areas can make her nervous.

She is improving steadily with continued exposure and training.

Nova is an active dog who enjoys running and outdoor activity, but she also settles well in the home and sleeps soundly overnight.

Nova would suit a patient, structured home able to provide regular exercise, routine and ongoing confidence-building. A secure garden is important for safe exercise. An adult-only home or one with older children would be most appropriate.

name: Alan
description:
Alan is a 3 year old neutered male medium mixed breed currently in Lincolnshire. He is iElisa negative.

Alan is described as calm and people-focused. He enjoys staying close to his humans and settles well into routine. He is not highly energetic and prefers companionship and quiet time in the garden over long, demanding adventures.

He is fully housetrained and sleeps through the night. He has interacted well with men and children.

Alan generally respects other dogs’ space and is largely uninterested in them. However, he can show dominant behaviour towards younger or smaller dogs.

For this reason, he would be happiest as an only dog or in a home without young or boisterous dogs.

He has not yet begun formal lead training and will require patient introduction to walking equipment and structured guidance as this progresses.

Alan would suit a calm, steady household looking for a relaxed companion dog who enjoys close human company and routine.

name: Bonnie
description:
Bonnie, also known as Bonbon, is an approximately 3 year old spayed female large mixed breed currently in foster care in Doncaster.

Bonnie is a gentle and sensitive dog who can be shy when meeting new people. She prefers a calm environment and takes time to build trust. Once bonded, she is affectionate and enjoys close companionship.

She is not aggressive but can be nervous around unfamiliar visitors. A quiet household with limited visitors will help her feel secure. She benefits from patient handling and consistent routine.

Bonnie thrives in the company of other dogs and must live with a calm, confident resident dog for reassurance and companionship.

She has previously lived with cats and may attempt to initiate play, so slow and managed introductions are required.

She is housetrained and crate trained. She sleeps overnight in her crate and can be left alone for short periods.

Bonnie walks well on a lead in quieter areas but remains cautious in busier environments. She is currently exercised on a long line due to a flight risk, and a secure garden is essential.

Continued confidence-building and structured training will be important.

Bonnie enjoys gentle play, grooming and relaxed time with her people. She responds well to food-based training.

Bonnie would suit a calm, rural or low-traffic home with patient adopters experienced in handling shy or sensitive dogs. Adults or older children who understand her need for space would be most appropriate.

name: Cassie
description:
Cassie is an approximately 10 month old female mixed breed currently in foster care in Lincolnshire.

She currently weighs around 13 kg and is expected to reach approximately 20 kg when fully grown.

Cassie was rescued from a public shelter and is now ready to find her permanent home.

She is described as affectionate and gentle in nature. Despite her young age, she shows calm behaviour around more nervous puppies and interacts well with other dogs.

Cassie is currently learning to walk on a lead and is making good progress.

As an adolescent dog, she will require continued training, structure and guidance as she matures into adulthood.

She would suit a home prepared to continue her training and provide routine and consistency.

name: Holly
description:
Meet Holly. Holly is a 7 year old female Akita and, despite not having the easiest start to life, her spirit shines bright.

She was found straying and taken to the pound in very poor condition — underweight, with open sores and patches of missing fur.

Thanks to good care and treatment, her coat is recovering beautifully, and she’s well on her way to looking and feeling her best again.

What’s truly remarkable is that, even after everything she has been through, Holly remains a happy, lively, and affectionate girl.

Holly is a joy to walk. She’s lovely on the lead and absolutely adores getting out and about for adventures. She’s also dog-friendly, so she could potentially live with a calm, compatible male companion, depending on how they get on when they meet.

Because we don’t have any background history for her, Holly will only be placed in a home with children aged 12 or over.

This little sweetheart loves to play, especially with her favourite balls. She’ll chase them, fetch them, and proudly drop them back at your feet, ready for another round.

At pint-sized perfection, Holly truly deserves a family of her own — one that will love her, include her in everyday life, and show her the kindness she has missed out on so far.

If you think Holly might be the one for you, we would love to hear from you.

name: Pernales
description:
Pernales is a 3-year-old male Griffon. Born on 03/05/2022, he is currently in the North of Spain and searching for his forever home. He was surrendered by his owner, a hunter, because he was not considered good at hunting.

He is described as a huge and soft animal, super elegant and dignified in his presence. Pernales is a very balanced and calm dog, which is a wonderful trait in such a strong and powerful boy. His impressive build is matched by a loving nature.

Pernales is sociable with other dogs and gets along well with them. He is also very obedient with people and is not shy, showing confidence in human company.

Everything about his description points to him being a very good dog with a steady temperament.

He is, however, very strong and powerful, so he will need someone physically capable of managing him on the lead. He is not used to walking on a lead, which means patience, strength and consistent training will be essential.

With the right guidance, he has the foundation to learn and adapt.

As a scenthound, Pernales has had some hunting training. Because of this background, he may have zero recall, so this will need to be carefully managed in his new home.

A secure environment and ongoing training will be important to help him settle safely.

He can live with cats, other dogs and older children, which makes him suitable for a variety of homes with the right structure in place. Full rescue back-up is provided, offering reassurance and continued support.

Pernales may not have been suited to hunting life, but he clearly has all the qualities needed to become a devoted and dignified companion.

name: Beans
description:
Meet Beans, a 15 month old female German Shepherd Dog cross Labrador Retriever.

Beans came into our rescue as an unclaimed stray. From the moment she arrived, it was clear she was a big, enthusiastic youngster with a zest for life and a lot to learn.

When Beans first arrived, she was showing signs of pain around her hips, which was concerning for such a young dog.

Our physiotherapist, Poppy, assessed her and confirmed she was uncomfortable, but also noted that Beans was poorly muscled for her age, something that can significantly contribute to joint discomfort.

While Beans was spayed, a full set of X-rays was carried out. These showed very mild hip dysplasia, which is extremely common in both German Shepherd Dogs and Labrador Retrievers.

Our vet advised that building muscle was essential, as increased muscle strength would provide better joint stability and reduce discomfort.

We are pleased to say that one month on, Beans’ fitness has improved significantly, and she is no longer showing any signs of pain after exercise.

Beans arrived as a big, rambunctious puppy who genuinely believes she is a small dog. She approaches life with unfiltered enthusiasm and excitement.

Since arriving with us, we have worked hard on her manners, and she has come on in leaps and bounds, particularly in learning to regulate her excitement.

Beans is still young and any new owner will need to be committed to continuing her training. She is a quick learner and does very well when given consistent boundaries and support.

Beans loves other dogs, but she is still learning how to read social cues. If another dog clearly tells her they do not want to play, she respects that.

However, if a dog corrects her in a way that also seems playful, Beans sometimes misunderstands and continues trying to engage, which can be intimidating given her size. Ongoing training and guidance will really help her here.

We feel Beans may previously have been a garden dog, as many everyday situations still seem brand new and incredibly exciting to her. The positive side of this is that she improves with every interaction and learns well when supported correctly.

Beans is very much a product of her environment.

High energy environment equals bonkers Beans.Calm environment equals calm Beans.

Because of this, we feel she would be best suited to a home with another calm, well-balanced dog to help guide and support her.

Horses: Good, though she occasionally forgets herself and play-bows, trying to get them to play.Sheep and goats: Generally good, but will chase if they run, not out of malice but because they think it is a game.Cats: Not yet tested. We will update once we have more information.

With continued training, Beans is very close to becoming a dog that is reliable around most animals. An experienced and committed home could shape her enthusiasm into an incredibly well-rounded family dog.

Older children only. She has shown no aggression but forgets her size when excited. At 40 kg, she could easily knock over a small child.

Owners who can provide at least one hour of exercise per day

A home with experience of German Shepherd Dogs, Labrador Retrievers, or similar breeds

Owners who are committed to continuing her training

Beans can currently be left for up to four hours, as long as she has had a walk beforehand and is left with a canine companion. She has been absolutely fine with this routine.

Rough Monthly CostsInsurance: £44.00Food: £60.00Supplements: £20.00Vet Club (vaccinations, flea and worming): £23.99

Beans is fully vaccinated, microchipped, neutered, and up to date with flea and worming treatment. She also comes with five weeks free insurance.

name: Apolo
description:
Stunning Apolo came to the UK in January 2026 after having waited in Romania for 4 years. This incredible boy is friendly with humans and is good with female dogs of the same or larger size.

He will tolerate smaller and male dogs but is not overly enamoured by them. He enjoys his walks and, once settled, he will love going on adventures. Apolo isn’t too keen on cats and has not been tested with children.

We are looking for experienced adopters as initially he can be shy. A rural or semi-rural home with a garden would be ideal for him.

Apolo is neutered, fully vaccinated and weighs approximately 22kg.

Full rescue backup and support throughout the adoption process and for the lifetime of the dog.

name: Blue
description:
Blue is a 4 year old male British Bulldog with a big personality and an even bigger heart!

Weighing in at 28kg, he’s a friendly, fun-loving boy who’s full of life — and bounce! Because of his excitable nature, he’s best suited to a home with children aged 13+.

True to his breed, Blue can be a little stubborn and occasionally over-boisterous, but unlike many Bulldogs, he loves a good walk and will happily trot along at your side.

He’s also sociable with other dogs on walks, so he could potentially live with a well-matched canine companion following careful introductions.

Blue is still working on his manners — he can bark in the car due to excitement and may get a little “humpy” when meeting new people.

However, this has already started to improve following his recent neutering (during which an umbilical hernia was also successfully repaired).

He’s looking for a patient and committed family who are willing to continue his training and help him channel all that energy in the right direction. In return, you’ll get a gorgeous, loving companion who is absolutely worth the effort!

Please note: We do not rehome to households with unneutered resident dogs.

name: Oren
description:
Oren is a 3-year-old male Lurcher. He is looking for a loving home where he can enjoy an active lifestyle and continue doing the things that make him happiest.

With his cheerful nature and playful personality, Oren is sure to bring plenty of enjoyment to the right family.

One of Oren’s favourite activities is going on long country walks. He enjoys exploring the outdoors and taking in everything around him, making him an ideal companion for someone who loves spending time in the countryside or enjoys regular walks.

Oren is also a big fan of mealtimes and has a healthy enthusiasm for his food. Alongside his love of food, he has a playful side and enjoys spending time with his toys.

He is particularly determined when it comes to finding his favourite one and will happily empty the entire toy box just to reach the toy hidden at the bottom.

He is dog friendly and could happily share his home with other dogs. However, he cannot live with cats and is looking for an adult-only home with no children.

A calm and understanding environment will help him continue to enjoy life and settle comfortably into his new home.

Oren is ready to find a forever family that will appreciate his love of walks, toys, and good food. With the right home, he will make a loyal and enjoyable companion who is eager to share everyday adventures with the people who care for him.

name: Groot
description:
Groot is a 2-year-old male Saluki Cross. He came into the rescue after being found as a stray and has since been given the care he needed to begin a fresh chapter in his life.

Since arriving at the rescue, he has made excellent progress and is now ready to find a loving forever home.

When Groot first arrived, he needed to gain some much-needed weight. With the care and support of the rescue, he has recovered well and is now embracing everything that life has to offer.

His improvement has allowed his personality to shine through as he continues to settle into a happier routine.

Groot is enjoying exploring the world around him and discovering new experiences. Every day brings new opportunities for him to learn and build his confidence.

He is also learning what it means to be a much-loved member of a family, something he clearly deserves.

He is dog friendly and would be happy to live with other dogs that can continue to help him enjoy life. However, he cannot live with cats, so his new home will need to be cat free. He is also looking for a home with children aged 14 years and over.

Groot is searching for a family that will continue to guide him as he settles into home life. With patience, kindness, and ongoing support, he has every opportunity to thrive.

He is ready to leave his past behind and enjoy the security, comfort, and companionship of a permanent home where he can continue to flourish.

name: Bella
description:
Bella. Nearly 10-month-old French Bulldog.

Currently living in an adult foster home with other dogs and visiting grandchildren.

Bella has had a rather unsettled start to life.

She spent her first 6–7 months with one family before being sold privately through Facebook for £250. She then lived with a lady and her young child in a flat, but after only a few months she was once again going to be passed on.

Thankfully, a relative of one of our foster families became concerned that Bella would simply be advertised on Facebook again and contacted us. She arrived with us just in time, as she had also just come into season.

Bella has now been with us for a month and has made lovely progress. She is very much a typical Frenchie in many ways – affectionate, funny and full of character – but it has become clear that she missed out on some important socialisation and basic training during her early months.

Her foster mum has been working incredibly hard to help her gain confidence and learn how to cope with situations she has never really experienced before.

Bella absolutely adores people. She loves fuss, cuddles and being close to you. She has also lived happily alongside the other dogs in her foster home, playing and relaxing with them most of the time.

However, when excitement levels suddenly rise – such as someone ringing the doorbell or at feeding time – Bella can become over-aroused and rush towards the other dogs.

Feeding time is easily managed by using her crate, but unexpected situations like visitors arriving are harder to predict.

For that reason, we feel Bella would be happiest as an only dog, where she doesn’t have the pressure of competing with or reacting to other dogs when excitement levels increase.

Please don’t let that put you off though – we’ve included plenty of videos below so you can see just how relaxed and happy she is with the other dogs during everyday life.

Shorts clips of different situations with Bella

Walking has also been a learning curve. Initially Bella pulled badly on the lead, but with a better-fitting harness she has improved enormously. She also wanted to chase moving cars, something that has reduced significantly with patient training.

She will still occasionally focus on traffic if she hears it, but this continues to improve.

Her favourite thing in the world is being somewhere quieter where she can run, chase her ball and proudly bring it back.

She now enjoys lovely walks on Dartmoor and along the river, where she has begun enjoying off-lead walks and her recall is coming on really well. Again, we’ve included videos so you can see her progress for yourselves.

Bella now travels well in the car too, especially if she is either in the footwell or in a covered crate where she feels secure.

She is clean in the house and sleeps happily in her crate all night without any problems.

She has also met her foster family’s grandchildren. Lots of younger children visiting together proved a little overwhelming for her, but with an older, calm granddaughter she was relaxed, affectionate and thoroughly enjoyed the company, as you’ll see in the videos.

When life is calm and predictable, Bella is a wonderfully easy little dog to live with. We feel her unsettled early life has left her finding busy households, frequent visitors and lots of activity quite stressful.

She simply hasn’t had the stability that every puppy deserves.

Because of this, we are looking for a home that can offer her exactly that.

No cats.A quieter home without lots of visitors or constant comings and goings.

Someone with experience of rescue dogs who understands that confidence takes time to build.

In return, you’ll have a loyal, affectionate little companion who is already showing just how much she can blossom when given patience, consistency and love.

Her foster family have done an amazing job helping Bella on her journey so far and will continue working with her until the perfect home comes along.

Please take the time to watch the videos below. They show the real Bella – playing, relaxing, learning and becoming more confident every day. We are incredibly proud of how far she has already come.

name: Sebastian
description:
Sebastian – 19-month-old Toy Poodle, currently being fostered in Gloucestershire in an adult home with other dogs.

This handsome little chap came into our care from a breeder, having had very little experience of the outside world. He arrived as a completely terrified, shut-down little dog who simply didn’t know how to cope with everyday life.

He was also in need of veterinary treatment. He had a badly infected mouth caused by retained baby teeth and painful ear infections.

Underneath it all was a beautiful little dog who had simply never been given the opportunity to experience life beyond the environment he had always known.

Sebastian is in a very experienced foster home with a wonderful group of confident dogs who have helped show him that the world isn’t quite so scary.

The transformation has been incredible. If you have watched our videos from the day he arrived until now, you will see just how far this special little boy has come.

However, despite all of his progress, the emotional scars remain.

Sebastian has formed a very strong bond with his foster mum and trusts her completely. She has carefully introduced him to new experiences, including visits to the local park and even a couple of agility shows, all managed at his pace.

He has coped incredibly well, but when he becomes frightened or overwhelmed, he can panic. On those occasions he has bitten—not through aggression or malice, but purely out of fear.

He is still very wary of other members of the household and needs time, patience and understanding to build trust.

We know this means Sebastian will not be the right dog for the majority of applicants, and we want to be completely honest about that.

Sebastian is looking for a genuinely experienced home. Not simply people who have owned dogs before, but adopters who have hands-on experience of rehabilitating extremely fearful, under-socialised dogs, particularly those from breeder or similar backgrounds.

He will also need one or more confident resident dogs to continue showing him the way.

We are deliberately not producing a long checklist of what Sebastian needs because those with the right experience will already understand the commitment involved.

They will know that progress comes in tiny steps, that trust cannot be rushed, and that patience, routine and gentle encouragement are the keys to helping dogs like Sebastian thrive.

If you have that experience, we would love to hear from you. If you are looking for an easy little companion or are new to rehabilitation work with fearful dogs, Sebastian is not the right match.

We owe it to him to find the home that can continue the incredible work his foster family has started.

Sebastian has now had his dental treatment, retained baby teeth removed, ear infections treated, has been neutered and is fully vaccinated. He is now ready to find that very special forever home.

name: Malna
description:
Malna is a 3 year old crossbreed girl, she was dumped on the roadside along with her sister at about 2.5 months of age. She is medium size, weight: 15 kg, shoulder height: 44 cm.

Malna is a lovely girl, she is friendly and kind and loves everyone. She is energetic and playful and sociable around her doggie mates.

She enjoys nothing more than running around in the fields with other dogs, playing a chase. She cooperates nicely with humans too and is very kind with humans.

She enjoys car rides and is good around children too. She also walks nicely on the lead.

Malna would be best suited for a family where she is not left alone for extended periods and she is included in her family’s activities. She would be happiest in an active family, she would happily be your company on long walks, hikes and holidays.

Older dog savvy children will be considered.

Malna would probably be happiest living with another playful dog but she could also live happily as the only dog and the centre of attention in her home.

As all rescue dogs, she will need time, patience, love and commitment from her adopting family to become a happy, well-balanced dog.

Malna is currently in Hungary and can travel to the UK as soon as the right family is found for her.

She comes spayed, fully vaccinated, microchipped, dewormed, flea and tick treated, with an EU passport and DEFRA approved paperwork.

Adoption is subject to Home Check and Adoption fee. Full RBU provided.

name: Chill
description:
Chill is a 1-year-old smaller medium-sized Puli girl with the softest eyes and the gentlest soul.

This beautiful girl was found abandoned alongside another Puli cross and taken to a kill shelter, where her future looked uncertain. Thankfully, she was given a second chance and came into our care.

When Chill first arrived, she was timid and reserved, unsure of the world around her. But once she settled into boarding and realised she was safe, her true personality slowly began to shine.

Today, her tail is up, she greets us with a smile, and every day she grows a little braver.

True to her name, Chill is exactly that – calm, quiet, easy-going and wonderfully relaxed. She is relaxed around other dogs, too and mingles beautifully with them, although she can feel overwhelmed by noisy or boisterous dogs.

She walks nicely on the lead and has a peaceful, gentle nature.

After being abandoned once, we would love her next chapter to be the one she truly deserves — a home where she will never be left behind again, where she is included in everyday life and can become a treasured member of the family.

Currently in Hungary and ready to travel to the UK once the right family is found.

name: Floki
description:
I’m a 5 year old medium size cross breed boy.

For 3.5 years, I’ve been living in a shelter in Hungary, that’s more than half my life spent waiting behind a fence, hoping someone might stop… might notice me… might choose me. But no one ever has. Sometimes I feel invisible. I’m only 5 years old.

I’m not loud or demanding. I’m patient and quiet. I’m the kind of dog who waits in silence and hopes that one day someone will see the good boy I truly am and will not walk past me.

I love my walks, and I walk beautifully on the lead. I enjoy sniffing the world and feeling the sun on my back. I love hoomans—every scratch behind the ears and every cuddle means the world to me, because I get so little affection here.

But I treasure every moment. I never take kindness for granted.

I’m calm and peaceful around other dogs. I don’t want trouble; I just want love.

And although my muzzle is beginning to grey, please don’t think I’m old. I’m still young, playful in my soft and gentle way, and I dream—every single day—of having a home, a bed of my own, and a family who finally calls me theirs.

I have spent so long waiting, but I haven’t given up.I still believe my person is out there.

If you’re reading this… maybe it’s you.Maybe you’re the one who will make sure I’m invisible no more.

Floki is ready to travel from Hungary once the right family is found.

He comes neutered, fully vaccinated, microchipped, with an EU passport.

name: Connie
description:
Connie is a 2 year old female Puli Cross. Her story began in a public pound, where she grew up in harsh conditions. A year ago, she was rescued in a heartbreaking state – skin and bone, frightened and frail.

With care, love, and patience, Connie has blossomed into a happy, affectionate girl. Today she’s full of life – her waggy tail never stops, she adores treats and cuddles, and she has even learned to smile when she’s with the people she loves. This beautiful girl has learned to trust again!

Connie loves the company of other dogs and is especially playful – wrestling and mingling are her favourite games! She would be just as happy snuggling up on the sofa as she is joining in on adventures.

Connie is still waiting in a small shelter in Hungary, dreaming of her forever family. She deserves a home where she will be cherished, spoiled, and loved for the sweet, resilient girl she is.

For Connie, an experienced rescue dog home would be ideal – someone patient and understanding, ready to continue guiding her on her journey.

She could live happily with another friendly and playful dog or as the only dog in the home.

2 years oldPlayful, affectionate, sociableSpayed, vaccinated, microchipped, with EU passportCan travel to the UK once her family is found

If you can give Connie the love-filled home she has been waiting for, please get in touch.

Adoption subject to home check & fee. Full RBU provided.

name: Gesztenye
description:
Gesztenye is a beautiful 2-year-old medium-sized brindle girl with the sweetest soul. She adores people, loves playing with other dogs and greets everyone she meets with a wagging tail and a hopeful smile.

For over two years, Gesztenye and her sister Zserbo have shared everything. They were rescued together from a kill shelter when they were only a few weeks old. They grew up side by side, slept in the same kennel, and waited together for someone to finally choose them.

Now Zserbo’s dream has come true. She has found a wonderful family in the UK.

But little Gesztenye will soon watch her sister leave… and for the first time in her life, she will be alone.

She has so much love to give and asks for so little in return – just a family to call her own.

Gesztenye is friendly with dogs and would happily live with another canine companion. She is affectionate, playful and kind natured, and can also live with older dog-savvy children.

She’s looking for a home where she will be part of family life and not left alone for long periods.

Like all rescue dogs, Gesztenye will need time, patience and love, but in return she will give you her whole heart.

Gesztenye is currently in Hungary and is ready to travel to the UK as soon as her forever family finds her.

She is spayed, fully vaccinated, treated for parasites, comes with and EU pet passport.

attributes.Breed: Staffordshire bull terrier cross labrador retriever

name: Zelda
description:
Meet Zelda, a 2 year old female Staffordshire Bull Terrier cross Labrador Retriever — a brave and beautiful girl who has survived unimaginable cruelty yet still greets the world with love.

She came from hell. Zelda spent her early life chained so short she couldn’t even stand, the chain cutting deep into her neck. Despite such cruelty, she never lost her spark. Once freed, she greeted her rescuers with a wagging tail and a forgiving heart.

Now safe, she’s blossomed into an energetic, happy-natured girl. She’s medium-sized, affectionate, and adores people.

Zelda gets along well with other dogs — though she can be a bit boisterous in her play — and would thrive either as an only dog or with a friendly, tolerant companion.

In the kennel, she doesn’t get the exercise or freedom she craves, and she’s longing for a home where she can run, play, and finally just be a dog. She loves her walks, though she does pull on the lead, simply excited to be out exploring the world she missed for so long.

Zelda would suit an active home that can give her the exercise, structure, and affection she craves, so her joyful spirit can shine at long last. Older children will be considered.

Zelda has endured pain no animal should ever know. She deserves a life full of love, freedom, and fun.

Fully vaccinated, spayed, microchipped, with an EU pet passport. Ready to travel.

name: Cleo
description:
Cleo is an adorable 11-month-old small mixed breed girl looking for a loving forever home. She and her three siblings were found abandoned as tiny puppies, all in very poor condition, frightened and unsure of the world around them.

With their parents unknown and their future uncertain, all they had was each other.

Thankfully, Cleo has blossomed into a wonderful young dog. Although naturally a little shy when meeting new people or experiencing new situations, she is incredibly sweet, gentle, and affectionate once she feels safe.

Her confidence continues to grow every day.

She loves playing with other dogs and enjoys spending time with people she knows and trusts. Cleo would thrive in a calm, patient home where she can continue building her confidence at her own pace.

In return, she will reward her family with unwavering loyalty and love.

Cleo could happily live with another friendly well-balanced dog and she has all the potential to live with cats, too.

As a small-sized girl, Cleo would make a lovely companion for someone looking for a gentle, kind-hearted dog.

She comes spayed, microchipped, fully vaccinated and with an EU pet passport.

name: Apollo
description:
Meet Apollo – a gentle soul ready for a new life.

Apollo, a 3.5-year-old medium size cross-breed boy, whose life until now has been far from kind, has finally been freed from a life lived on a chain. Yet somehow, despite everything, he has held onto his sweetness, his trust, and his huge heart.

Apollo is incredibly human-centred, affectionate, and loving — the kind of dog who just wants to be close to people and soak up kindness.
