name: Odin
description:
Odin is an 18-month-old male Cross-Breed. Odin is one of three brothers currently searching for the forever home of his dreams. He’s already had quite the start to life and is more than ready to trade kennel walls for the comforts of a loving family.

Odin’s the size of a small Collie, so he’s a great medium-sized companion — not so big that he’ll knock over your nan, but not so small he’ll disappear between the couch cushions.

Odin has been neutered, fully vaccinated, and microchipped, which means he’s ready to go without any of the faff. He’s a friendly chap who gets along well with his brothers, which shows he’s got solid doggy social skills already.

That’s a major win if you’re hoping to bring him into a multi-dog home or want a pup who can make friends at the dog park.

Odin also seems to be friendly with cats, which is basically the Holy Grail of dog qualities — no fur-flying drama in sight.

His easy-going nature will make him a delightful addition to many kinds of households, whether it’s a busy family home, a couple who love outdoor adventures, or an individual looking for a loyal sidekick.

Because Odin is still a young dog, he needs a family, couple, or individual with time and patience to teach him about the world. He’s eager to learn and experience life outside kennel walls, so he’ll thrive in a home where he can get plenty of guidance, attention, and love.

He’s already spent a significant chunk of his life in kennels, which is just heartbreaking for a pup as sweet as him. Giving Odin a stable home now would mean giving him the chance he deserves to discover the joys of comfy beds, long walks, and the occasional cheeky treat.

To make things easier, Odin will be delivered straight to his new home by a registered pet transport company, so you won’t have to worry about a stressful handover or tricky logistics. All you have to do is open your door — and your heart — to this lovely boy.

Odin is truly a diamond in the rough, and whoever adopts him will not only be changing his life forever but will gain a loyal, happy companion who will return that kindness tenfold.

name: Brown
description:
Brown – 5 year 8 month old male Cross-Breed is a brown, medium-sized pup in Cyprus who has come a long way from the terrified dog he once was.

This is Brown. He doesn’t push to be first in line for treats. He doesn’t run to greet strangers. Instead, Brown watches quietly from a distance, his soft eyes filled with a lifetime of stories he can’t tell.

Brown is one of the many abandoned hunting dogs in Cyprus—discarded when no longer “useful.” When he first came to the shelter, he was terrified of people. He cowered in the corner, trembling at the sound of footsteps, flinching at the touch of a kind hand.

It broke our hearts. But over time, something beautiful started to happen. Slowly—very slowly—Brown began to learn that not all humans would hurt him. He began to trust.

A little tail wag here, a gentle nuzzle there. He still hides when strangers come, but if he knows you… he leans in. He gives you his heart.

Brown is shy with people, but once he bonds with you, he is deeply affectionate and loyal. And with other dogs? He’s wonderful. Calm, gentle, happy to share his space and his love. Other dogs give him confidence. They show him that the world isn’t such a scary place after all.

Brown has come so far. Now he just needs a home. He’s looking for someone patient, someone kind, someone who understands that healing takes time—but love makes it all worth it. He would thrive in a calm home, ideally with another dog to help guide him.

name: Chance
description:
Chance is a 2 year old male Cross-Breed and is currently being fostered in Surrey, ready to find his forever home with a family who will adore him.

Chance is a small-to-medium-sized dog with a soft white coat, a cheeky personality, and the cutest little Mohawk. He’s full of character, very affectionate, and ready to find his forever home.

He walks beautifully on the lead and enjoys off-lead time at the park. Chance is muzzle trained, and when he is off lead, he does wear his muzzle. That said, he’s friendly with most dogs and people—especially if they have a dog with them!

Chance currently lives with a resident dog and gets along wonderfully with her.

At home, he’s loving, cuddly, and calm. He enjoys a good walk followed by a nap (sometimes even before breakfast is finished!) and will happily flop over in front of you for belly rubs. He’s food-motivated, learns quickly, and does an adorable little spin when asked to sit.

He does best with slow introductions to new people in the home and builds trust over time. Once he knows you, he’s loyal, doting, and will look at you like you’re his whole world.

We’ve grown very attached to Chance, and while it’ll be hard to say goodbye, we’re excited to see him find the love he deserves. If you ever need someone to care for him while you’re away, we’d happily take him back in a heartbeat.

If you think Chance could be the one for you, get in touch to arrange a meet-and-greet. He’s ready to steal your heart.

name: Kia
description:
Kia is a lovely approximately 2-3 year old, large sized crossbreed who travelled to the UK from Spain recently and is currently fostered in the west midlands area.

Kia was originally rescued from the streets of Spain and spent over a year waiting in the shelter for her chance of a home.

In her time in the shelter Kia was noted to be people and dog friendly but disliked cats.

She is currently under assessment in the UK and so far has shown to absolutely love people, she would probably be best living with a calmer male dog on correct introductions. She isn’t sure about big bouncy dogs and can grumble at them.

Kia is happy to be crated and is clean in the home. She has not been destructive and walks well on the lead too. She is currently learning basic commands such as sit, down etc

Kia is a calm girl who loves attention and is more than happy to climb into your lap to get it! (Although with her size this is quite a challenge at times).

Despite being calm for the majority of time she does have bursts of energy and due to her size would be best homed with children 8+ due to the potential for knocking little children over by accident.

name: Aladdin
description:
I am a charmer and will want fuss from most people even strangers.

I need a prospective adopter to visit me a couple of time or more to get to know me before I can go on a home trial

I cannot be placed in a property with no direct access to a private garden.

I need a home that is at ease with my kind of dog, who have a good understanding and experience of dog behaviour.

name: Cleo
description:
I need a prospective adopter to visit me a couple of time or more to get to know me before I can go on a home trial

I need a home that is at ease with my kind of dog, who have a good understanding and experience of dog behaviour.

name: Jewel
description:
I have been through a lot and need a home who has dog experience and wants to offer a home to a real Underdog

She is new to lead walking and would like to continue this training in her new home so that she can go on plenty of adventures! She can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged, 13+ who are sensible and will allow her time to settle in at her own pace. She will need adopters with ex-breeding experience who can understand her needs, and will need an extra-secure garden where she can be safe as she settles in.

Minnow is a lovely girl who just needs plenty of time, patience and TLC. With the support of a confident canine companion and an understanding family, we're sure she will continue to blossom and become a wonderful addition to her forever home.

name: Jerry
description:
I need a calm and quiet adult only home with adopters with experience of collies.

I could live with another dog, or by myself. I cannot live with cats.

I would love a garden to run and play in!

I would like an active home and love to go for walks.

I have lived in a home before so know the basics.

I am neutered and ready to find my forever home!

Jerry is a lovely boy who originally came to us from a breeder a few years ago and went on to find a wonderful forever home. Sadly, through no fault of his own, he has now returned to our care due to his adopters' ill health.

Jerry is a Collie lover's dream! He is affectionate, clever and eager to be part of the family. He is house trained, walks beautifully on the lead and we are told he has excellent recall too. He is a very smart boy who already knows a range of commands includingsit,wait,off,dropandleave, and he would thrive in an active home where he can be kept mentally and physically stimulated.

Since moving down to one of our field kennels, Jerry has become much more relaxed and settled. Being in a quieter environment has really allowed his wonderful personality to shine. He is incredibly loving and has shown us just how well he can socialise with other dogs. In fact, he has been so calm and sensible around them that he has even been used during one-to-one behaviour sessions with reactive dogs, where he has been an absolute superstar. Because of this, we feel Jerry could happily live with another well-matched dog, although careful introductions would still be important.

Jerry would still be best suited to an adult-only home with adopters who have experience of Collies and rescue dogs. He would love a rural or quieter home where he can continue to enjoy a peaceful lifestyle, and he would benefit from adopters who are around for much of the day and have plenty of time to spend with him.

Jerry has shown some signs of separation anxiety in the past, so his new family will need to continue building up the time he is left gradually. We are told that he is happy being left for short periods but will need patience and understanding while he settles into his new home.

One area where Jerry has made fantastic progress is with his noise sensitivity. While he can still notice unexpected noises, he is coping with them far better than before. Rather than becoming distressed, he is now much more likely to simply look towards his handler as if to ask, "What was that?" before moving on. His growing confidence has been wonderful to see, although his adopters should still be prepared to continue supporting him with gentle reassurance and positive experiences around unfamiliar sounds.

Jerry has settled back into rescue life beautifully. He loves a cuddle, enjoys a good play session and is an incredibly rewarding dog to spend time with. He is a truly special boy with so much love to give, and we know he has all the qualities to make an exceptional companion for the right family.

Jerry previously had a wound on his right paw which caused a limp. This has now healed well and he is no longer showing any signs of lameness.

Jer-bear, Jerry! This handsome boy is going to melt someone’s heart.

Jerry has come in from a home with a variety of noise related triggers but do not let this put you off meeting him, for he is one quick brave border collie. He was once visibly stressed at the sight of a can of pop and more stressed when carbonated drink cans/bottles were opened. He has improved and is not as stressed when he sees a can of pop and due to him moving around the rescue we have given him some time to settle as he wasn’t feeling himself in his previous kennel.

Since moving he has been showing us bit by bit his playful sassy side. He loves going for his morning walk to take a break from the overwhelming kennels, Jerry has even been socialising with other dogs. We have found that he gets on well with other dogs however if put into an overwhelming situation he is likely to redirect onto his kennel buddy so is safer for him and any other dogs if he is not homed with one. We have found that once he is comfortable with his people, he is quick to desensitise to certain triggers.

For example: one of his handlers is diabetic and uses cans of lucozade to treat hypos on walks and in kennels. He has become alert but has not reacted and is less anxious at the sight of cans or bottles now

When I first met Jerry I had heard about his triggers and was very curious, he is a very interesting young dog who is bound to be the light of someone’s life!

I have been working with Jerry for a little while now and have found that his can/bottle related trigger is a bit deeper than we were led to believe, the visual prompt causes him some stress, but found that he is quick to look for comfort. He really enjoys spending time with his doggy friends and looks to humans for comfort, and enjoys going out for walks, he seems to feel more relaxed on walks and have found once triggered by a noise he over analyses the indoor environment not so much the outdoor space.

During Jerry's stay here I plan to slowly introduce new noises and help him to understand that new noises are not necessarily a bad thing.

Jerry is a lovely boy who originally came to us from a breeder a few years ago and went on to find a wonderful forever home. Sadly, through no fault of his own, he has now returned to our care due to his adopters ill health.

Jerry is a Collie lover’s dream! He is affectionate, clever and eager to be part of the family. He is house trained, walks nicely on the lead and we are told that he has good recall too. He is a very smart boy who already knows a range of commands including sit, wait, off, drop and leave, and would thrive in an active home where he can be kept both mentally and physically stimulated.

Jerry would like to be the only dog in his forever home. He would be best suited to an adult only home and would benefit from adopters with collie and rescue dog experience. He would love a rural home, as he can be sensitive to certain sounds and so homes in busier areas wouldn't be suitable for him. He would really benefit from adopters who are around for much of the day and have plenty of time to spend with him.

Jerry does show some signs of separation anxiety, so his new family will need to continue building up the time he is left gradually. We are told that he is happy being left for short periods but will need patience and understanding while he settles. He isn’t keen on car travel, and he can be sensitive to sounds and may react to sounds such as fizzy drink cans or bottles opening, sneezing, coughing, nose blowing, printers, hoovers, microwaves, lorry reversing beeps, motorbike revving, army range noise and fireworks. He will bark towards you but with reassurance he settles quickly. He has never bitten and is just worried but his new owners will need to continue noise desensitization training in the home. It may never be something he entirely overcomes.

Jerry has settled back into the rescue well and is a wonderful boy who is already enjoying snuggles and really loves to play! He is a truly special boy who has so much love to give and is ready to find a calm, understanding home to call his own once again.

He has had a wound on his right paw that has caused a limp, which has since healed and he is no longer showing signs of limping.

Whimsey came to us from a breeder as a very worried little girl who found the world quite overwhelming. When she first arrived, she was unsettled and skittish, needing plenty of time and reassurance to help her feel safe. Since then, she has made wonderful progress and has really started to show what a special girl she is.

While Whimsey has come on tremendously, she can still be nervous and unsure around new people. She will need a calm, patient and understanding home that is willing to give her the time and space she needs to build trust and settle at her own pace. Once she feels safe, her affectionate and loving personality truly shines through. She could also live with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over who can respect her need for a gentle introduction and allow her to settle in at her own pace.

Whimsey walks nicely on a lead, but as she can still be sensitive to new experiences, her adopters will need to continue introducing her to the world gently and at a pace she is comfortable with, helping her build confidence without becoming overwhelmed.

Whimsey really enjoys spending time with other dogs and loves socialising with her canine friends in the exercise yards. We now feel she could happily live with another resident dog of a similar size, provided they get along well during a successful meet and greet. Like many dogs, Whimsey can be a little selective about her friendships, so finding the right canine companion will be important. She would also be perfectly happy as the only dog in the home, where she could soak up all the love and attention from her family while continuing to enjoy opportunities to socialise with other dogs on walks. She cannot live with cats.

Whimsey has such a sweet heart and has already shown just how much progress she can make when given kindness, patience and understanding. With the right home behind her, we know she will continue to blossom into a wonderfully affectionate companion and a much-loved member of the family.

Whimsey arrived with an abscess on the right side of her jaw, which has been treated by our veterinary team. Our vets have also noted that she has a fractured canine tooth with no root or nerve exposure. At this stage, no treatment is required, but it should be monitored by her adopters and their own vet. She has also received treatment for a urinary tract infection, which has been successfully managed under veterinary guidance.

Oh, my heart. Whimsey has completely stolen it.

She is honestly one of the most loving, affectionate, and gentle girls I've ever met. The moment I walk into her kennel or sit with her in the yard, she melts into me. All she wants is kisses, cuddles, and to be as close to you as possible. She has so much love to give!

She's doing so well with her dog socialising too and absolutely adores her best friend, Royal.

Whimsey is going to make the most incredible addition to a very lucky family. She deserves so much more than just being someone's dog. She deserves to be a cherished member of the family, included in all of life's little moments, loved unconditionally, and never made to wonder if she's enough again.

I truly can't wait for the day she finds the home she's been waiting for. Whoever gets to call this beautiful girl theirs is going to be incredibly lucky.

Whimsey has come on so well since she first arrived. She’s bonded with me so much and always welcomes me with a big kiss and cuddle.

She can be nervous and unsure around new people, but with time, patience, and understanding, she’s going to make the most wonderful addition to someone’s home.

Although she needs to be the only dog in the home, she can happily socialise with other dogs and loves going down to the big yard with her friends.

Whimsy has come to us from a breeder and is a very worried girl. When she first arrived, she was very unsettled at the moment and could be quite skittish, finding so many of the sights and sounds of the world quite overwhelming. Once she gets to know you, she will quietly approach you and allow a gentle fuss.

Whimsy needs time to learn and to trust, and needs a calm and quiet home home that understands ex-breeding dogs and will allow her the space she needs to learn about trust at her own pace. She will need a calm, patient, and understanding family who are willing to let her take things slowly and gently as she begins to discover the comforts of home life.

She will need a kind and confident resident dog in her home that she can look to and rely on as she learns about home life and settles in. Having a canine companion to guide her will really help build her confidence and show her that the world can be a safe and happy place.

Whimsy does walk well on a lead, but as she can be a bit skittish, her adopters will need to take the outside world at her own pace, allowing her the time she needs to gain confidence in her surroundings without feeling pressured.

Whimsy seems like she has such a sweet heart, and with time, patience, and kindness, she will begin to show her loving and gentle nature. She just needs someone special to help her learn about trust and companionship and to show her that she is safe and loved.

Whimsy has come to us with an abscess on the right side of her jaw, which is being treated by the vets. Our vets have noted that she has one fractured canine, but no root or nerve exposure and so it is advised to leave it at this time, but will need monitoring by her adopters and their vet. 17-07-26 Davina came to us from a breeder and is now searching for a patient and understanding forever home. We have been told she is a Miniature Doodle (she weighs just under 10kg), but whatever her mix may be, one thing is certain, she's absolutely adorable.

Davina is a very gentle and sensitive little girl who is still finding the world quite overwhelming. She takes a great deal of comfort from the company of other dogs and relies on them for reassurance while she learns that people and new experiences aren't so frightening. Although she is beginning to observe what's going on around her, she is still a very worried girl who needs time to build trust and confidence.

Because of this, Davina is looking for a calm, quiet home with adopters who haveexperience of ex-breeding dogsand understand that confidence cannot be rushed. She will need people who are happy to let her settle entirely at her own pace, allowing her to make progress in her own time without any pressure or expectations.

Davinamust have another kind, confident resident dogin her new home. Having a canine companion is essential for her, providing reassurance, helping her understand home life and giving her the confidence to follow their lead as she discovers the joys of being part of a family.

Having never lived in a home before, everything will be completely new to Davina. She will need help with house training, learning household routines and gradually becoming accustomed to everyday sights and sounds. Lead walking will also be something to build slowly, beginning with gentle introductions in the safety of the garden before venturing further afield when she feels ready.

Due to her nervous nature, Davina is looking for anadult-only homewhere she can enjoy a peaceful, predictable environment while she continues to blossom.

Davina is a sweet little soul who simply needs time, patience and understanding. Watching a frightened ex-breeding dog gradually discover that life can be safe and happy is incredibly rewarding, and we have no doubt that, in the right home, Davina will continue to grow in confidence and become a devoted companion.

Davina has been given the Gift of Life by Ceri Mann

name: Kelly
description:
I would like a calm and quiet home where I can settle in.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I can walk on a lead and harness and love to explore quiet areas.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I have a very overshot jaw, and I have been spayed.

Kelly is a lovely girl who has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. When she first arrived, she was quite worried but she soon started to settle in and come out of her shell. She has since moved to a wonderful foster home where she is settling in well and experiencing home life for the first time.

She will be looking for a calm and quiet home, where she can settle in at her own pace. She would love her adopters to be around most of the time and we would consider homing her with gentle, dog savvy teenagers.

Kelly has taken to home life well andreally enjoys pottering around the garden and laying in the shade. She is also happy to take treats nicely and loves her food too! She is happy to accept a fuss, has a waggy little tail and is learning all about playing with toys too. She gets very excited to see her fosterers when they come downstairs in the morning, which is lovely.

Kelly loves other dogs and will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home to be her friend and help her settle in to her new life.

She had never lived in a home before moving to foster, so her adopters will need to be kind and understanding as she continues to learn all about home life. She is already doing well learning about house training. She has already learned how to walk on a lead and harness and we think she will really enjoy going for walks in quiet areas as she builds up her confidence.

She is a truly wonderful girl and we think that whoever adopts her is going to adore her!

She has arrived with an overshot jaw that does not bother her, but should be monitored in her new home to ensure she is comfortable.

Kelly has been given the Gift of Life by Hannah Wadsworth

Kelly arrived last Sunday and has settled really well in foster.  She enjoys pottering around the garden and lying in the shade - she has her favourite spots.

She has lived happily with our 4 small dogs and has been polite and friendly with all dogs she has met outside the home. She has been on two walks so far - on a longline so she can choose her pace and have a sniff in the shade - and she absolutely loves it.

In just a week she has progressed so well - she takes treats nicely and very gently and loves her food. She is accepting a fuss from us, starting to play with toys, wagging her tail and very pleased to see us when we come downstairs in the mornings.

It is great to see her look so relaxed and happy already. She is going to be a fabulous little addition to any household.

Kelly is a lovely girl who has come to us from a breeder. She would very much like to be your friend, but she is feeling a little worried and lacking in confidence at the moment.

She is still adjusting to her new surroundings and will need time, patience, and understanding to help her settle. We believe that with plenty of reassurance and gentle encouragement, Kelly will soon begin to come out of her shell and show her true personality.

Kelly will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home. Having a canine companion to look up to will help her learn about home life and continue to build her confidence. She can live with older dog-savvy teens who are sensible and allow her to settle in at her own pace.

As she has never lived in a home before, Kelly will need patient adopters who can help her learn all the basics, including house training and walking on a lead. To begin with, she may prefer gentle garden explorations while she gains confidence and gets used to her new environment.

Given the time, love, and support she needs, Kelly is sure to blossom into a wonderful companion. She is looking for a calm and understanding home where she can continue her journey and enjoy plenty of TLC.

name: Holiday
description:
I need a quiet adult-only home where I can feel safe and loved.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I’m frightened and will need a secure garden to learn about being outside.

I am too scared to go out for walks right now and will need a careful introduction.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I have been spayed and am ready for my forever home.

Holiday originally came to us from a breeder. She was adopted and found a lovely home, but sadly it wasn't the right match for her as the resident dog wouldn't accept her, so she came back into our care. Holiday has since moved to a foster home where she is settling beautifully and continuing to learn all about life in a home.

Holiday is a very sensitive girl who had very little socialisation before coming into our care. When she first returned to us, she found people incredibly worrying and was very hand-shy. Her first instinct was always to run away, and she wasn't comfortable being picked up or handled. If she felt pushed beyond her comfort zone, she could react by nipping out of fear, and she did nip her previous adopter once when she became overwhelmed during handling.

Holiday will still be looking for a calm, quiet, adult-only home with no visiting children. She will need adopters who understand the needs of scared ex-breeding dogs and who are happy to let her settle at her own pace, without pressure or expectations. She relies heavily on other dogs for comfort and reassurance and will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help guide her.

Since moving into foster care, Holiday has made some really lovely progress and is growing in confidence every week. She now happily comes into the sitting room and chooses to settle nearby while her foster family relax. She enjoys being part of family life and likes to know where everyone is, often coming to find them and quietly checking in throughout the day.

She is now happily taking treats from our hands and has recently started giving gentle little nose bumps to our hands, which is a wonderful sign that her trust is growing. She also greets us with a wagging tail and will happily sit and listen while we talk to her, maintaining eye contact. When she first arrived, she would run away as soon as anyone spoke to her, so this has been a huge milestone.

Although Holiday is becoming much more confident, she still isn't ready to be handled much and is not yet comfortable wearing a harness or going for walks. Her adopter will need to be happy to continue building her confidence at her own pace, allowing her to decide when she is ready for each new step.

Minus her brief adoption, Holiday had never lived in a home before, but she has settled brilliantly into foster care. She is now 99% clean in the house and has established a lovely routine. She absolutely adores the other dogs, taking great comfort from them and often following their lead. She enjoys spending time in the garden and small secure field, where she loves exploring, relaxing and watching the world go by. She has also been left at home with the other dogs for a few hours and has coped very well.

Holiday is a very special little girl who has already come such a long way. She is learning that people can be kind and that home life isn't so scary after all. She still has a journey ahead of her, but with plenty of patience, understanding and the support of another dog, we hope she will continue to grow in confidence and enjoy everything her new life has to offer.

Holiday has been given the Gift of Life by Ellie Worron

Holiday has made some lovely progress since coming into foster care and is growing in confidence every week. She now happily comes into the sitting room and chooses to settle close by while we relax. She enjoys being part of family life and likes to know where we are, often coming to find us and checking in throughout the day.

She is happily taking treats from our hands and has recently started giving gentle little nose bumps to our hands, which is a wonderful sign that her trust is growing. She also wags her tail when she sees us and will happily listen while we talk to her, maintaining eye contact. When she first arrived, she would run away as soon as we spoke to her, so this is a huge milestone for her.

Holiday is now 99% clean in the house and has settled brilliantly into a routine. She absolutely adores the other dogs and takes great comfort from them, often following their lead. She loves spending time in the garden and our small field, where she enjoys exploring and relaxing.

At the moment, Holiday is not yet ready to wear a harness or go for walks, and she will need an adopter who is happy to continue building her confidence at her own pace. She is making steady progress and, with patience and kindness, continues to blossom.

Holiday is a very gentle, sweet little girl with the softest, kindest eyes. She has such a lovely nature, and it is a privilege to watch her confidence grow a little more each day.

Holiday has settled well into foster care. She is worried about being handled at the moment so we haven’t tried to stroke her or pick her up, we wanted to give her the chance to settle and feel safe first.

She will take treats from our hands, walk through doorways easily, even with us there, and she seeks us out if she doesn’t know where we are. This all indicates that it won’t be long until we can begin gentles strokes etc. When we are fussing our dogs she gets closer to watch and has touched my hand or sniffed my legs. Holiday is not as jumpy as I thought she would be, which is great, and we can walk quite close to her without her moving away.

When we are all settled in the evening, she comes into the sitting room to see where we all are and what we are doing. She isn’t phased by the TV and will often sit on a rug next to my chair.

We have a very small field which most new fosters are a bit scared of as they are not used to big spaces, Holiday loves spending time out there exploring and watching the other dogs play, we’ve even seen her do the odd little sprint!

She has been clean in the house and loves snuggling with the dogs at night in the kitchen, she is left overnight and we can go out for a couple of hours and she is fine as long as the dogs are with her too.

She has the potential to be the best dog and I don’t think it will be long before she is seeking attention and ready to try her harness again. She has very gentle eyes and you can see the sadness ebbing away a little more each day.

This week Holiday has been making lovely progress with lead work. We have been helping her get used to having a lead clipped onto her harness and trailing behind her, and she is becoming much more comfortable with this. Clipping the lead onto her harness is now far less of a concern for her, which is a big step forward, and when she is out in the yard she barely seems aware of it anymore.

She is also doing wonderfully with different people putting her harness on, which is a very significant achievement for Holiday given how sensitive she has been around handling. She is taking these steps in her stride and continues to make really encouraging progress.

Recently, I’ve been spending some dedicated time working with Holiday, and she’s making such lovely progress. She’s beginning to trust me more each day and has even allowed me to gently put a harness on her. Everything is done slowly and at her pace, with plenty of treats and reassurance, but this is a huge milestone for this sensitive girl.

We’ve also been working on gentle touch, always on her terms. When she chooses to come and sit beside me in her bed, we take things one small step at a time, building her confidence with each positive experience (and a few tasty rewards along the way!).

Holiday is starting to show more of her personality now. She’s often one of the first up for a treat and has even begun wagging her tail. It might sound like a small thing, but for Holiday, it’s truly something special.

She’s a wonderful dog who just needs a patient, understanding home where she can continue to grow in confidence and feel safe. Watching her come out of her shell is incredibly rewarding, and she’s so ready for someone to give her the love she deserves.

I am writing this update as someone who has not had much interaction with Holiday although I have worked with her on a few occasions. It is obvious from her previous update that there has been progress in her coming out of her shell and I was surprised to discover that Holiday would accept treats from my hand although when trying to smooth her coat, Holiday swiftly moved out of reach.

She is getting there but slowy and anyone wanting to adopt her will need to go slowly and earn that important trust. Holiday's regular carer can stroke Holiday when she is settled in a bed but only in one place. If a position is changed, Holiday will become scared and move.

It is apparent after speaking with Holiday's regular carer that for Holiday to make that important next step in her progress, it would be better for her to be in a home situation. Holiday is fantastic with other dogs and would definitely need to live with at least one other dog to give her that hope of progress and comfort. There is always someone out there for every dog and vice versa Holiday is waiting.

Holiday originally came to us from a breeder a few months ago. She was adopted and found a lovely home, but sadly it wasn't the right match for her and the resident dog wouldn't accept her, so she is now back in our care.

Holiday is a very scared girl who is very overwhelmed to find herself here and clearly hasn't had much socialisation before. She finds human interaction quite difficult at the moment and is very hand-shy, so she will need a patient and understanding home that can help her come out of her shell at her own pace. Holiday will run away from you when you enter her kennel and isn't keen on being picked up or handled. She finds this so scary, that if she feels like she is being pushed out of her comfort zone she can choose nip or bite, purely through fear. She did bite her previous adopter once when she was being handled as she became so worried.

For this reason, Holiday will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult only home where there are no visiting children. She will need adopters who hav experience with scared ex-breeding dogs and who will let her settle in slowly at her own pace with no pressure or expectations.

Holiday finds comfort and reassurance from the company of her canine friends and so she will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home to take her under their wing. This dog will need to allow her to snuggle up to them and will need to be happy for her to follow them around. A kind resident dog will be an important source of reassurance and companionship for her as she adjusts to her new life.

Although she spent some time in foster and was adopted for a short period, she had never lived in a home before this, so Holiday will still need to learn all about home life and new skills like house training. She will also need to learn to walk on a lead and harness and will need to practice wearing these around the home and garden, once her confidence with handling has grown a little more. She will then need to practice walking around the garden until she is confident enough to venture further.

Since arriving back with us, Holiday has started to make some more progress and will now take a treat from our hands as long as she has a doggy friend next to her for support. With time, love and patience she will start to leave her past behind her and will truly start to blossom. Holiday's journey won't be a short one, but it will be so worth it when you see her tail wag for the first time or when she first willingly accepts some fuss and attention. In the right home, she will thrive, so please don't keep her waiting too long.

name: Royal
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I would like to live with a female dog. No cats please!

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I can walk on a lead and harness and love to explore quiet areas.

I am learning about house training in my foster home, and am doing so good!

I'm fully vaccinated and have been neutered.

Royal is a very special Chow Chow who has come to us from a breeder in search of his forever home. When he first arrived, he was extremely frightened of the world around him and was very wary of being touched or handled. Thanks to gentle care and patience, Royal has made incredible progress and is continuing to blossom in foster, where he is experiencing home life for the very first time.

Royal has exceeded all expectations with how well he has settled into foster. He has been an absolute superstar, sleeping soundly through the night, travelling well in the car, walking beautifully on lead and has even been completely clean in the house. Every day brings a new milestone, and it has been a joy to watch his confidence grow as he discovers all the comforts and pleasures of family life.

Although Royal is still nervous of people initially, he so desperately wants to trust and tries his hardest to be brave. He has begun asking his foster carers for gentle neck and bum scratches, happily takes treats from their hands, enjoys rummaging through the toy box, has found his little voice and now greets them with his wonderful wagging tail. He is such a sweet, gentle soul who simply needs time to work things out at his own pace.

Royal absolutely relies on the resident female dogs in foster for confidence and reassurance. He watches their every move, learning how to be part of a family, and loves playing alongside them. He will need to share his forever home with at least one kind, confident female dog who enjoys a good play and can continue to show him the way. He cannot live with cats.

As this is Royal's first experience of living in a home, he thrives on routine and will need patient, understanding adopters who will allow him to settle without pressure. He has made remarkable progress already, but he is still very nervous of the unknown and benefits from people who understand that he needs time to process new experiences. A calm, rural or quiet home would suit him best, as he is currently worried by traffic. He is looking for an adult-only home with breed experience and experience with very nervous rescue dogs would be highly beneficial.

Royal has recently had a bath and full groom at the rescue and was an absolute gentleman throughout. As a Chow Chow, his beautiful coat will require regular daily grooming. He is very tolerant of being brushed when it is introduced slowly, little and often, and this has become an important part of his routine.

Royal is an incredibly special boy who has embraced this new chapter in his life with quiet bravery. With patience, kindness and the continued support of confident canine companions, he will become a wonderfully loyal and loving companion. Watching him continue to discover the world and grow in confidence will be an incredibly rewarding journey, and he is sure to make his forever family smile every single day.

Wow! This darling boy has just exceeded all expectations with how well he’s settled into his very first home, in his first week. Not a single accident (unheard of for a boy), sleeps soundly over night out of a crate, happy to be left alone with the company of the resident dogs, walks well on a lead, travels well. A literal angel boy.

Royal is the sweetest soul, he doesn’t trust humans easily but he really wants to and tries so hard to be brave.

He relies heavily on our resident girl gang for confidence & reassurance, watching & copying them intently to learn what being a member of a family is all about.

After an initial overwhelming few days for him, every day now brings a new ‘first’ & burst of joy on our part! Asking for a neck / bum scratch, taking a treat from our hand, rummaging in the toy box, playing with the girls, finding his little voice & wagging his amazing tail when we talk to him. He is just loving this next step in life and is so ready to be someone’s special boy.

Royal currently needs an adult only home as has not yet been tested with children. He needs confident kind resident female dogs who like a good play. A rural / quiet location would be preferable as he’s currently quite scared of traffic.

He is still very nervous of the unknown, thrives on routine and needs to be guided and given time to work things out without any pressure so experience with very scared dogs would be helpful.

As a Chow, his beautiful coat will need grooming daily. He is very tolerant of this if done slowly, little & often.

Please get in touch if you feel you might be the right match for this special big guy, he will make you smile every day.

Royal is not a dog I’ve had the chance to work with until recently. I’ve heard a lot about him, as he’s one of our longer stayers. I had heard many great things from other members of staff, including the incredible progress he’s made since joining us!When I did get the chance to work with him, my first impression was “oh my days, you are beautiful!” On first sight, he is one of the most beautiful dogs I’ve ever seen and certainly the most stunning chow I’ve ever seen! How can you look at this handsome boy and not fall in love?!When I actually began working with him, I realised how shy and timid he actually was. Initially, he wouldn’t come to the front of the kennel to see me, he’d hide away in the back. It was evident to me that this boy did not trust me. As I continued to work with him, I was very aware of my actions, to ensure I wasn’t causing any anxiety. I began with treats (who doesn’t love a cheeky bribe?). It slowly worked. Initially, he wanted nothing to do with me. I didn’t want to invade his safe spaces (safe spaces are so important for a more scared or anxious dog. Could you imagine a big scary stranger coming into your home and not leaving? I wouldn’t feel too easy if that occurred to me). So, I’d place the treat and leave the kennel. He’d come out, have a little nosey and take the treat. With time, he began slowly coming out of the back as I entered his kennel. He then began taking treats from my hands and now, whenever I walk onto the section, he comes straight to the gate and waits for me. Honestly, such an incredible feeling making a bond like this with such an incredible boy! There is honestly no feeling like it. They say a dog is a humans best friend but, what no one tells you it works both ways. To build that bond, teach him that I’m not scary, I’m here to help him feel safe, comfortable, happy and to get such a response… it’s honestly the best feeling in the world. Royal needs a home, he needs people to show him this on a day to day basis. We do what we can but, we can’t teach him the safety and comfort of a home, of a family that’s there for him 24/7.Once I got to know this guy a little more, I was taken away. We go out on walks. I feel like this was another bonding experience for us. He loves a walk but, loud noises and interactions with loud people/dogs do freak him out, thus we try to go for quieter walks. He also loves frolicking in the yard. From my experience, he seems to just love being outside!When I worked with him, he didn’t have a friend in his kennel, however, since working with him I have seen him enjoying in the yard with other dogs and is now kennelled with a boxer. He seems very happy. As previously mentioned on his profile, he is to be homed with females around his size or alone. I have not worked with him enough to comment further on his compatibility and amiability with other dogs so, please read the rest of his profile and updates to get a fuller understanding of this incredible boy!At this point, I’ve worked with him enough for him to trust me. He’s happy to see me, he’s fine for me to touch him and fuss him. The Royal I see is a happy dude. He is a scared dog, I’m very aware of that but, the Royal I know now is far different to the Royal I first met. You just have to gain his trust and he’ll let you see him. When you first meet him, he will be shy. He’ll hide and he will not trust you. DO NOT let this deter you. He is one of the sweetest dogs I’ve ever met. From when I first met him to now, I feel like he’s a completely different dog. I was respectful of his boundaries, slow and calm, I did what I could to make him feel comfortable and safe, he then began to trust me and show me his true self (he hides it beneath all that fur). Honestly, I love him. I will take time out of my day to go see him, give him a little treat and some love, just because he is honestly that special. I cannot believe he’s been here over a year. He is one of our most special dogs. I don’t see how anyone can get to know this dog and not love him.Don’t overlook this fluffy dude. Yes, he’s shy and nervous but, the longer you spend with him, care for him and gain his trust, the more you’ll fall in love with him. I can say with confidence; if you put the effort in with Royal, you will fall in love with him.

I absolutely love this boy with my whole heart.

I've been working hard on helping him get used to being brushed because, as a Chow, it's something his future adopters will need to keep up with regularly to keep his coat healthy and prevent mats from developing, especially behind his ears.

Royal is now an absolute angel when it comes to grooming. I brush him every day, and with it being shedding season, no matter how long I brush for, there always seems to be more fur coming out! These days, he simply finds a comfy spot, settles down, and lets me get on with it. If he's had enough, or if I come across a mat that's uncomfortable for him, he communicates so well to let me know he's done for the day.

I also recently decided it was time to give him a bath. I wasn't sure how he'd cope, as it involved picking him up and putting him in the bath, but he was an absolute angel from start to finish. He allowed me to pick him up without any fuss and stood beautifully while I bathed and shampooed him.

I'm so incredibly proud of him. Afterwards, I introduced him to the grooming blower to help remove some of his loose coat. He wasn't a huge fan of it, but he tolerated it for a short while, and I'll continue using it regularly so he can build his confidence with it.

I honestly think all this grooming time has strengthened our bond even more, because lately he seems to be seeking out so much more affection and attention from me. He's such a special boy, and it has been wonderful watching his confidence grow.

Royal has now been with us for over a year, and we’re still waiting for the right person to see just how special he is. He’s had two meet and greets during this time, but sadly neither worked out as he was too nervous meeting new families.

Royal is a sensitive boy who simply needs time, patience, and understanding. He can be unsure at first, but once he begins to trust you, his cheeky, affectionate personality really shines through and it’s such a joy to see.

With a consistent routine, Royal truly thrives. He now enjoys running freely around our large yard without a harness or lead, and when it’s time to go back, he comes straight over. He’s also been out on two longer walks away from the rescue with one of our regular volunteers and has done amazingly well.

All Royal is looking for is someone willing to give him the time and patience he deserves. In return, he’ll become a loyal and loving companion.

I’ve come on leaps and bounds over the past month. I’m still a little shy and can get nervous when I meet new people, but I’m working on it!

I feel most comfortable when I spend quality time with people. It doesn’t take long for me to start feeling at ease (though I still sometimes like my own space). The more time you spend with me, the more comfortable I become—and treats help too! I’ll return your love in equal measure, as long as I’m given the right time, support, and respect.

I love going out for walks, though I can get nervous around loud noises or sudden movements. They might make me jump or feel uneasy, but a bit of love and reassurance always helps!

I feel more comfortable every day. I benefit not only from interaction with my humans, but also from the company of my kennel friends that I live with.

Another month has gone by, and my cheeky boy Royal is still waiting in kennels. I honestly don’t know why this handsome lad isn’t getting much interest. Not only is he completely unique-looking, but he also has the funniest, quirkiest personality. If you want a dog who’ll make you laugh every single day here he is!

Royal is 99% kennel clean and always keeps his bedding tidy… well, until I make his bed perfectly for him. Then he likes to “show me how it’s supposed to be done” by pulling it all across the floor. He walks beautifully on the lead now; he can still get a little spooked from time to time, but he’s made massive progress since the day he arrived.

He loves his toys he just doesn’t love sharing them! He’s also a bit selective with kennel mates, so his ideal home would include a calm, placid large female dog who won’t make too much fuss over him.

Royal truly is an amazing boy, inside and out, and I hope he doesn’t have to wait much longer for the forever home he deserves.

Royal never fails to make us smile with his crazy, funny, and quirky personality. He’s got such a cheeky side to him just waiting for the right people to help it shine.

On the lead, Royal is already walking beautifully, though he can still get a little nervous at times. His new family will need to be patient and willing to help him build confidence. Loud noises or sudden movements can overwhelm him, so he’ll do best with calm, quiet walks to start.

This week Royal had his very first trip down to the big yard! He loved it, though he found his confidence by sticking close to his doggy friend. With more practice, we’re sure he’ll begin to explore on his own.

Royal absolutely adores other dogs. Once he’s settled in, he loves to play, so he’ll need a kind and confident resident dog to show him the ropes, give him reassurance, and of course, enjoy plenty of playtime together.

He’s such a handsome boy with so much love to give we can’t believe he hasn’t found his forever home yet!

This past month has been a huge step forward for our boy Royal! Once a little unsure of the world, Royal is now walking beautifully on lead, it’s such a massive step for him considering how nervous he once was!

Royal currently shares his kennel with both a male and a female dog and he’s proving to be a respectful and easy companion. He enjoys their company, often watching what they do and following their lead. Royal will definitely need another resident dog around his size in his home, so he can continue to have the doggy companionship to help him continue to grow in confidence.

Despite his progress, Royal is still a sensitive soul, and it takes a little time for him to warm up to you. Royals forever family will need to give him time and patience to come out of his shell, so for this reason I believe Royal would be best suited to a home with no children.

Please don’t leave Royal waiting much longer for his forever home, he really deserves a cosy sofa to curl up on!

I’m so proud of Royal, this boy has come on tremendously since arriving at Many Tears. From arriving a terrified dog and very unsure of us humans, he has now slowly but surely begun to trust us and realise we are not so bad, especially when we arrive with cheesy treats.

Royal loves food, toys and being outside in our yards. He has just began harness training, ready to begin lead walking. At the moment he is not so keen on lead walking but he has taken a few tentative steps and with the help of some squeezy cheese and possibly a confident doggie friend to follow I think it won’t be long before he can begin to enjoy exploring the world.

Royals adopters will need to understand he is still very wary and unsure of his environment and he is going to need plenty of time, love and patience to trust his humans, but in the right home and given time I think this boy is going to be a big, playful and lovable boy. Royal will need a home where there is already a resident dog.

Royal is a very scared boy who has come to us from a breeder. He is especially scared when it comes to being touched by us humans but when you get him in the back of the kennel he will allow you to gently stroke him but he is uncomfortable with this. At the moment Royal could possibly make the wrong decision if handled incorrectly but this is purely through fear and he is already starting to make improvements. He will actually get excited to see his kennel mum in the mornings and will wag his tail but he’s not sure how to interact with her yet.

Royal has never lived in a home so this is going to be completely overwhelming at first and he will definitely need at least one other dog in the home to help his confidence. This will help him with house training and lead walking but these are things that are going to take him time to learn as the garden may be as scary as the home at first.

Royal will need a very calm and quiet, adult only home and adopters who have lots of experience with scared dogs. We think he’ll come out of his shell a lot more over time but Royal needs a lot of TLC, time and patience.

name: Enfys
description:
I can live with older children, aged 16+, who understand I need time to settle in.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in.

I am new to lead walking, and would like to continue this once I have settled in.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

06-08-26 Enfys is a very nervous girl who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. She has a gentle, sensitive nature and will shy away from us, all whilst wagging her tail. Although she is understandably worried, Enfys is happy to accept a gentle fuss and allows herself to be handled. Once we leave the kennel, her excitement starts to show and she becomes much more animated, giving us little glimpses of the happy girl she has the potential to become.

Enfys gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends and relies on their company for comfort, so she will need a kind resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in and finds her paws. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who are sensible and will allow her time to settle in.

As Enfys has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to be patient and understanding as she adjusts to a completely new way of living. Enfys is new to lead walking, but she would like to continue this training in her new home once she is settled.

Enfys is a lovely girl who is already showing us little flashes of her personality. With time, patience, and the support of a friendly resident dog, we hope she will continue to grow in confidence and enjoy the happy future she deserves.

Enfys has arrived overweight, so she will need a good diet and gentle exercise to help her reach and maintain a healthy weight. This will need to be continued in her new home. She also has a Grade 1 patella luxation in her right hind leg, although this may continue to improve with gentle exercise as she builds muscle.

Enfys is also being treated for a skin rash and has some areas of alopecia. Our veterinary team will continue to monitor her progress and ensure she receives any care she needs.

Enfys has been given the Gift of Life by Ruth Butterworth

name: Molly
description:
I can live with dog-savvy teens, and would love an active home!

I can be an only dog or live with other dogs. I have never met cats.

I would love a garden to run and play in!

I would love plenty of adventures once I am fully vaccinated!

I am just a puppy! Please be patient with me while I learn the basics!

My adopter will need to agree to have me spayed when I'm old enough.

01-08-26 Molly is an amazing puppy who has come to us with her siblings following an accidental litter. She is a happy, confident girl who is full of fun and has a wonderful zest for life.Mollyis already a big girl for her age, and we believe she is a Cane Corso Cross, so her adopters will need to be prepared for her to grow into a large adult dog.

Mollyis a friendly and affectionate pup who is looking for a loving home where she can continue to learn and explore the world. She has started learning about walking on a harness, and would like to continue this, out and about, once she is fully vaccinated and settled into her new home, she will love getting out and about on plenty of adventures with her family.

Mollycould live with older, dog-savvy children, aged 13+ who understand that she is a large, boisterous puppy and will need help learning her manners as she grows. She could happily live with another friendly dog who doesn't mind sharing their home with a playful youngster, or she could be an only dog, providing her new family have plenty of time to dedicate to her training, socialisation, and exercise.

As with all puppies,Mollywill need continued guidance with house training, lead walking, and all the basics of family life. Her adopters must be committed to taking her to puppy socialisation and training classes to help her develop into a confident, well-mannered adult and agree to have her spayed when she is of age.

Mollyis a truly lovely girl with so much potential. She is looking for a family who will give her the love, time, and commitment she deserves, and in return she is sure to become a wonderful and loyal companion.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Clippa
description:
I’d like an active home home filled with love and kindness!

I can be an only dog or live with others. No cats or small furries please!

I would love a secure garden with 6ft+ fences that I can run and play in!

I walk on a lead but need some training as I'm strong and can pull.

I did have some separation anxiety which my fosterers have worked on.

I have been spayed! Please read below for more information.

Clippa is a wonderful girl who came to us from a breeder in search of a fresh start. From the moment she arrived, she showed us what a loving and affectionate little girl she is. Whilst in our care at the rescue, Clippa quickly became a favourite with staff and volunteers thanks to her happy nature and love of human attention. She adored going out on walks with volunteers, loved exploring the Welsh countryside and was always happiest when she was close to people getting cuddles and fuss. She also got on brilliantly with her kennel friends and enjoyed the company of other dogs.

She has now moved to a foster home where she has continued to blossom and has settled beautifully into home life. On arrival, she immediately made it her mission to explore every single inch of the garden, showing just how adventurous and inquisitive she is! Because of this, she will need a very secure garden with minimum 6ft fencing as she is an active little spaniel who loves to investigate everything around her.

We think that Clippa is a bit hard of hearing and doesn't hear human voices easily. This doesn't slow her down, but, for this reason future adopters will need to be aware that she will likely need to be on lead for her walks and be let off only in secure fields to keep her safe.

Clippa is an incredibly affectionate and people orientated dog who absolutely adores human company. Visitors are instantly greeted by Clippa demanding cuddles, belly rubs and attention, and she will happily snuggle into you whenever given the opportunity. Although she enjoys playing with polite dogs and gets on wonderfully with the resident dogs in foster, people will always be her favourite. When first in foster she did experience some separation anxiety, her fosterers have already worked hard on building her confidence and independence, and her future adopters will need to continue this, gradually building up the time she is left.

She has taken to home life brilliantly and despite having never lived in a home before, she has been clean around the house, with no accidents indoors. She settles beautifully overnight and loves curling up somewhere warm and cosy with her foster family. In fact, she gets so comfortable at bedtime that convincing her to go outside for her final toilet trip can sometimes be a challenge!

Clippa absolutely LOVES her walks and thrives on getting out and exploring the world around her. She would love an active home that understands the busy, intelligent and inquisitive nature of spaniels and can provide her with plenty of mental and physical stimulation. She already walks well on lead most of the time, although she can sometimes be strong and excitable when out and about. At the moment, her recall is non-existent in secure fields as she is far too busy exploring to pay attention, so her adopters will need to be committed to continuing her training with this.

She could happily be homed as an only dog as long as her adopters were around most of the time and had plenty of time to spend with her, but she could also be homed with another kind and playful resident dog. She could live with gentle dog savvy teenagers but cannot live with cats or small furries.

Clippa arrived in our care with bilateral conjunctivitis which responded very well to treatment and continues to be monitored. She also had one tooth removed at the time of her spay.

Clippa is such a happy, loving and affectionate little girl who has embraced her new life with enthusiasm. Whether she is out exploring, making new friends, or snuggled up for cuddles, she throws herself wholeheartedly into everything she does. We think she will make an absolutely wonderful companion for a very lucky family.

Clippa has been given the Gift of Life by Carol Unsworth

Clippa is the friendliest girl that we have ever fostered. All she wants to do is be with you for cuddles. She has been clean in the house from day 1 and sleeps soundly all night in her bed in our bedroom (although she does like to see if you are awake at 5:30am in case you can give her early breakfast!) She also gets super excited for her bedtime snack routine.Despite her age, Clippa still has quite a lot of pep in her step and LOVES going on long walks and exploring the local countryside, woods and beaches that we have local to us. She is also a huge tennis ball fan! Although Clippa isn't particularly strong, she is very 'busy' so will need someone that can handle her to let her 'Spaniel' to her full potential.Clippa gets on really well with our 2 dogs and likes to snuggle with our Labrador but we also think that she could be an only dog for someone that is around most of the time and willing to build up being left gradually.We think that Clippa is a bit hard of hearing and doesn't hear human voices easily. For this reason future adopters will need to be aware that she will likely need to be on lead for her walks and be let off only in secure fields.Clippas perfect adopters would be someone who is home most of the time, loves snuggly dogs and going for long walks. Some experience of gundog breeds would be useful.

Clippa has now moved into foster and is settling in brilliantly! On arrival, she made it her mission to explore every inch of the garden, so she will definitely need a very secure garden with a minimum of 6ft fencing as she is an adventurous and inquisitive girl.

She has settled beautifully into home life and gets on really well with the resident dogs, although her true preference is definitely humans! Every visitor is instantly greeted by Clippa demanding cuddles, belly rubs and attention. She is such a happy, affectionate little girl who absolutely adores people.

Clippa LOVES her walks and exploring the world around her. She would thrive in an active home that understands the busy, inquisitive nature of spaniels and can keep both her mind and body stimulated. She enjoys playing with polite dogs too, but people will always be her favourite.

At the moment, Clippa has zero recall in secure fields and is far too busy exploring to pay any attention to you! She will need lots of training and practice with this before potentially being allowed off lead and her adopters must be prepared to put the work in.

She has met older children calmly and could be homed with kind and gentle, dog savvy teenagers. She has taken everything in her stride. Around the home she is very clean, has never had a single accident indoors, and settles beautifully overnight sleeping upstairs in the bedroom. In fact, she gets so cosy at bedtime that getting her outside for her final toilet trip can be a challenge and her Foster Dad often has to carry her out because she doesn’t want to leave her warm snuggle spot!

Meal times can sometimes be entertaining as Clippa tends to take a bite, wander off to investigate something else, then come back for another bite as there is always something more exciting to check out! Her absolute favourite things in life are walkies, cheese, and snuggling up with Foster Daddy.

Since arriving in foster, Clippa has decided she loves people so much that she finds being away from them difficult, even for 30 seconds. Her fosterers are already working on her separation anxiety with her and gradually increasing the time she is left, but any future adopters will need to continue working with her and making this a priority with patience, consistency and understanding.

Clippa is an absolute angel girl. She is lovely and affectionate and will snuggle right in for cuddles. Clippa also loves going on long walks and meeting new people.

This week Clippa has been enjoying the sunshine at the rescue, and has been out on some super walks with our lovely volunteers and having plenty of sniff time in our play yards.

Clippa would love a home where she will be able to join in on all the family adventures and have plenty of cuddles.

Clippa is an absolutely lovely Springer Spaniel who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. She is a very affectionate girl who loves human company and will happily snuggle right into you for a cuddle.

Clippa gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends and enjoys their company, so would be happy to share her home with another kind resident dog. She is also confident enough that we would consider homing her as an only dog in the right circumstances, as long as her adopters were around most of the time. She couldn't be homed with cats or small furries. We would consider homing her with dog savvy teenagers.

As Clippa has never lived in a home before, she will need support with house training and learning the basics of home life. With her friendly and affectionate nature, she is likely to enjoy this learning process with her new family.

Clippa can already walk on a lead and enjoys getting out and about, though she can be a little strong at times and can pull, so she will benefit from ongoing guidance and gentle training to help her with her lead manners. She would love to find an active home where she can go on lots of walks and adventures!

Clippa arrived with bilateral conjunctivitis which is already looking much better following veterinary care and will continue to be monitored. She has had 1 tooth removed at the time of her spay.

Clippa is a loving, affectionate girl who clearly enjoys being close to people and other dogs and we think that she will make a wonderful companion!

name: Unity
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I haven't tried walks just yet and will find this a bit overwhelming at the moment.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I will be spayed before finding my forever home.

19-07-26 Unity has come to us from a breeder to find the loving forever home she deserves. She is a very frightened little girl who is finding all the recent changes in her life overwhelming. Everything around her is new and unfamiliar, so she will need patient, understanding adopters who can help her discover that the world isn't such a scary place.

Unity is looking for a calm, quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience of scared ex-breeding dogs and understand the time, patience and commitment they need. She will thrive with a family who are happy to let her settle at her own pace, allowing her confidence to grow naturally without putting her under pressure.

She finds great comfort in the company of other dogs and will need to live with at least one other kind and confident resident dog who can show her the ropes and help her feel safe. A canine companion will play a vital role in helping Unity gain confidence as she adjusts to her new life.

Unity has never experienced life in a home before, so she will need gentle guidance as she learns about home life and new skills like house training. She has not yet learnt to walk on a lead or harness and will need to practice first around the home and garden until she is feeling brave enough to venture further.

Unity is a gentle, sensitive girl who has so much potential. With a loving, experienced family, a confident canine friend by her side and all the time she needs to settle, we are sure she will gradually blossom into the wonderful companion she was always meant to be.

Unity has been given the Gift of Life by Judie Fisher

name: Crispin
description:
I would like a calm and quiet home where I can settle in.

I could live with other dogs, or be the only dog. I don't mind. I don't mind cats!

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I walk well on a lead and love being out and about!

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

Crispin originally came to us from a breeder last October. He was adopted for a few months but has come back into our care after his adopters sadly realised they were not the right match for him. Although they gave him every opportunity to settle, Crispin remained very worried whenever the male in the household was home and simply couldn't relax in his company.

Since returning to us, Crispin has moved to a foster home and has settled in beautifully. He is an incredibly loving, cuddly little boy who simply wants to be close to his people and enjoy all the love and affection he has missed out on. While he is still worried by some men due to his past experiences, once he trusts you his affectionate nature really shines through. Crispin lives alongside two cats in his foster home and he is not bothered by their presence.

Crispin will be best suited to adopters who understand the needs of scared ex-breeding dogs and who will give him all the time he needs to settle at his own pace. He gets on wonderfully with the other dogs in his foster home and sleeps happily alongside them through the night. Although he enjoys their company, his foster carer feels he could also be very happy as an only dog, where he can soak up all the cuddles and attention he so craves. In the right home, with owners who are around enough to reassure him and who have experience with ex-breeding dogs, he would thrive.

One thing Crispin has discovered is just how much he loves going for walks! He gets wonderfully excited when it's time to head out, twirling around and eagerly waiting by the front door. He now walks beautifully on both a lead and harness, is very sociable with other dogs he meets, enjoys exploring new places, and travels well in the car. Walking has become one of his favourite activities and is a lovely way to watch his confidence shine through.

As Crispin has now experienced life in a home, he has become familiar with many of the sights and sounds of everyday living. He has settled quickly into his foster home's routine and sleeps soundly through the night. He has had the occasional wee indoors first thing in the morning, but this has already improved over the last few days as he has established a routine. His adopters should still be prepared to continue his house training with patience, consistency, and plenty of encouragement.

Crispin has also shown that he forms incredibly strong bonds with his favourite person. He loves to be close by and wants to be involved in everything they are doing. Because of this, he showed signs of separation anxiety in his previous home when left for more than a couple of hours. His ideal home would therefore be one where someone is around for most of the day, and where any time left alone can be built up very gradually, helping him feel safe and secure.

Crispin has a cataract in his right eye and is developing a cataract in his left eye. Despite this, he gets around brilliantly, and you would hardly know he has any issues with his eyesight. He has also had all of his teeth removed, so he will need to remain on a soft diet for the rest of his life. He has Grade 2 patella luxation in both hind legs, although this may continue to improve with gentle exercise as he builds muscle.

Crispin really is a special little boy who has had a difficult start in life but has so much love to give. He is looking for a very special family who will understand his worries, cherish the affectionate little dog he has become, and give him the love and security he so deserves. In return, they will gain the most devoted and loving companion.

Crispin has a travel document, which says he is 7 years old, but we do feel he could be a little older than this.

Crispin has been given the Gift of Life by Katrina Pirner

Crispin recently moved foster homes through no fault of his own. He is a gorgeous, well mannered, cuddly boy who loves his walks, his humans and his food.

He gets along with the cats and dogs in my home, though initially Crispin demanded all the attention and would push the other dogs out of the way to get his cuddles first but with careful handling this has improved over the week.

He loves to cuddle up on my bed with my own dogs and sleeps all night there. He lives for his walks and gets very excited when his lead/harness appear. He can walk on his own or with another dog for company.

He happily shares his food bowl with his foster friend Lemon Pie. Even the cats dig in with him sometimes. He is getting used to being left when I go shopping and I am extending these trips so he gets used to being without humans for a while. Crispin does bark initially when visitors come into my home but this soon subsides when he realises they will do him no harm. Keep up the good work Crispin, you've got this my boy

Crispin has been back in foster care for a week and has settled in beautifully. He is an incredibly loving, cuddly little boy who simply wants to be loved. Sadly, he was returned because he became anxious and barked whenever the man in the household moved around.

He walks beautifully on a lead and harness, sleeps soundly through the night alongside the other foster dog, and travels well. Although he is perfectly happy living with other dogs, he could also be an only dog so he can enjoy all the cuddles and affection he deserves. He has had a few little accidents indoors first thing in the morning, but over the last few days he has settled into a much better routine.

Crispin has no teeth, so he will need to remain on a soft diet for the rest of his life. He also has a cataract in one eye and the beginnings of a cataract in the other, but you would hardly know he has any sight issues as he gets around so well.

He really is a very special little boy who simply needs a loving home where he can feel safe, secure, and cherished.
