It is clear that he had very little socialisation in the past, and although he has made lovely progress since living in a home, he still needs patient adopters who understand that building trust takes time. He can be touch-sensitive when he is feeling anxious, so gentle handling and allowing him to approach in his own time will help him continue to gain confidence.Crispin will be best suited to adopters who understand the needs of scared ex-breeding dogs and who will give him all the time he needs to settle at his own pace. He would be happy to share his home with another kind and confident resident dog in his new home. However, in the right home, with owners who are around enough to reassure him and who have experience with ex-breeding dogs, he could also be the only dog in the home.One thing Crispin has discovered is just how much he loves going for walks! He gets wonderfully excited when it's time to head out, twirling around and eagerly waiting by the front door. He has Grade 2 patella luxation in both hind legs, although this may continue to improve with gentle exercise as he builds muscle.Crispin is a gentle soul who has had a difficult start in life, but he has already shown that, with kindness and patience, he is capable of making wonderful progress. He is looking for a very special person who will understand his worries, celebrate his achievements, and enjoy watching him continue to blossom into the loyal and loving companion we know he can be.Crispin has a travel document, which says he is 7 years old, but we do feel he could be a little older than this.

name: Berry
description:
I need a quiet, adult only home that understands ex-breeders.

I need to be the only dog in the home, and cannot live with cats!

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I walk well on a lead but I can be frightened, so I will need to take it slow.

I have lived in a home for a short period and may already know the bascis.

I am being treated for dermatitis around my paws.

02-07-26 Berry originally came to us from a breeder in 2022 and was adopted into a home, but she has unfortunately been returned as she was still struggling to live with the resident dog. While she socialises well with other dogs when out and about, she is looking for a home where she can be the only dog, as she has shown resource guarding behaviours around high-value items such as food and treats within the home.

When Berry arrived back here, she was a very worried little girl who preferred to keep her distance. Since then, Berry has made some lovely progress. Although she can still be a little nervous in new situations and with unfamiliar people, she has grown so much in confidence with the people she knows. She now actively seeks out fuss from her handler and, if they stop, she'll gently paw at them and even have a little cry to ask for more attention.

In her previous home, Berry displayed resource guarding behaviours around both dogs and people. Around people, this can be managed by giving her a little space and swapping the item for something of higher value, rather than trying to take it away. Her guarding comes from insecurity and likely reflects a life where she never truly had anything of her own. Because of this, Berry is looking for an adult-only home with adopters who understand resource guarding, have ex-breeder experience and are committed to using kind, positive management techniques.

We have been told that Berry is clean in the home, although she may need a few reminders while settling into a new routine. She walks nicely on the lead and doesn't pull, although she can be timid and easily startled, so she will benefit from gentle encouragement as she continues to gain confidence in the world around her.

Despite her worries, Berry has so much love to give. She is simply looking for a calm, patient home where she can finally feel safe, build trusting relationships, and enjoy life at her own pace. With understanding, consistency, and plenty of kindness, Berry will blossom into a wonderfully loyal and loving companion.

Berry is currently being treated for some dermatitis around her paw area.

name: Uma
description:
I could live with older, dog-savvy children who respect my space.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in.

I walk on a harness and would enjoy a daily walk when settled in to my new home.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I have been spayed & am ready for my forever home!

18-07-26 Uma is a gorgeous girl who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. She can be a little shy when you first meet her, but it doesn't take long before her playful side begins to appear. After a few minutes, she'll often invite you to play with a sweet little play bow. Uma enjoys gentle handling and is happy to take treats from our hands, although she does appreciate people taking things slowly when picking her up. Her favourite thing is to sit right next to you for fusses

Uma loses confidence when she is away from her doggy friends, so she will need another kind and confident resident dog in the home to help her feel safe and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in. She has a lovely fun personality that's just waiting to come out. We would consider homing her with gentle, dog savvy teenagers.

As Uma has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, practice her skills walking, and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to be patient while she adjusts to her new surroundings and discovers everything that home life has to offer.

Uma has arrived slightly overweight, so she will need a good diet and gentle exercise to help her reach and maintain a healthy weight. This will need to be continued in her new home.

Uma is a real sweetheart with so much potential. She's already showing us glimpses of the happy, playful dog she is, and with the support of another dog and a patient family, we hope her confidence will continue to grow.

Uma has been given the Gift of Life by Anne Davies

name: Derby
description:
I would like a home filled with love and kindness!

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have had 22 teeth extracted and will need some mammary lumps removed.

29-07-26 Please meet Derby. She has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for a loving forever home where she can begin to enjoy the life she has always deserved.

Derby is a shy little girl with the most gentle nature. Although she can be a little unsure at first, she will quietly come over to say hello and is easy to handle. She has a lovely, sweet temperament and is already showing that, with a little patience and reassurance, she is keen to learn that people can be kind.

Derby is looking for a calm and quiet home where she can settle in at her own pace. She will need patient adopters who understand that she has never experienced life in a home before and will need time to adjust to all the new sights, sounds and routines that come with family life.

A kind and confident resident dog will be essential for Derby, as she will take comfort from having a canine friend to help guide her and build her confidence. She could also live with sensible, dog-savvy older teenagers aged 16 years and over who will give her the space and understanding she needs while she settles.

Derby has never lived in a home before, so she will need help with house training and learning all about home life. She will also need to learn to walk on a lead and harness and will need to practice around the home and garden before venturing further.

Derby is a truly lovely little girl and with love and TLC, we think she will truly blossom.

She has had a dental and had 22 teeth removed, so will need a soft food diet moving forwards. She has an undershot jaw, but this doesn't bother her. Our vets have noted that she has a few mammary lumps, which will be removed.

Derby has been given the Gift of Life by Faith Harrison

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Lemon Pie
description:
I would like a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I don't mind cats!

I would like a secure garden to spend time in as I get comfortable in my new home.

I am too scared to go out for walks right now and will need gentle introduction.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I have been spayed and my right eye has been removed.

Lemon Pie is an absolute heartbreaker who came to us from a breeder and initially found it difficult to settle into her new environment. We believe this was partly due to discomfort in her right eye, which has since been removed. She has recovered well from her surgery and already seems much more comfortable. She has corneal scarring on her left eye that will need to be monitored for any future issues that may arise, but she is able to see around it well for now.

Lemon Pie has now moved to a foster home and is making lovely, gentle progress. She arrived as a very scared little girl who adored the company of the other dogs but didn't want to be close to people. She would spend much of her day in the garden or the kitchen, quietly watching her foster carer from a distance. With time, patience, and understanding, she has already started to show just how brave she can be. She is now happy to stay in the same room as her foster carer and no longer feels the need to run away whenever someone moves nearby. She will accept gentle strokes in the night when in her fosterers bed, but isn't ready for this in the daytime yet. Lemon Pie lives alongside two cats in her foster home and she is not bothered by their presence.

Lemon Pie can still be sensitive to touch and may shy away from hands, suggesting that she may not always have been treated with the kindness she deserves. She needs adopters who will allow her to build trust at her own pace and never rush or overwhelm her. Every small step she takes is a huge achievement, and she continues to grow in confidence each day.

Having never lived in a home before moving to foster, Lemon Pie will need understanding adopters who can guide her through all the new experiences and routines of family life. At the moment, harness and lead walking are still a little way off, and her foster carers are allowing her to progress entirely at her own pace. She absolutely loves pottering around the secure garden, where she feels safe and can explore without pressure. As her confidence continues to grow, we are sure she will be ready to take on new adventures in time.

Lemon Pie absolutely adores other dogs and takes enormous comfort from their company. She loves sharing her food bowl and curling up to sleep alongside her doggy friends, so having at least one kind and confident resident dog in her forever home is essential. They will provide her with the reassurance and confidence she needs as she continues to blossom. She could live with older, dog-savvy teenagers who will respect her space and understand that she needs time to settle.

Lemon Pie is an incredibly deserving little girl who has already shown how much progress she can make when given patience and understanding. She is looking for a calm, loving home where she can continue to build trust at her own pace and finally enjoy the happy life she has always deserved.

Lemon Pie has been given the Gift of Life by Sarah Hicklin

Lemon Pie has been so brave this week. While she still remains hand shy, she will accept gentle fusses and strokes in the darkness of the night while she sleeps on my bed.

She loves her canine companions and lives alongside my 2 cats here. Lemon Pie is an inoffensive little girl who needs to suss out this home life from the safety of her bed. She loves to snooze outside in the garden and potter around with my dogs and her foster friend Crispin. Lead walking is a long way off at the moment.

She will be looking for her first forever home with experienced adopters who will let her develop at her own pace.

Lemon Pie has been in foster for a week now. She arrived as a scared little girl who loves all the dogs but didn't want to be in my company and would spend her days in the garden or kitchen, watching me from a distance.

Over the week she has started to show how brave she can be with time and patience and we have progressed to her being in the same room and not running into the garden when I move. She loves to share her food bowl and sleep curled up with a doggy pal, so this is very important in her forever home. Harness and lead walking are a way off yet but she loves mooching in the garden.

With time, as she builds trust, these things will come but for now we are taking things at her pace as to not overwhelm her.

Lemon Pie is an absolute heartbreaker who came to us from a breeder and initially found it difficult to settle into her new environment. We believe this was partly due to discomfort in her right eye, which has since been removed. She is recovering well and already seems much more comfortable. She has corneal scarring on her left eye that will need to be monitored for any future issues that may arise, but she is able to see around it for now.Lemon Pie can be a little sensitive to touch and may shy away from hands, suggesting that she may not always have been treated with the kindness she deserves. However, once she is gently picked up and held, she settles nicely and simply needs plenty of love, patience, and reassurance to help her learn to trust.Having never lived in a home before, Lemon Pie will need understanding adopters who can guide her through all the new experiences and routines of family life. She may initially be too nervous for lead walks, so spending time exploring a secure garden at her own pace would be a great way to help her build confidence as she adjusts to her new surroundings.Lemon Pie will need at least one kind, confident resident dog in her new home to help show her the way and provide reassurance as she settles in. She could live with older, dog-savvy teenagers who will respect her space and offer her the patience and understanding she needs.She is an incredibly deserving little girl who simply needs time, kindness, and patience to blossom into the happy companion she was always meant to be.Lemon Pie has a travel document.

name: Pushkin
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult-only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I am learning to walk on a harness, and would like to continue this in my home!

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

Pushkin has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for a loving forever home. She can be nervous when meeting new people and situations, but her confidence has grown so much during her time with us. She simply needs a little time to warm up and figure people out, and once she feels comfortable her wonderful personality starts to shine through.

Pushkin is a truly lovely girl with a fun, quirky nature and a very affectionate side. She has become a firm favourite with the staff who know her, and once she trusts you she is incredibly rewarding to spend time with. She loves being around people she knows and has a gentle, sweet temperament that is impossible not to fall in love with.

Pushkin takes a great deal of comfort from the company of other dogs and becomes worried and stressed when left on her own. Because of this, she will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home to take her under their wing and help guide her through life. She gets along beautifully with other dogs and has happily shared kennels and enjoyed play dates with a variety of canine companions. She is respectful around toys and eats well alongside other dogs, making her an easy companion to have around.

She is now walking on a harness and has made lovely progress, although some things can still make her nervous when out and about. Her adopters will need to be patient and reassuring, helping her to feel safe and encouraging her when she encounters new experiences. She gains confidence from having another dog alongside her and would benefit from a calm canine friend to help her navigate the world.

Pushkin has never experienced life in a home before, so her new family will need to be kind, patient and understanding as she learns all about home life. She will need help with house training and learning the everyday routines that most pet dogs take for granted. She enjoys treats, so positive reinforcement will be a wonderful way to help her learn and build confidence. She will need an adult-only home with adopters who have experience of ex-breeding dogs and who will allow her to settle in at her own pace. She will also need a secure garden with fencing of at least 6ft to ensure her safety while she adjusts to her new home.

Pushkin is a special little lady who has so much love to give. With plenty of patience, reassurance and the support of a canine friend, she will continue to blossom into a wonderful companion. She has brought so much joy to those caring for her, and we know that the lucky family who adopts her will absolutely adore her.

Pushkin has been given the Gift of Life by Cherry Lewis

This beautiful lady brightens up my days, and as this has been a difficult week for me personally, she has been there to put a smile on my face through it.She can be nervous when you meet her initially but her confidence has grown so much she just needs time to warm up to you and figure you out, but once she's comfortable and her personality comes out she's just so much fun, and so loving. She has such a quirky personality and I absolutely adore her.Pushkin does walk on a harness, although some things do make her nervous still when out on a walk so adopters will need to be aware of this and let her know she is safe as well as some encouragement.Pushkin gets along with pretty much all dogs, any dog she has been kennelled with or introduced to for a play date she has always been so good, is fine with toys around and also eats well around the other dogs.She has never lived in a home before so her new family will have to show her the ropes and help her with her house training, be encouraging and use positive reinforcement, she does enjoy treats so they should be a big help.I'm not lying when I say I genuinely get excited to see her everyday I'm at work, she really is a little ray of sunshine.

Pushkin has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for a loving forever home. She is initially quite nervous and unsure, but once you spend some time with her she starts to come out of her shell and even begins to enjoy a fuss.

Pushkin is a sweet girl who simply needs understanding and the chance to build her confidence at her own pace. She will be looking for a calm and quiet home where she can settle in gradually and continue to blossom. She takes a great deal of comfort from the company of other dogs and becomes quite worried and stressed when left on her own. Because of this, she will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home to take her under their wing and show her that the world isn't such a frightening place.

Pushkin has never experienced life in a home before, so her new family will need to be kind, patient and understanding as she learns all about home life and new skills such as house training. She has made lovely progress with her harness training and is now walking on a harness, although she is still a little nervous when out and about. She is much more confident when she has another dog alongside her, so having a calm canine companion to help reassure her on walks will be a real benefit. She will need an adult-only home with adopters who have experience of ex-breeding dogs and who will allow her to settle in at her own pace. She will also need a secure garden with fencing of at least 6ft to ensure her safety while she adjusts to her new home.

With plenty of love, reassurance and the support of a canine friend, Pushkin will continue to grow in confidence and become a wonderful companion. She is a lovely girl with so much potential, and we can't wait to see her enjoying the happy life she truly deserves.

name: Disco
description:
I could live with older, dog-savvy children who respect my space

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in.

I've been introduced to a harness but I'm not ready for lead walking yet.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

17-07-26 Disco is a sweet girl who has come into our care from a breeder. She really enjoys the company of other dogs and loves playing with her kennel friends and takes a lot of comfort from being around them. Disco is easy to handle and will happily approach us, although she is still a little timid while she gets to know people. Although she looks very Maltese she is a bigger girl at 9.2kg.

She will be looking for a calm and quiet home, where she can settle in at her own pace and learn all about life as a cherished family member. We would consider homing her with gentle, dog savvy teenagers.

Disco gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends and relies on their company for comfort, so she will need a kind resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in and finds her paws.

As Disco has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, walking on a lead and harness, and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to be patient and allow her to settle at her own pace.

Disco is a gentle little girl with a playful side that shines through when she's with her doggy friends. With a patient family and a kind canine companion, we hope she will continue to grow in confidence and enjoy everything her new life has to offer.

Disco has received treatment for conjunctivitis and has had one tooth extracted at the time of her spay. She has had a cyst drained from the top of her head, which our vets will continue to monitor. She also came to us with a fluid-filled swelling on the side of her neck/chest area, which our vets diagnosed as a sialocele. This occurs when a salivary gland becomes damaged, allowing saliva to leak into the surrounding tissue, where it collects and forms a soft, usually painless, pocket of fluid. Our vets have drained this, however, it is likely to gradually refill over the coming weeks or months and would need to be drained again if this happens. The only permanent treatment is surgery to remove the affected salivary gland, which would need to be carried out by a specialist. Disco's adopters would need to be aware that any vet treatment surrounding this would not be coverable by insurance as it's pre-existing.

Disco has been given the Gift of Life by Caroline Hellings

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

Danube relies on the company of her kennel friends for comfort, so she will need another kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in and finds her paws.

name: Jenny
description:
I can live with older, dog savvy teenagers, aged 13+ who respect my space.

I can be an only dog or live with other dogs. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I will need to learn how to walk on a lead, and would like quiet walks.

I have lived in a home before so I may already know the basics.

I have severe dry eyes, and a small lump. I will be spayed before adoption.

06-08-26 Jenny is a sweet and friendly older lady who has come to us from a breeder but has lived in a home in the past. She has a gentle, affectionate nature and loves to show her love by giving little kisses and gently nibbling your fingers, which is her own special way of asking for attention.

Jenny is a lovely girl who can be a little timid at times, so she is looking for a calm and peaceful home where she can enjoy her golden years surrounded by love and kindness. She would thrive with adopters who are happy to let her settle at her own pace and enjoy a quieter way of life.

Jenny could be an only dog in a home where her family have plenty of time to spend with her, or she could happily live with calm and gentle resident dogs who don't mind sharing their home. She could also live with sensible, older children who will respect her gentle nature and allow her the peace and quiet she enjoys.

As Jenny has previously lived in a home, she should already be familiar with many aspects of family life, including house training, although she may need a little reminder as she settles into a new routine. She will also need to learn to walk comfortably on a harness so that she can enjoy gentle strolls with her new family.

Jenny is a truly wonderful older lady who has so much love to give. She is looking for a calm, caring home where she can relax, be cherished, and enjoy all the comforts she deserves. In return, she will make a loyal and loving companion.

Jenny has come to us with severe dry eye and a small lump that at this time, does not need to be removed. She will receive treatment for her dry eye and this may need to be continued in the home.

Jenny has been given the Gift of Life by Vicki Webb

name: Kira
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I am learning to walk on a harness but may need more time as I heal.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

Kira is a super sweet and gentle lady who has come to us from a breeder. She has now spent a week in foster care and has made lovely progress. Her first day was understandably overwhelming, and she spent hours pacing around the garden, too frightened to come into the house. However, with patience and reassurance, she has already started to settle into her new routine.

Kira has grown in confidence over the past week and now happily follows her foster carer around the house, enjoying being nearby. She is curious about what is going on around her and is no longer fazed by everyday household noises. Although she is still a little shy, she will happily sniff an outstretched hand, gently take treats, and accept a little fuss as people pass by, even if she doesn't actively seek attention just yet. It seems that chicken is certainly the way to Kira's heart!

Kira has a healthy appetite and would happily help herself to the resident dogs' meals if given the opportunity! She enjoys the company of the other dogs and has even started joining in with their excited races up the garden whenever they spot a squirrel, although she's still learning exactly how the game works. She hasn't shown much interest in toys yet and hasn't quite discovered the sofa, but we are sure these milestones will come in time as her confidence continues to grow.

She has been wonderfully clean in the house from the very beginning, helped by having easy access to the garden, and she sleeps soundly through the night. However, she may some reminders of this in her new home. She is also happy wearing a harness, and her foster carers will soon begin introducing lead walking once she is ready.

Kira is looking for a calm, adult-only home where she can continue to blossom at her own pace. She will need plenty of time, reassurance, and TLC as she learns that life can be full of comfort, companionship, and love. Her coat is also beginning to grow back nicely where she had alopecia, and she is looking healthier every day.

In the right home, we believe this gentle little girl has every chance of becoming a wonderful and devoted companion. With kindness, patience, and plenty of tasty chicken treats, Kira's future is looking brighter every day.

Kira has been given the Gift of Life by Raychel Mount

After a week in Foster Kira has made good progress. She found her first day here overwhelming and spent hours pacing the garden too frightened to come into the house.

A week later what a difference she now shadows her Foster Carer, is curious but not phased by household noises. Kira has a good appetite but given the chance will move in on the resident dogs food bowls.

She sleeps through the night and has been clean in the house from the start, helped by the back door always being open. Chicken is the way to win over the heart of this gentle little girl. She happily wears her harness and we will start lead training in the coming days. Kira will sniff a hand, take treats and accept a little fuss in passing but does not seek attention.

She has started joining in on squirrel alert racing up the garden with my girls but doesn’t understand the rules of the game. She has not shown any interest in toys and has not jumped up onto the sofa yet, Kira is not using a crate.

Kira’s coat is starting to grow back where she has alopecia.

Kira is a super sweet and gentle lady who has come to us from a breeder. At the moment, she is feeling quite unsure of her surroundings and will often stand completely still when approached, as she is still learning to feel safe and confident.However, after spending some time with her, Kira begins to relax and will even give a little tail wag, showing that beneath her shy exterior is a lovely girl who wants to trust. With patience, kindness, and understanding, we are confident that she will continue to come out of her shell.Kira is looking for a calm, adult-only home where she can settle at her own pace without any pressure. As she has never lived in a home before, her adopters will need to be patient while she learns all the basics, including house training and walking on a lead. To begin with, gentle garden explorations may be a great way for her to build confidence and start experiencing the world around her.Kira will need plenty of time, reassurance, and TLC as she learns that life can be full of comfort, companionship, and love. In the right home, we believe this sweet girl has every chance of blossoming into a wonderful and devoted companion.

name: Daisy
description:
I’d like a home filled with love and kindness!

I need a larger, male, doggy friend in my new home. I haven't met cats!

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I had an entropion on both lower eyelids, but these have now been surgically repaired

02-06-26 Daisy is a scared Cocker Spaniel who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start.She is finding human interaction very difficult at the moment and will often move away if we get too close. Daisy is worried by handling, so she will need careful and gentle management while she learns that people can be kind. Having had very little life experience, much of the world is still new and overwhelming to her, and she will need patient adopters who are willing to let her progress at her own pace.

At the moment, Daisy is feeling a little less brave and is finding comfort in the company of her kennel friends. We feel it would be best for her to be re-homed with another large, male dog for support and companionship. Having a confident canine friend by her side will help her feel more secure as she settles into home life.

As Daisy has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training, and the other basics of home life. Her adopters will need to be understanding and prepared to guide her through these new experiences with patience and reassurance.

Daisy prefers to enjoy her meals on her own, so mealtimes are carefully managed here and should continue to be managed in the same way in her new home. Feeding her separately helps prevent any confusion over whose food belongs to whom and allows her to feel more relaxed. Treats should also be given thoughtfully and managed in the same way to ensure a positive experience for everyone.

Daisy could share her home with quiet, older dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over who can appreciate and understand that she will need a gentle, quiet introduction to the home and her own space to settle in.

Daisy has arrived with bilateral entropion of the lower eyelids, which have now been surgically repaired by our vets. She is also underweight, so we will be helping her reach and maintain a healthier weight during her stay with us. This will need to be continued in her new home to ensure she remains happy and healthy.

Although Daisy is finding life quite frightening right now, there is a lovely girl underneath those worries. With time, patience, and the support of a canine companion, we are confident that she will begin to blossom and discover that the world is not such a scary place after all.

Daisy has been given the Gift of Life by Lynn Carrivick

name: Olive
description:
I'd like a calm and quiet, adult only home.

I could be the only dog or live with a male resident dog. I can't live with cats.

I would like a secure garden that I can explore.

I walk well on a lead and would enjoy one or two walks a day!

I have lived in a home so I know the basics.

Olive originally came to us from Romania as a puppy with her siblings and was quickly adopted. Sadly, she was recently returned as she was finding life in a busy city and busy household too overwhelming.

She will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult-only home where she can settle at her own pace. We feel she would really benefit from adopters with experience of Romanian dogs. Since being back with us, Olive has shown us just how sociable she is with other dogs and now happily shares her kennel with a lovely male dog called Cooper. The two get along brilliantly and spend much of their time together, often alongside Olive's best friend, Buck. We now feel Olive would happily live with another friendly male dog, although she can also be homed as the only dog. She does occasionally show some guarding behaviours around food with other dogs, but this is easily managed by feeding separately or giving her plenty of space at mealtimes. She cannot share her home with cats or small furries.

Olive can struggle with busy environments and traffic, so we feel she would be much happier in a quieter area where she can enjoy more rural walks. She can also bark at loud noises and strangers visiting the home, so this is something her adopters will need to be willing to work on with her. Her adopters will need to be patient, calm and consistent, helping her gradually build confidence and feel secure in her new environment.

Olive is house trained but may need gentle reminders as she adjusts to a new routine. She walks nicely on the lead and would love an active home where she can enjoy plenty of walks and adventures. She is a clever girl who already knows basic commands such as "sit" and "paw". Olive is a very sweet girl who enjoys being close to her people, happily sitting beside you, though she isn't overly fond of cuddles.

When Olive first arrived back with us, she was quite nervous and wouldn't approach us, but she has grown enormously in confidence during her time here. She now eagerly greets her kennel mummy every morning and has become an absolute joy to care for. She loves going out for walks with our volunteers, which has really helped her confidence continue to blossom, and she absolutely adores chasing balls around our big play yard. She is often at the centre of our larger play groups, encouraging all of the other dogs to run around and play with her. Watching Olive run freely and enjoy herself is truly heartwarming.

After spending the last seven weeks getting to know Olive, we can honestly say she has been an absolute angel. She has settled beautifully into kennel life, but it breaks our hearts knowing she has experienced the comforts of a home and is now waiting for another family to find her. She deserves so much more than kennel life and has so much love to give.

With time, love and TLC, we know Olive will blossom into the most wonderful companion. She really will make one very lucky family complete, so please don't leave this special girl waiting any longer.

Olive has tested negative for Brucella Canis.

Olive has now been with us for 7 weeks, and what an absolute angel she has been, it’s a pleasure being able to care for Olive everyday but it makes me so sad knowing that she has lived in a home and is now waiting in kennels for her forever home to find her!

Olive is always at the centre of the big play group, encouraging all the other dogs to run around and play with her, it is so heart warming watching Olive run freely!

Olive does now also share a kennel with a lovely male dog called Cooper, and the two get along brilliantly. They spend much of their time together, along with Olive's best friend, Buck.

From getting to know Olive during her time with us, we are now happy that she  could happily  with another male dog. With a few gentle introductions, she builds lovely relationships with male dogs and enjoys their company. She also gets on well with female dogs, but if there is already a resident dog in the home, we feel Olive would be happiest sharing her space with a male companion.

Olive can show a little guarding behaviours around food time when it comes to other dogs, but as long as she is fed at distance she is absolutely fine!

Olive deserves so much more than kennel life, she will really make your life’s complete!

Olive has now been here a whole month and has sadly had little to no interest!

I’ve been working with Olive since she first arrived, at the beginning, she was a very nervous girl who wouldn’t really approach me, but over time she has grown so much in confidence. Now, every morning when I arrive, she’s waiting at the front of her kennel to greet me.

Olive also now enjoys going for walks with volunteers it’s really helping her confidence build! She also absolutely loves chasing a ball down our big yard!

Olive does socialise really well with other dogs here at the rescue, however we feel she would be happiest as the only dog in the home where she can have all the attention she deserves, but she could share her home with a calm male dog.

Olive will make the most perfect companion for someone, please don’t leave her waiting much longer.

Olive originally came to us from Romania as a puppy with her siblings and was quickly adopted. Sadly, she has recently been returned as she was finding life in a busy city and busy household too overwhelming.

She will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult only home where she can settle at her own pace. We feel she would really benefit from adopters with experience of Romanian dogs. Olive would be happy to be homed as the only dog but she could also live with a male resident dog, although she can resource guard her food from other dogs so her adopters would need to ensure they were fed separately. She cannot share her home with cats or small furries.

Olive can struggle with busy environments and traffic and so we feel she would be much happier in a quieter area, where she can go on more rural walks. She can also bark at loud noises and strangers visiting the home, so this is something her adopters will need to be willing to work on with her. Her adopters will need to be patient, calm, and consistent, helping her gradually build confidence and feel secure in her new environment.

Olive is house trained but she may need gentle reminders as she adjusts to a new routine. She walks nicely on the lead and would love an active home where she can enjoy plenty of walks and adventures.

Olive is a clever girl who already knows basic commands such as “sit” and “paw”. She is a very sweet girl who enjoys being close to her people, happily sitting beside you, though she isn’t overly fond of cuddles.

With time, love and TLC, we think she will blossom into a wonderful companion, so please don't leave her waiting too long.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Nimbus
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I can walk on a lead and harness and love to explore quiet areas.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

Nimbus is a beautiful girl who has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. When she first arrived, she was very nervous and found everything quite overwhelming. Since then she has started to settle in and has come out of her shell more each day. Nimbus has now moved to a wonderful foster home where she is getting to experience home life for the first time.

While she is still nervous, she has settled into her foster home well. She really loves her food and will sleep all night quietly with the resident dog. She has been clean so far in the home, so is doing really well with her toilet training too. She has started learning all about walking on a lead and harness and now loves to go on walks, so we think she will really enjoy going on walks with her new family.

Nimbus will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult only home with adopters who have plenty of time to spend with her and to help her settle in. She will need another kind and confident resident dog in her new home to be her friend and take her under their wing. It's clear how much she relies on her canine companions for reassurance.

It's clear that she hasn't been used to much socialisation or handling prior to arrival with us and she is still quite wary of people and isn't keen on being handled, but once in your arms she does begin to relax and settle.

As Nimbus had never lived in a home before moving to foster, her adopters will need to be kind and understanding as she continues to settle in and learn all about home life. With patience, kindness, and plenty of reassurance, she will slowly begin to flourish.

Nimbus has been given the Gift of Life by Scott Ferguson

Nimbus or Nell as she is known here in foster, is doing really well. She is house trained and sleeps all night with my dog. She loves her food and will take treats from my hand.

She loves her walks and is fine walking past traffic on quite busy roads, she also enjoys visiting pubs and cafes. Nimbus is fine with all the dogs she meets and is really loves my dog, so she will definitely need a kind confident dog to cuddle up too.

She will let me groom her and check her ears and we have started a little teeth clean, she loves the beef flavoured toothpaste. The only thing Nimbus is still uneasy about is being picked up, but once she settles in your arms she does relax and does enjoy a little cuddle.

Nimbus is a really sweet funny little girl and deserves a forever home where she will make someone a really lovely companion.

Nimbus or Nell as she is known here, has been in foster with us for a week.  Nell is a sweet timid little girl and needs time and patience to help her settle into home life.

She has been clean in the house since she arrived and will now sleep all night with my dog. She loves her food, and is walking on a lead and harness in quiet areas. She really is enjoying her walks and loves meeting other dogs.

She is still wary of people and is not keen on being handled, but once you do pick her up she will settle.

She does rely on my dog and follows him everywhere, so she will need another dog or dogs in her new home, which would need to be a quiet, adult only home.

It will take Nell time to build her confidence, she has done really well so far so hopefully she will find her forever home.

With the recent heatwave, Nimbus has had a much needed and well overdue groom and I think we can all agree she looks absolutely beautiful!

She definitely appreciated being cooler in the hot weather, and it’s allowed her to enjoy the lovely weather the last couple of weeks (within reason of course!!)

Nimbus has been slowly finding her feet here at the rescue, and taking her time with opening up to us. She was incredibly frightened when she first arrived, but with time and patience from her kennel mums and dads, her true personality is slowly coming to the surface.

We find that a lot of our ex-breeders struggle more in the presence of men, but Nimbus is opening up to her kennel dad too. They’re not at the cuddling stage as of yet, but she happily comes up to him and gives him hand kisses so we think with routine, TLC and quality time spent together they’ll get there in no time!

Nimbus is a nervous, flighty little girl who has come to us from a breeder and finds the world quite overwhelming. She is touch-sensitive and clearly hasn’t been used to much handling, so she will need kind, patient adopters who can gently show her that human hands can be kind and reassuring. Despite her worries, once she is in your arms she does begin to relax and settle.

Nimbus relies heavily on the comfort and reassurance of her kennel friends, so she will need a kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help guide and support her as she learns about life in a home and continues to build her confidence. When she feels unsure, she will often retreat to her bed or a quiet corner where she feels safe.

As Nimbus has never lived in a home before, her adopters will need to be patient, gentle, and understanding while she learns all about home life and house training. Walking on a lead may feel overwhelming for her at first, so starting with gentle garden sniffs and allowing her to explore at her own pace will help her gain confidence.

Nimbus is looking for a calm and understanding home with adopters who understand the needs of ex-breeding dogs and are willing to give her the time and space she needs to come out of her shell. With patience, kindness, and plenty of reassurance, we are hopeful she will slowly begin to flourish.

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. name: Cloe
description:
I need an adult only home that understands ex-breeders.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I need an extra secure garden and home that can accommodate my needs.

I am learning to walk on a harness but may need more time as I heal.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have had 7 teeth extracted and an inguinal hernia repaired. Read below for more!

Cloe is a very worried little lady who has come to us from a breeder and is still learning that people can be kind. It is clear she has had very little positive experience with humans in the past, and as a result she finds trust incredibly difficult. She can be flighty when worried and may choose to protect herself if she feels pressured or uncomfortable.

Cloe is a sweet but complex girl who has already shown us that, once she truly trusts someone, she has a wonderfully affectionate side. Although progress has been slow, it has also been incredibly rewarding. She now greets her favourite carers every morning with an excited waggy tail and is trying her absolute hardest to be brave around the people she trusts.

She has made lovely progress with handling and has recently enjoyed a full groom. Cloe was an absolute angel throughout, allowing herself to be groomed beautifully. She has also recently been bathed and gently dried, taking it all in her stride. These may seem like small achievements, but for a little dog who once found human contact so frightening, they are huge milestones.

We have also discovered that being picked up is only scary for Cloe at first. Once she is safely in someone's arms, she relaxes completely and allows herself to be handled without fuss. We truly believe that, with continued patience and positive experiences, this fear will continue to fade and she will become even more confident.

Cloe has also recently started her harness training. Although she is still a little too timid to venture out on walks just yet, she is making a fantastic start and we are confident that, with a little more time and encouragement, she will soon be ready to begin exploring the world beyond the rescue.

Cloe will need a calm, quiet, adult-only home with no visiting children and adopters who have experience of very worried ex-breeding dogs. Her new family will need to understand that building a relationship with her will take time and that the best way to win her trust is to allow her to approach on her own terms, without rushing or placing expectations on her.

She absolutely loves the company of other dogs and will need a kind, calm and confident resident dog in her new home. Having a canine friend gives her comfort and reassurance and will help guide her as she learns about life beyond the rescue. We have also discovered that Cloe is not comfortable around cats and can become quite fixated by them, so she will need a cat-free home.

As she has never lived in a home before, Cloe's adopters will need to be patient as she learns about house training and everyday routines. Progress with Cloe may never be fast, but she proves time and time again that she is willing to try for the people she trusts.

We are incredibly hopeful for Cloe's future. She has already come so much further than we ever imagined possible in the rescue environment, and we truly believe she will flourish in a patient, understanding home. She simply needs someone willing to take a chance on her, give her all the time she needs, and let her discover that the world isn't such a scary place after all.

Cloe has had seven teeth extracted at the time of her spay, as well as an inguinal hernia repaired. She also had a lump removed from her right upper eyelid.

Cloe has been given the Gift of Life by Carol Unsworth

So Cloe has been with me for about 3 months now and I can happily say I’m finally starting to see the light as the end of the tunnel with her. I think she finally has trust in me and knows that I’m not going to hurt her, and she’s trying her absolute hardest to be brave around me. She still gets really excited to see me every morning and it always instantly brightens my days.

She’s had a busy few weeks since my last update and I really couldn’t be prouder of her. To start with, she had a full groom with our incredible resident groomer who is perfect with our scared dogs, and she was an ANGEL through the whole thing. We were both so proud of her and now she looks absolutely beautiful. I of course had to pick her up to take her into the grooming room and I was a little worried she’d hold a grudge against me, but she didn’t. She was happy when I went to get her and still had a waggy tail at me when I put her back down in her kennel. We decided not to bath her that same day as it would have been too much for her, so I bathed and dried her myself yesterday. Again, she was amazing. She was so good in the bath and let me give her a good shampoo all over. She was more scared of the dryer so I was as gentle as I could have been, and I didn’t dry her completely as I didn’t want to push it. Again, no grudges were held!!!

What I’ve come to learn about Cloe is that she’s only worried and panicky with being picked up initially. As soon as I’ve got her comfortably in my arms, she no longer stresses or fusses and lets me handle her with no issues. I really believe she’ll get over her fear of being picked up in time, and when she does, I think she’ll drop all her guards.

I am truly, truly hopeful for Cloe’s future and I really do think someone just needs to take a chance on her. Even though progress here at the rescue has been slow, it’s still progress, and that is difficult to achieve for dogs like Cloe in such a busy environment. She needs a home, so PLEASE don’t keep her waiting too much longer!!

Progress with Cloe is still very slow, but it is there and it is happening, so that’s all that matters. Since my last update she has opened herself up to me ever so slightly, and now gets very excited to see me everything morning and will run up to me and sniff my fingers with a waggy tail. I know that may not sound like a lot to most, but for a dog like Cloe it’s a big step forward.

I mentioned in my last update that I had to take her into the vets a few times and it made her more frightened of me, so since then I’ve completely left her be as I felt as though we needed to reset. I’ve spent a lot of time with her, just sitting down and being present, but no touching (until today). She wasn’t happy about me picking her up and was trying to bite the blanket I was holding, but she put up way less of a fight than she did a few weeks ago … so I’m taking that as a win!! I took her outside of her kennel just to try and take some nice photos of her and she coped really well. When we were finished and I put her back in her kennel, I got down on the floor and wiggled my fingers at her to see if she was still my friend, and thankfully she did come over with a waggy tail, so that made me happy.

Over the next few weeks I’m going to continue some gentle handling like today, every so often so that she gets more used to it, but it also won’t overwhelm her. I’ll listen to her and what she’s telling me .. stop if it’s too much, and do a little more if she’s ready.I really love Cloe and I’m understanding her more and more each day, and I think she feels the same way about me. I’m starting to feel hopeful!!

Cloe is a sweet but complex little girl who has clearly been through a great deal in her life. She has major trust issues with humans and so far only trusts one person out of all the staff that work here. At the rescue we see 2 sides of her. One side is a happy, excitable girl who enjoys a little fuss and is fine to be picked up (by her favourite person), and the other side is a scared girl who would rather be left alone (by everyone else). Her favourite person here is the first person that worked with her when she first arrived, so I think she sees him as her ‘rescuer’ which is very sweet. She definitely trusts him and it’s quite shocking to see the difference in her when she’s around him - in a good way! With everyone else, she’s still very standoffish and doesn’t tolerate being touched or handled at all. She will nip to protect herself, but this doesn’t mean she’s a nasty dog at all .. she’s simply just that scared.I’ve been working with Cloe for about a month now and even though she’s a lot more comfortable around me now than she used to be, she definitely still doesn’t trust me. I think it’s because I had to take her into the vets a couple of times when she first came over to my section, and it’s definitely stunted our relationship. Normally with dogs like Cloe, I won’t handle them for a good while until I establish some form of bond with them, but I couldn’t do this with Cloe as she had to see the vet. Since then, I’ve been leaving her to her own devises and trying to win her over from afar. Although she still hardly approaches me, she’s more relaxed in my presence now .. so at least we are making progress.I think in Cloe’s case, the best way to work with her is to just leave her come to you first. If she can work out by herself that you’re kind and not a threat, you’re heading in the right direction!! And then when she trusts you, she’ll drop her guard with you and become a little sweetheart like she is with her favourite staff member here. In a home where she has all the time in the world to bond with her new parents, I think she will absolutely blossom!!! But it may take a little while to get there, so her future adopters will need to be very understanding and patient with her. It will be SO worth it though, I promise!

Cloe is a very worried little lady who has come to us from a breeding environment and is not yet comfortable with being handled. It’s clear she has had very little experience of kindness, so she can be quite flighty and may panic if approached too quickly and can choose to make the wrong decision if pushed out of her comfort zone.

Cloe settles quickly once she feels safe and has already begun making lovely progress. With her favourite member of staff she is already showing her funny and affectionate side and is happy to approach him, kiss his fingers and will even do a little excited dance. With patient, understanding adopters who can appreciate why she may feel scared or defensive and support her as she builds trust, we believe she will settle in and start to come out of her shell.

She will need a calm and quiet adult-only home with no visiting children and with adopters who have experience of scared ex-breeding dogs and who are willing to give her the patience, kindness, and time she needs to truly thrive.

Cloe is already starting to approach you slowly on her own terms and so will need plenty of time, gentle encouragement, and extra TLC to continue building her confidence. She absolutely loves the company of other dogs and will need a kind, calm, and confident resident dog in her new home to help guide her as she adjusts to home life.

As she has never lived in a home before, Cloe's adopters will need to be kind and understanding as she settles in and learns all about home life and new skills like house training. She doesn't yet walk on a lead and harness and will need to practice around the home and garden once she is more comfortable with being handled.

Cloe has had 7 teeth extracted at the time of her spay as well as an inguinal hernia repaired. She had a lump on her right upper eye lid that has been removed.

name: Lassie
description:
I need an adult-only home where I can feel safe and loved.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I cannot live with cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I can walk well on a lead and would love an active home.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have been spayed and am ready for my forever home.

Lassie has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. When she first arrived she was a very nervous girl as she had not had much experience with people, so everything felt very new and overwhelming to her. She could be quite skittish when approached and was worried about meeting new people and being handled. Since then her confidence has started to really grow. Once she gets to know you, she is the most loyal, loving and affectionate girl and it's so wonderful to see.

Lassie will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult only home where she can settle in at her own pace. She would benefit from adopters who have breed experience and experience with worried dogs.

She will be looking for a home where there was at least one other kind and playful resident dog to be her friend and guide. She gets on brilliantly with all dogs here out and about and socialises well with a variety of breeds and sizes. However, we have found that she is most comfortable sharing her home with other Collies and will therefore need a home with at least one resident Collie. She cannot be homed with cats or small furries. She doesn't like to share her food with other dogs, so her adopters would need to ensure she was fed separately and would need to separate when feeding any long last treats or chews too.

Lassie now walks well on a lead and would love to find an active home where she can go on lots of walks and adventures with her new family and where her clever collie brain can be kept both mentally and physically stimulated. She is only used to walking in quiet areas, so would need gentle introduction to any busier places. Lassie has never lived in a home before so her adopters will need to be kind and understanding as she settles into the home and learns all about home life and new skills like house training.

With time, patience, and lots of love, Lassie will blossom. Once she has settled and gained confidence, she will become a cracking addition to her new family and will enjoy all the adventures life has to offer.

Lassie will need more than one meet and greet with her prospective adopters to allow her time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

Lassie spent some time in the office today and coped really well. She happily tucked into a chicken foot for a tasty treat, although she couldn't resist pinching her kennel friend's one too! She was very curious about everything going on around her and enjoyed exploring her surroundings.

A member of staff she hadn't met before came into the office, and although Lassie was a little wary at first, she quickly settled and went back to happily enjoying her chicken foot. It was lovely to see her take the new experience in her stride and continue growing in confidence.

Beautiful beautiful Lassie! What a collie she is, she is so bright and has really come on so much with her basic training. Now knowing "sit" and "lie down". When we're out walking and a car is approaching, all I have to do is ask her to the verge and she sits and waits beautifully until we're able to start walking again. She really doesn't seem to be fazed by much traffic, but is very fixated with sheep if she comes across any. She passes horses lovely and will happily walk past other dogs no issue, but isn't keen on them approaching her. She's a big fan of food which helps with her training.She just needs people that understand that the girl she is when they first meet her is very worried but once she trusts you, her true personality really shines through.

Lassie is such a pretty girl who would do anything for you when she trusts you but is still wary of people initially. She did take treats off of a new person yesterday which was amazing to see. She needs to be in a collie experienced home with someone who will allow her the time to trust them at her own pace. She does love having a playfriend and she seems to be happiest when amongst other collies and collie crosses. She doesn't like sharing her food but is happy to share toys, beds and treats.

Lassie absolutely loves going out for her walks and gets very excited when she knows it’s time to head out. She really enjoys having a good sniff along the way and is always very interested in watching what’s going on in the fields as she passes by. Once she gets to know you, she is incredibly loving and affectionate, although she can take a little bit of time to warm up to new people. Lassie would still need a home with a resident dog, and she would truly thrive in a collie-experienced home where her needs and personality can be well understood.

Lassie is such a beautiful girl and once she knows you, she is the most affectionate, loyal and loving companion. She now walks well on a lead and absolutely loves her walks.

She will need a home with at least one other kind and confident resident dog who is a similar size to her and who loves to have a good play sometimes.

She doesn't like to share her food bowl, so he will need to be fed separately and this is something that her adopters will need to manage. In the right home she'll be someone's absolute best friend.

Lassie is a worried little lady who has come to us from a breeder. She has not had much experience with people, so everything feels very new and overwhelming to her. She can be quite skittish when approached, so she will need a calm, experienced home where she can be given the time and patience she needs to learn to trust.

At the moment, Lassie is scared of being touched, but she has already started to build a bond with her kennel mum and now allows gentle strokes from her. This shows that with consistency and kindness, shecanlearn to trust, and once she feels safe, she will begin to show her sweet side.

Lassie does walk on a lead, though she finds new experiences worrying, so she will need gentle introductions to the big wide world. She will also need to learn about house training and all the basics of living in a home, as these are things she has never known before.

Because Lassie is such a sensitive soul, she will need an adult-only home with no visiting children, and adopters who are happy to take things slowly at her pace. She will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home who can help her feel secure and show her the ropes. She gets on brilliantly with all dogs here and socialises well with a variety of breeds and sizes. She cannot be homed with cats or small furries.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Sally
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a larger, resident male dog to help me settle in and I have met cats fine.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I am learning to walk on a lead and harness, but it's still very new for me.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

Sweet little Sally has come to us from a breeder to begin her search for a loving forever home. When she first arrived, she was understandably feeling a little worried to find herself here, but she has been trying so hard to be brave and has really started to come out of her shell.

Sally is growing into the funniest and cutest little dog, and for such a small girl she certainly has a big personality that is beginning to shine through. Her confidence continues to grow, and she now happily enjoys receiving fuss and attention from people she knows and trusts. She has also made lovely progress with her harness training. While this was initially a brand-new experience for her, she now walks happily on her harness with people she feels comfortable with and enjoys exploring by their side. As with everything, she will need a little time to build the same confidence with her new family.

Sally is a super little dog who is just waiting for someone to give her the time, patience and love she needs to continue building her confidence. With the right home and lots of kindness, we are sure she will blossom into a wonderful companion.

She will be looking for a calm, kind and understanding home with adopters who are around most of the time and who will allow her to settle in at her own pace. She has never lived in a home before, so everything about family life will be new to Sally. She will need gentle guidance as she learns the routines of home life, including house training and continuing to build her confidence in new situations.

Sally absolutely loves other dogs and gains a great deal of comfort from having canine friends around her. She will need another dog in her new home to help her feel secure, but she would prefer the company of a smaller male dog. Sally can be a little bossy with female dogs, so she is best suited to living with a male companion. She has also met a cat at the rescue and coped well (please see the video in her gallery!), so she could potentially live with a dog-savvy cat.

This sweet little girl just needs someone to give her the chance she deserves, and we are sure she will repay that love tenfold with her own blossoming confidence and affectionate nature.

Sally has a lick granuloma on her left front leg, which is healing, and an old scar on her left hip. She had an umbilical hernia repaired at the time of her spay and is currently being treated for bilateral conjunctivitis.

Sally has been given the Gift of Life by Carolina Olsen

Super little Sally is doing so well. I absolutely adore this lovely lady. She grows in confidence every day, and it really hasn’t taken her all that long to come out of her shell.

Sally still needs a little time with new people to feel safe, but she tries so hard, and once she feels comfortable with you, her funny personality shines through, from showing you her full-body rolls, to running over for gentle fusses, or scrambling all over you for foodie treats. I’m very proud of how hard she tries each day to be brave.

Today, Sally enjoyed another little walk around the rescue with her new kennel companion. Sally is by no means confident on the lead yet and will need gentle encouragement and patience to continue her learning journey and start to relax on her walks.

Sally looks to her kennel buddies for support, and her perfect home will already have a friendly (male) resident dog to help show her the way. Sally is best suited to a quiet, adult-only home, ideally with knowledge and/or experience of ex-breeding dogs.

Sally is just the growing into the funniest, cutest of little dogs. For a small being she has a big personality and it’s really starting to shine through. She grows ever confident, and happily takes fusses from me and today successfully begun harness training.

Sally is a super little dog just waiting for a loving home to help continue bringing her out of her shell. Sally will need a friend in her new home but prefers the company of smaller male dogs, she can be a bit bossy with female dogs and is best suited to an adult only home.

Sweet little Sally has come to us from a breeder to begin her search for a loving forever home. She is a very gentle girl who is understandably feeling a little worried to find herself here, but she is trying so hard to be brave.

Sally will gently approach you for a little sniff and is already showing what a sweet nature she has, she just needs time, patience and reassurance to help her confidence grow. With the right home and lots of kindness, we are sure she will blossom into a lovely companion.

She will be looking for a calm, kind and understanding home with adopters who are around most of the time and who will allow her to settle in at her own pace. Everything in a home environment will be completely new to Sally, so she will need gentle guidance as she learns about everyday life and new skills such as house training and how to walk on a lead.

Sally absolutely loves other dogs and gains a lot of comfort from them, so she will need at least one other kind and gentle resident dog in her new home to be her friend and show her the way. Sally will need a larger, male dog in her home and cannot live with females or smaller dogs.

This sweet girl just needs someone to give her the chance she deserves and she will repay your love tenfold.

Sally has a lick granuloma on her left front leg, which is healing and an old scar on her left hip. She has had an umbilical hernia repair at the time of her spay and is being treated for bilateral conjunctivitis.
