name: Cora
description:
I can live with dog-savvy  teens, and would love an active home!

I can be an only dog or live with other dogs. I have never met cats.

I would love a garden to run and play in!

I would love plenty of adventures once I am fully vaccinated!

I am just a puppy! Please be patient with me while I learn the basics!

My adopter will need to agree to have me spayed when I'm old enough.

01-08-26 Cora is an amazing puppy who has come to us with her siblings following an accidental litter. She is a happy, confident girl who is full of fun and has a wonderful zest for life. Cora is already a big girl for her age, and we believe she is a Cane Corso Cross, so her adopters will need to be prepared for her to grow into a large adult dog.

Cora is a friendly and affectionate pup who is looking for a loving home where she can continue to learn and explore the world. She has started learning about walking on a harness, and would like to continue this, out and about, once she is fully vaccinated and settled into her new home, she will love getting out and about on plenty of adventures with her family.

Cora could live with older, dog-savvy children, aged 13+ who understand that she is a large, boisterous puppy and will need help learning her manners as she grows. She could happily live with another friendly dog who doesn't mind sharing their home with a playful youngster, or she could be an only dog, providing her new family have plenty of time to dedicate to her training, socialisation, and exercise.

As with all puppies, Cora will need continued guidance with house training, lead walking, and all the basics of family life. Her adopters must be committed to taking her to puppy socialisation and training classes to help her develop into a confident, well-mannered adult and agree to have her spayed when she is of age.

Cora is a truly lovely girl with so much potential. She is looking for a family who will give her the love, time, and commitment she deserves, and in return she is sure to become a wonderful and loyal companion.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Tippins
description:
I can live with older children, aged 16+, who understand I need time to settle in.

I need a larger doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats yet!

I would like a large, and secure garden that I can settle into.

I do walk on a lead, but am still gaining my confidence and will need support.

Please be patient with me, I haven’t lived in a home before.

I have been spayed and am ready for my forever home!

06-07-26 Tippins is a lovely lady who has come into our care from a breeder. She is a little apprehensive when she first meets new people, but she is already showing signs that her confidence is growing. Once she knows you, she enjoys a fuss and is happy to be handled. Tippins has a big personality and is a fun girl to spend time with.

At the moment, Tippins is feeling a little less brave and is finding comfort in the company of her kennel friends. We feel it would be best for her to be rehomed with at least one other confident resident dog for support and companionship. She has always lived with bigger dogs and seems happiest around them. Tippins can be a little bossy with less confident dogs, so she wouldn't be suitable to live with smaller or younger dogs. We will continue to assess her confidence while she is with us to see if she could adapt to being an only dog. She will need adopters with ex-breeding experience that can understand her needs.

As Tippins has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to be patient while she settles in and learns what home life is all about. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens, aged 16+ that can allow her time to settle into a calm environment.

Tippins already walks on a lead, but doesn't seem to be overly confident on this so she will need continued support as she learns, and once she has settled into her new home, she would enjoy one or two walks around the local area with her resident dog so that she can continue lead training.

Tippins is a lovely girl with lots of character. She's already showing us what a sweet dog she is, and we hope that, with time and patience, she'll continue to grow in confidence and enjoy everything home life has to offer.

Tippins is now receiving regular cleanings from the vets for waxy ears and this will need to be monitored in her new home.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Calypso
description:
I can live with older, dog-savvy kids aged 13+ who are sensible and loving.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I will need an extra secure garden as I can be nervous and flighty!

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I will be spayed before going to my forever home!

24-07-26 Calypso is a shy lady who has come into our care from a breeder. She is a sweet and gentle girl who is still very unsure of people. Calypso isn't a fan of being picked up and may run away when we approach her, as she is not yet sure of our intentions. However, once she is safely in our arms, she settles enough to allow gentle handling.

Calypso gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends and relies on their company for comfort, so she will need a kind resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in and finds her paws.

As Calypso has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training, and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to be patient and allow her the time she needs to adjust to her new surroundings.

She can live with older, dog-savvy teens who are aged 13+ that are sensible and will allow her time to settle in at her own pace. She can be a bit flighty, and nervous of fast movements so she will need an extra secure home and garden to keep her safe.

Calypso is a lovely, gentle girl who is just beginning to learn that people can be kind. With the support of a friendly dog and a patient family who are happy to go at her pace, we hope she will gradually grow in confidence and begin to enjoy all the comforts of home life.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Trixie
description:
I'll need an adult only home with adopters with experience of ex-breeding dogs.

I am looking for a home where I can be the only dog & get all the love and attention.

I need an extra secure garden and home that can accommodate my needs.

I walk on a lead but will need my adopters to be extra secure.

I understand toilet training, but will need a reminder in a new home!

I have been spayed and am ready for my forever home! Read below for more info!

Trixie is a very sweet lady who has come to us from a breeder in search of a new start. Although her tail is constantly wagging, she will shyly approach for a gentle fuss and tends to stay away and watch from a distance until she feels safe. Once she builds trust, she is affectionate and will enjoy a snuggle and a gentle fuss.

In foster, she shown herself to be a nervous girl in new environments who still needed encouragement to engage with new people. She would often hang back and observe, but once more secure she would come forward for interaction and enjoy fuss and attention from her fosterer.

Despite the fact that she is still a nervous girl, she also isn't keen on sharing her home with other dogs and so we feel she would be happiest as an only dog in her new home. Although she has been in foster with other dogs, she can be jealous when her fosterer is showing attention to other dogs and has reacted towards them on occasion. She is fine with socialising with other calm dogs, but can be reactive towards barking or yappy dogs ordogs that are in her face too much or too boisterous.For this reason, we feel she would be best suited to an adult only home with adopters who have experience of nervous ex-breeding dogs. She has met cats fine, but due to her tendency to become jealous, we would not look to home her with cats.

In the garden, she has shown signs of digging and has previously tried to escape a foster home, so very secure boundaries are essential. Her new home will need to have 6ft minimum fencing height and her new adopters will need to keep her on lead in the garden until she gains confidence outside. She might enjoy having a sand pit to play in so she can enjoy digging in appropriate areas.

Trixie had been mostly clean in the house in her foster home, and seemed to be a star at toilet training. However, she may need some reminders in her new home as she settles in new surroundings.

She is walking on a lead and harness, but can still become startled and may try to back out if frightened. She needs experienced adopters, a secure garden (6ft+ fencing) as she has been digging in her foster garden, and additional safety measures indoors.

She will need a calm, secure, adult-only home and a gentle introduction to home life.

She has had a small lump removed from her left mammary gland and is recovering well.

Trixie has been given the Gift of Life by Tanya Player

Hello, my name is Trixie and I'm living at Many Tears whilst I wait for my forever home to find me.

My perfect home would be with lovely, gentle people, that enjoy a quiet life. I am easily worried by new sounds and loud noises and so I will need lots of time to adjust to my new home and environment. I love a squishy bed to lie on and one of those sofas I hear about sounds perfect to try.

I would be very happy in a secure garden where I won’t be bothered by other people, just my family, sitting with me and a few toys for little plays. Perhaps when I get used to my new people we could go for walks in quiet places together - but I will need time before I’m fully ready to do this.

I enjoy my food, so a good supply of tasty meals would make me very happy. I really don’t want much just a simple, safe and loving home.

Side note from my kennel mum:Trixie is a wonderful loving dog once she feels safe with you. She is a flight risk when startled - and she is easily startled!

If every day was a Trixie day, life would be lovely. Trixie is the sweetest and loveliest of dogs. Her favourite pastimes include tummy rubs and cuddles, and if there’s a home out there with a Trixie-sized spot on the sofa and a human to shower her with fusses, she would be in heaven.

When Trixie is happy, you know it, and she will bounce around you outside for a little play before parking herself next to you for more belly rubs. She loves sitting outside and just relaxing with you.

Trixie does also enjoy a walk (in very quiet areas); however, she can be very, very easily spooked and, if startled, will bolt and has done so previously. Any adopters would need to be very aware of this and work on building her confidence at home before considering outings. Adopters will also need to ensure a very secure setup for her at home, i.e. secure entrances and exits from the house.

Trixie prefers to have a human all to herself and, for this reason, she would like to be the only dog with a human who will be home most of the time.

Trixie truly is a gem of a girl with a heart of gold. A special and sweet lady, who longs for safe hands (and laps) to snuggle into. This super dog needs a little time and a lot of security,  give her that and you will have a bond for life.

Trixie is looking for a home that is quiet, gentle, patient and super secure on a practical level. Trixie is incredibly spooky and even if she trusts you, the slightest of frights in her environment and she will bolt. Because Trixie is a high flight risk she would be suited to a dog experienced home, ideally with knowledge of flighty and/or ex-breeding dogs.

It’s important that her new people have a secure plan for getting her out of the car on arrival home after adoption and are able to keep entrance and exits to the house escape safe. In return for your kindness Trixie will be the cutest of best friends. Trixie is looking to be the only dog and is suited to an adult home with no visiting children.

Trixie has been in foster with me for three weeks now and is settling into our routine fairly well.

When she first arrived, Trixie was very human-oriented and showed signs of jealousy towards other dogs, which led to a few altercations. She would often growl if another dog came close to me, as she wanted all the attention for herself. This is something we’ve been working on, but we still feel it is best if she is homed as an only dog in her new home.

From her interactions with my resident dogs, it’s clear that Trixie isn’t comfortable with small, yappy dogs. She does seem to prefer female human company, although she is continuing to build confidence more generally. She currently sleeps downstairs in an open, covered crate, which she uses as her safe space.

For the first couple of weeks, Trixie has slept downstairs quietly through the night with no accidents. Over the last few nights, she has been a little more unsettled and has had a couple of accidents, which seems to be linked to wanting more human attention.

Trixie is fed on dry Arden Grange and is currently fed separately, as she will try to eat other dogs’ food if given the chance. She was also caught eating poo, so I have started soaking her food in hot water and letting it cool, which she seems to prefer.

In her first week, Trixie did try digging in the garden and looking for ways to escape, but this behaviour has now settled. She clearly recognises me and gets very excited when she sees me, running over happily for fuss and attention.

She has been out on walks and does reasonably well when accompanied by another dog, but she is still quite flighty and easily startled. For now, she should only be walked in secure areas, as she will try to back out of her harness if she feels unsure and has demonstrated this once already.

Trixie can be complex at times, so she will need a calm, experienced adopter who understands nervous, ex-breeding dogs and can handle her with patience and care. It will be important to give her time to settle at home and build trust before introducing too many new experiences, especially.

Trixie absolutely craves human attention and is happiest curled up next to me on the sofa. As her confidence continues to grow and her jealousy is managed, she has all the makings of a very loyal and loving companion who simply wants to feel safe and adored.

Trixie is now in foster and is settling in well. She travelled well and was clean on arrival with no issues noted in the car or on entering the home.

Once in the foster home, Trixie has shown herself to be a very nervous little girl who is still unsure of new environments and needs encouragement to engage with people. She will often hang back and watch, but once she feels a bit more secure she will come forward and seek interaction. On these occasions she has chosen to snuggle close to me and will sit gazing and enjoying contact, although she does need to be gently encouraged each time as confidence doesn’t yet seem consistent.

It has quickly become apparent that Trixie is quite a complex girl in the home. She is very focused on attention and has already shown signs of jealousy when sharing human interaction. On one occasion, when another foster dog came onto the sofa, Trixie reacted strongly and became defensive. She can also be particular about other dogs in general and can be especially reactive to barking dogs, and has shown a clear dislike of a small dachshund in the home. For this reason, she will now be looking for a home as an only dog where she can get all of the attention for herself.

Outside of this, she is an active little girl and has already shown she is a determined digger, having previously managed to dig under fencing and patio areas. This will need careful management going forward with very secure boundaries required.

Overall, Trixie is settling in but is still very much finding her feet.

name: Whispy
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have not met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I haven't tried walks just yet and will find this a bit overwhelming at the moment.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have had 2 mammary lumps removed and 2 teeth extracted.

Whispy has come to us from a breeder and is a truly heartbreaking girl. When she first arrived, she was incredibly shut down and would bury her face into the wall in the hope that nobody would notice her. She would tremble when approached and could sometimes grumble or bark, but this has always come from a place of pure fear rather than aggression.

After spending a couple of weeks settling into her kennel routine, it is clear that Whispy has experienced very little kindness in her life. Her fears are deeply ingrained, and she has no understanding of what people's intentions are. When someone enters her kennel, she will often bark and grumble in panic because she is so frightened of what might happen next. Despite this, she allows gentle handling, strokes, and being picked up without any fuss, almost as though she has simply resigned herself to it. It is incredibly sad to see, and all she really needs is someone who will show her that people can be kind.

Whispy takes enormous comfort from other dogs and has formed lovely bonds with her two current kennel companions, who she happily shares everything with. She can be selective about the dogs she befriends and seems to prefer smaller, calm, gentle dogs rather than larger or more boisterous companions. Once she trusts another dog, they become an enormous source of reassurance, so she will need at least one kind, quiet, confident resident dog in her forever home who can help her navigate the world and show her that life doesn't have to be so frightening.

Whispy is looking for a calm, adult-only home with adopters who have experience with very scared ex-breeding dogs and who understand that trust cannot be rushed. As she has never lived in a home before, she will need help learning everything from house training to settling into a routine. Walks are not something she is ready for at the moment, and her adopters must be prepared to let her progress entirely at her own pace. Gentle garden exploration will be much more appropriate until she feels safe enough to take the next steps.

Because Whispy is an older girl and her fears are so deeply rooted, she may never completely lose all of her worries or become the confident dog people often imagine. Her adopters will need to love and accept her exactly as she is, celebrating every tiny step forward without expecting her to become a different dog. For the right family, watching Whispy slowly learn to feel safe will be incredibly rewarding.

Whispy is a very special little lady who has spent far too much of her life living in fear. She deserves a safe place to call home, where she knows nobody will ever hurt or give up on her again. With endless patience, understanding, and unconditional love, we hope she can finally experience the peaceful and happy life she has always deserved.

She has had two mammary lumps removed at the time of her spay and has also had two teeth extracted.

Whispy has been given the Gift of Life by Alison Smith

Whispy has been on my section for a couple of weeks now and oh my goodness is she a heartbreaker. I have no idea what she’s been through in her life, but her fears are deeply ingrained. She has no trust in anything or anyone, apart from a select few dogs at the rescue that she has dropped her guard with. She has absolutely no idea about human kindness, nor what our intentions are. She grumbles and barks when we enter her kennel in pure panic, as she’s so scared of what we’re going to do to her. Even though she may sound a little scary, she lets me stroke her and pick her up absolutely fine .. kind of like she’s just given up. It’s quite sad actually.Whispy currently has 2 kennel friends who she gets on well with and shares everything with. One is a Shih Tzu Cross and one is a Poodle Cross. I have tried quite a few dogs with her and it does seem as though she favours smaller dogs to larger ones. And definitely calmer, quieter ones that don’t get in her face.Whispy will need a very patient and understanding home with adopters who have experience with very scared dogs. Because she’s on the older side, she may never truly lose all of her worries and fears, and may never become a ‘normal’ dog, and this is something her adopters will need to be okay with, and love her and accept her anyway. Things such as going out for walks are not currently in the near future for Whipsy, and it’s going to take a lot of time and gentle guidance to ease her into such things.This poor, sweet girl does not deserve to live her life in fear and panic mode. She deserves to have a safe place to call her own, where she knows nobody is going to hurt her. She deserves to be loved unconditionally, and to not be given up on no matter what.

Whispy has come to us from a breeder and is a truly heartbreaking girl. When she first arrived, she was incredibly shut down, and would bury her face into the wall in the hope that nobody would notice her. She would tremble when approached and could sometimes be a little grumbly, but this was simply because she is so frightened and overwhelmed by her surroundings.

Since then, she has started to settle in and is trying so hard to be brave. She can be vocal with people and is still nervous to approach you but with patience and kind handling she has been joining in on yard times and taking treats, but she still has a ways to go. Whispy has never known the kindness of people so will retreat to a corner when she feels stressed.

Whispy will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience with scared ex-breeding dogs and who are willing to give her all the time, patience and understanding she needs to settle and learn to trust.

She relies on other dogs for reassurance and so she will need at least one other confident, laid back resident dog in her new home who can take her under their wing and provide reassurance as she begins to build confidence. She can be selective over the dogs she enjoys spending time with however once she takes to a friend, she does so well with them and it boosts her confidence. She will need a very placid dog in the home who won’t worry when she is scared. She has had a few grumbles when meeting new dogs but she is just scared and needs time to develop a bond with them.

As she has never lived in a home before, Whispy will need kind and understanding adopters as she learns all about home life and new skills like house training. She doesn't yet walk on a lead and harness and this will be too overwhelming for her at the moment and once she is more comfortable she can begin learning in a secure garden until she feels brave enough to venture further.

Whispy is a very special lady looking for an equally special home. She has missed out on so much in her life and will need a home who will take things day by day with her and give her the support and love she’s so desperate for.

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Toby
description:
I need an experienced, adult only home with no visiting children.

I would prefer to be an only dog and no cats please!

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I can walk well on a lead but can be reactive to bikes.

I was born with some deformed toes, which have been amputated.

Toby is a handsome Cocker Spaniel who has been through a lot in his young life and is now looking for a special someone to help him write his next chapter. Originally coming to us from a breeder at just three months old, Toby was a very scared little puppy who found the world overwhelming. Although he found a loving home, he was sadly returned to our care after his adopters felt unable to manage some of his behaviours.

Toby is still a sensitive soul and will need a calm, adult-only home with no visiting children. His new family should have experience with worried or complex dogs and be confident in helping him feel safe. He will need a home without cats as he has met them at the rescue, and was too interested. While he is generally affectionate and loving, Toby has shown some resource guarding tendencies, such as grumbling when people pass by his bed or the sofa when he is resting there. He did once nip his adopter. This was an isolated incident, but it’s important that any new adopters are comfortable managing and working with these behaviours using gentle, positive methods. That said, since being back with us Toby has come out of his shell beautifully. He greets staff with a wagging tail, and absolutely loves attention, affection, and food, especially food! Those who work with him absolutely adore him and think he is the most special and wonderful boy!

Toby will be looking for a home where he can be the only dog. He did live with another dog previously and while they did get along, he did sometimes guard his adopter’s attention, so for this reason he is best suited to being homed as an only dog.

Out and about, Toby enjoys his walks and is lovely on and off the lead. He has good recall and mixes well with other dogs, although he can be reactive to bicycles, so should only be let off lead in safe, secure areas away from the public.

Toby was born with some deformed toes that were later amputated. He has always had a slightly unusual gait due to this, but our vets have noted he does also have a luxating patella and is on pain relief for this at the moment, but this may improve with gentle exercise. He also has a naturally short tail, which just adds to his unique charm.

Toby is a sweet, loving boy who truly wants to connect. He has already won the hearts of everyone here, and we’re all rooting for him to find a calm, understanding home where he can feel safe, build trust, and thrive.

If you have the time, patience, and experience to offer Toby the gentle guidance he needs, he will reward you with loyalty, love, and plenty of cuddles.

Tobywill need more than one meet and greet with his prospective adopters to allow him time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

This week, Toby’s kennel mum celebrated his 1 year anniversary by breaking him out of the rescue for a couple of hours of fun!!Toby travelled good as hold in the car, and happily climbed into the back of the car & had his seatbelt harness fitted with no issues at all.He travelled to Pupstars Paddock with his kennel mum & another staff member who was new to him. He was absolutely brilliant with that staff member who could only sing his praises!!Toby absolutely LOVED the secure field, his tail did not stop wagging, he followed his kennel mum around everywhere and was (very gently) taking treats of both staff members.Once Toby bonds with you, he is the most loyal boy in the world. His circle of trust is only getting bigger, with more and more staff members falling in love with him as time goes on. He may have a stricter criteria than most, but it just means he is just an incredibly special boy in need of a special home. He is such a darling and we wish more people would be able to see it!

Toby’s one year anniversary with us is slowly approaching, and it honestly breaks my heart every day knowing he’s still not curled up on a sofa in a home of his own.

Toby is literally such an amazing dog when he knows you, all he wants to do is spend time with you, whether that be sitting with you, or going out for a gentle stroll!

Recently, I’ve been working on Toby’s lead reactivity, and he’s been doing incredibly well. He’s making such good progress, and I’m so proud of how far he’s come!

I really hope this is the last update I have to write about toby, hopefully his next updates will be coming from his new pawrents, showing us him blossoming in a home and how truly special he really is!

I’ve had the absolute joy of working with Toby for a couple of months now, and he truly is one of my more sensitive, special boys!

Once Toby gets to know you, he turns into the happiest, most affectionate little soul you could ever meet! He absolutely loves zooming around our big play yard, or heading out for a calm, gentle stroll along the lanes taking everything in at his own pace, Toby can be reactive towards passing cars or other dogs, it is something we are currently working on with him!

With the weather getting nicer, I decided it was the perfect day for a little adventure down to the river! To get there, we walk through a huge open field, so I popped Toby on a long line to give him some extra freedom to explore.I don’t think I’ve ever seen a dog so happy he spent most of his time rolling around on his back in the grass with the biggest grin on his face!

When we reached the river, Toby was a little unsure at first. He sat at the edge, watching the water. But after a few minutes of building up his courage, he dipped his paws in and that was it, he was happily paddling back and forth, enjoying every second. It was such a special moment to watch.

I truly adore Toby with my whole heart, he’s one of those dogs who just stays with you, always on your mind.

He can still feel a bit unsure when meeting new people and might bark or back away at first, but give him a little time and patience, and he’ll become your most loyal, loving best friend.

I honestly can’t believe Toby is still waiting for his forever home. He is such a gentle, beautiful soul who deserves the absolute best life has to offer!

Toby is a sweet older gentleman who truly enjoys the quieter side of life. He loves nothing more than snuggling up for a nap and being close to his people.

Toby still has a playful spark and enjoys his daily walks as well as pottering around the yard. He would thrive in a calm, peaceful home and is best suited to a household with no children or cats, where he can relax and enjoy his golden years in comfort.

I love Toby. He is so loved by many of us here at the rescue. He's a confident boy once he knows you, but until he feels comfortable around you he can bark and sometimes be a bit standoffish.

Toby is a big cuddle bunny, he absolutely loves a fuss, and will happily accept butt scratches any time of the day.

He enjoys going out for walks but absolutely loves being off lead and running around the big play yard, when his butt wiggles with happiness and excitement it really doesn't stop, it's super adorable. He likes chasing a tennis ball but he won't bring it back, instead he rolls around with it usually in his mouth and will then lay with it and play with it, he's a comical boy.

Again, once he's comfortable with you he's very easy to handle, I can get a coat or a jumper on him with no problems, I can pick him up and I can brush him with no problems, he had a groom recently and he was no issue at all.

It's a shame he keeps getting overlooked, yes he might have some typical cocker issues such as guarding, but it hasn't been a huge issue since he's been here, I can go in and out of his kennel, pick things up etc and he's been fine. I've also been yarding him with other dogs to try and socialise him more, and although he can be selective of who he likes, once he's found a friend then he just wants to play. He is a beautiful boy inside and out, and in my opinion anyone would be lucky to have him as part of their family.

Also he is kennel clean so house training shouldn't take any time at all.

Please, don't let Toby spend another year in kennels, he truly deserves to find his forever home, as they all do. It's getting colder, it's been snowing, a nice warm, cosy house with a loving family is what he wants, I know his forever home is out there somewhere so please come and find him.

Toby is still doing incredibly well with us here and hasn’t shown any signs of guarding, while this has stopped with us here we still are unsure how he will react in a home environment.

It is an absolute pleasure working with Toby and he always brings a smile to your face throughout the day. Toby is a gentle, loving and happy boy and is desperate to have somebody he can give all his love to.

Toby has definitely come out of his shell since he's been here, he still barks when you first see him but it's a happy bark and his tail doesn't stop, before he would stay for scratches for a little bit, but know he doesn't want to leave you and wants all the attention. He is a very loving dog.

Toby originally came to us from a breeder when he was around 3 months old. He was a terrified puppy who was worried about everything and would even squeak in fear when being handled. He was quickly adopted and found a loving home, but he has sadly been returned to our care as he was displaying some behaviours that his adopters felt unable to cope with.

Toby was homed with another dog and while they got along well, he did show some signs of guarding his adopter from the other dog, for this reason we now think he would be most suited to being homed as an only dog.

Toby can also sometimes grumble if people walk past the sofa or his bed and he is on them, so he will be looking for an adult only home with no visiting children, with adopters who have experience with dogs with similar issues and will be able to work on this with him. He did nip his adopter once around 18 months ago, but that was the only time that resulted in more than a grumble.

Toby is still quite a scared boy in some aspects and certain things will make him extremely nervous, such as the hoover or sometimes even minor things like the sounds of a drawer closing, but with confident owners with experience of scared dogs we do believe he will progress further. He would be best suited to a calm and quiet home, where he can settle in at his own pace and follow a routine.

He enjoys going for walks and is very good both on and off lead. He has good recall and gets along well with other dogs outside of the home. He can be reactive to bikes, so his adopters would need to be mindful of this and keep him on lead in any areas where he may encounter bikes and only let him off lead in secure areas.

As he has lived in a home before, we believe he is house trained, but he may need some reminders.

Toby is a sweet boy at heart and in the right home and with the right adopters we think he will thrive. Since his arrival with us he has been on his best behaviour and already adores all of the staff that work with him and they adore him too. He absolutely loves his food and has a true zest for life which makes us smile each day, so we are so hopeful that his perfect home is out there and will find him soon.

Toby was born with some deformed toes, which have since been amputated but don't seem to bother him, though he does walk with a slightly abnormal gait. He also has a short tail.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

name: Cooper
description:
I would like a calm and quiet, adult only home.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would love a good sized garden to explore!

I am a beginner to walking on a lead, but would like an active home.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am neutered and ready to find my forever home!

Meet Cooper, a lovely boy who has travelled all the way from Romania to begin his new life and search for his forever home. He is a sweet boy who was quite overwhelmed when he first arrived, but is starting to come out of his shell more and more each day. He can be worried when he first meets new people, but will now greet his kennel mummy with a wagging tail every day! Despite his worries, he is easy to handle and in the right home we think he will truly thrive.

Cooper absolutely adores other dogs and takes great comfort from having canine friends around him, so he will need another kind, confident and playful resident dog in his new home to be his companion and show him the ropes. He is also beginning to discover the joy of toys and is enjoying learning how to play, which is so sweet.

As Cooper has never lived in a home before, his adopters will need to be patient, kind and understanding while he settles in and learns all about home life, including new skills like house training. He is very much a beginner when it comes to walking on a lead and harness, but he is already starting to enjoy his walks and would love an active home where he can continue exploring the world at his own pace.

Cooper would love to find adopters who are experienced with dogs and, whilst not essential, experience with Romanian rescue dogs would be a bonus. He would be happiest in a calm, quiet, adult only home where he can settle in at his own pace and continue building his confidence. With patience, understanding and plenty of love, Cooper will start to discover just how wonderful his life can now be. In return, this gentle boy will reward his family with the privilege of watching him blossom into the happy and loved companion he was always meant to be.

He has tested negative prior to arrival for heartworm, lyme disease, ehrlichia, anaplasma, giardia, leishmania and brucellosis.

When Cooper first arrived, his world was filled with fear. He would quietly tuck himself away at the back of his kennel, very unsure of all his surroundings and who we all were. It was so heartbreaking to see how scared cooper really was.

But every day, with kindness, patience and love, Cooper has taken another tiny step forward. Those tiny steps have turned into giant leaps. Today, the Cooper who once hid away greets his kennel mum with a wagging tail every morning and spends his days happily playing or relaxing with his kennel friends. His personality is really staring to come through and he is slowly learning that the world isn't such a scary place.

When Cooper first arrived, he'd had very little experience walking on a lead. Now he is improving so much more, he even happily takes trips down to our big play yard!

Cooper still finds unfamiliar places and new people a little scary, but it doesn't take long for him to realise he's safe. Once he trusts you, you see the sweetest, gentlest soul who simply wants to love and be loved.

Cooper has done everything we've asked of him. He's been brave. He's learned to trust. He's opened his heart. Now, we're asking for someone to do the same for him.

This beautiful young boy shouldn't be growing up behind kennel doors. He should be learning about the world from the comfort of a sofa, chasing toys around a garden, falling asleep after long walks, and knowing what it feels like to be in a home.

I am so incredibly proud of the progress Cooper has made and I have no doubts in a home with all the patience and kindness he will blossom into the most amazing loving family member anyone could wish for.

Meet Cooper, a lovely boy who has travelled all the way from Romania to begin his new life and search for his forever home. He is a sweet boy who is quite overwhelmed to find himself here, but is starting to settle in and adjust to his new surroundings. Understandably, he is feeling quite scared at the moment, especially when he first meets new people. With those he knows, he is starting to come out of his shell and its lovely to see his confidence growing. Despite his worries, he is easy to handle and in the right home we think he will truly thrive.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Luca
description:
I'd like an active home and enjoy human company!

I’d like to be the only dog in the home. I can't live with cats or small furries!

I will need a large secure garden with minimum 6ft fencing.

I walk well on a lead and would enjoy an active lifestyle!

Please be patient with me, I haven’t lived in a home before.

I am neutered and ready to find my forever home! I have had 1 tooth extracted.

Luca is an incredible boy who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a fresh start. He already knows his name very well, so his new adopters should keep this the same to avoid confusing him as he settles into his new life.

Luca was previously used as a fake security dog and spent most of his life living outdoors, but beneath his impressive appearance is a real softie. He is easy to handle and genuinely enjoys human company, although he understandably found kennel life quite stressful when he first arrived and would often pace his kennel and the exercise yard, struggling to settle.

As Luca has become familiar with the routine, his surroundings and the staff at Many Tears, his confidence has grown enormously. One of the biggest changes we've seen is his newfound love of toys. For the first couple of weeks, he showed no interest in them at all, but now he absolutely adores them! His favourite game is a good game of fetch in the big yard, where he happily charges after his ball with great enthusiasm.

Like many large, playful dogs, Luca can occasionally become overexcited during play. He may jump up to catch the ball or become a little mouthy in his excitement, but this is never intended to cause harm. He is an incredibly gentle boy who simply gets carried away having fun. Because of his size and strength, we are helping him learn commands such as "sit", "wait" and "drop", as well as encouraging calmer play so he can enjoy himself without becoming overstimulated. This training will be important for his future adopters to continue, as an overexcited Luca could unintentionally knock over someone who is less steady on their feet.

Although he loves chasing a ball, Luca's absolute favourite toys are cuddly toys! He delights in carrying them around and showing off his softer side, which perfectly sums up his character.

Luca would be happiest as the only dog in the home, where he can enjoy all the attention, settle into a routine and build a strong bond with his new family. He will need adopters who have plenty of time to spend with him and who have experience of the breed or similar breeds. Luca cannot live with cats, small furries or small dogs.

As Luca has spent most of his life outdoors, he will need to learn about house training and the other basics of home life. With patient guidance and consistency, we are sure he will adapt well and enjoy all the comforts that a family home has to offer.

Luca already walks on a lead, although he can pull initially, so this is something his adopters will need to continue working on. He is an active, intelligent boy who would love a home where he can enjoy plenty of adventures, enrichment and quality time with his people. He is also a strong dog who can jump and even open gates, so he will need a very secure garden and confident handlers who can safely manage his strength.

Luca is an affectionate, loyal and wonderfully characterful boy who simply wants to be part of the family. Now that he has settled and his playful personality has begun to shine, it has been a joy to watch him embrace life. In the right home, with structure, ongoing training and plenty of love, Luca will make an incredibly rewarding companion.

Luca has had one tooth extracted at the time of his neuter.

Luca has been given the Gift of Life by Lynne Hughes

Before they arrive at Many Tears, many of our dogs have never had toys, and, as strange as it sounds, may not know what to do with them. Fetching, licking, and chewing are important forms of enrichment for dogs and can help to regulate their nervous system and reduce stress, but it can take a while for these dogs to figure out how to use toys in these ways. It's one of the reasons many of our dogs are recommended to have a resident dog at home, as they can learn from each other.

When Luca arrived, he did not engage with toys for the first two weeks or so. He was also very anxious, pacing his kennel and the yard and struggling to settle. However, as he has become used to the routine, surroundings, and staff at Many Tears, Luca has settled very well and discovered a love of all sorts of toys!

We try to give our dogs a mix of toys and enrichment until we know what they like. Luca is not very interested in food-based enrichment like LickiMats or Kongs. He will tug-of-war hesitantly with a rope toy but doesn't really engage with it. However, Luca LOVES a game of fetch down the big yard. He may occasionally jump up to try and get the ball and become over-excited and mouthy, so we are working on balancing his stimulation so he can get his energy out without getting worked up, and on commands like "sit", "wait", and "drop". Luca is incredibly gentle and does not want to hurt anyone, but he is a big boy and could knock a vulnerable person down if he gets too over-excited, so this kind of training is important.

Luca's FAVOURITE type of toy, though, is cuddly toys! It just proves what a big softie he is, as he really loves nothing more than carrying around his stuffed pig toy or cwtching up with his favourite, a string of stuffed Brussels sprouts. It's really lovely to see him relax and enjoy himself this way. Even better when he's doing it on your lap!

Luca is loved by all the staff and volunteers who meet him, but he's definitely ready to be someone's best friend.

Luca was previously used as a fake security dog and has spent most of his life living outside, but beneath his big appearance he is a real softie. He is easy to handle and enjoys human company, though he has understandably found kennel life quite stressful and will often plead with us to come back when we have to leave him.

Luca would be happiest and thrive best as the only dog in the home, where he can enjoy all the attention, settle more easily into a routine, and build a strong bond with his new family. He will need adopters who have plenty of time to spend with him and who have experience of the breed or similar breeds. Luca cannot live with cats or small furries and he cannot be around small dogs.

As Luca has spent most of his life outdoors, he will need to learn about house training and the other basics of home life. He will need patient adopters who can help guide him through these new experiences as he adjusts to living in a home environment.

Luca can already walk on a lead, though he does pull at first and so this is something his adopters will need to work on with him. He is a very active boy, so he would love an active household where he can enjoy plenty of adventures and become a loyal companion once he is settled in. He is a strong dog and can both jump and open gates, so he will need a very secure garden and confident handlers who are able to manage his strength safely.

Luca is an intelligent, affectionate, and loyal boy who simply wants to be close to his people. In the right home, with structure, companionship, and plenty of love, he will make an incredibly rewarding companion.

Luca has had 1 tooth extracted at the time of his neuter.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

name: Grape
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in.

I’ve learnt how to walk on lead but its still a bit scary for me.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training.

Grape came into our care from a breeder in search of a fresh start. When she first arrived, she was a very worried little girl who clearly hadn't experienced much human interaction and found the world an overwhelming place. Despite her fears, she always tried so hard to be brave, gently accepting strokes while she learned that people could be kind.

Size wise Grape weighs approximately 14.5 kg. She's a lovely medium-sized girl, around the size of a cocker spaniel.

Fast forward a few months, and Grape has come on in leaps and bounds. She still has a sensitive soul, but each day we see more of the happy, playful little girl she was always destined to be.

When Grape first arrived, her coat was dirty and badly matted, so her first groom was more of a fresh start than a pamper. Now that her beautiful curls have grown back, she recently enjoyed a proper makeover to show off what an adorable little teddy bear she really is. The bath was a little scary for her, but she coped brilliantly, and by the end she was a gorgeous fluffy princess, looking every bit as special as she is.

One of Grape's biggest achievements has been her growing confidence. She is now walking on a lead and is doing really well, although she isn't quite 100% confident yet, particularly with people she doesn't know well. With someone she trusts, she is making fantastic progress and continues to improve every day.

She absolutely adores other dogs and gets on wonderfully with every dog she meets. Their company gives her confidence, and because of this shewill need a kind, confident resident dogin her new home to help guide and reassure her as she continues to settle into family life. We recently caught Grape playing for the very first time, doing joyful little bounces around a tennis ball. It may seem like a small thing, but for Grape it was a huge milestone and another step away from the life she once knew.

Although she's still a little nervous about human fuss, she now greets us every morning with a waggy tail and the sweetest smile. She's also a complete sucker for treats, making winning her over much easier! She is still learning about life in a home, so her new family will need to continue her house training, build her confidence, and help her discover all the joys of being a much-loved pet. A calm, patient home with adopters who understand ex-breeding dogs would suit her perfectly.

When Grape arrived she was a little overweight, but with a healthy diet and gentle exercise she has been making great progress. She has also been through quite a lot medically since arriving with us. She has been spayed, had two teeth extracted, undergone a hernia repair, and had a small cyst removed during her spay. Her hormonal alopecia should continue to improve following her spay, and she has also completed treatment for an ear infection.

We truly cannot understand why Grape has been overlooked for so long. She has blossomed into such a sweet, gentle little dog, and while she will need a family willing to continue building her confidence, the rewards of watching her flourish will be immeasurable.

Grape has been given the Gift of Life Wendy Stewart

Sweet, sensitive Grape has now been with us for around three months, and we honestly can't understand why she hasn't had floods of interest. She is such a lovely little dog who has come on in leaps and bounds since arriving at the rescue.

When Grape first came to us, her coat was dirty and badly matted, so her first groom was more of a fresh start than a pamper. Now that her beautiful curls have grown back, we thought she deserved a proper makeover to show everyone what an adorable little teddy bear she really is. The bath was a little scary for her, but she coped so well, and she was an absolute star with the dryer (apart from preferring us not to fuss around her head too much!). By the end, she was transformed into a gorgeous, fluffy little princess, ready to strut around the rescue.

It's not just her appearance that's blossomed. Grape has grown so much in confidence over the last few weeks. She is now walking on a lead and is doing really well, although she's still not 100% confident, especially with people she doesn't know well. With someone she trusts, she is making fantastic progress and continues to improve every day.

One of the loveliest things about Grape is how much she adores other dogs. She delights in every dog she meets and loves having canine friends around her. We even caught her playing for the very first time, doing playful little bounces around a tennis ball. It might seem like an ordinary moment, but for Grape it was a huge milestone and another step further away from the life she once knew.

She can still be a little nervous about human fuss, but every morning she greets us with a waggy tail and the sweetest smile. Each day she lets her guard down a little more, and we're seeing more of the happy, playful girl she was always meant to be. She's also very partial to treats, which definitely helps when making new friends!

Grape would make a wonderful addition to almost any family that's happy to give her a little patience and understanding while she continues to build her confidence. We truly cannot understand why this gorgeous little girl has been overlooked for so long.

Grape is still a nervous girlie and is taking longer to trust humans, given we know nothing of her past this is understandable.

I am trying to show her that all I want to do is help her and show her love, while also respecting her space and going slowly with her, which is what her adopters may have to do depending on where’s she’s at.

She will allow a gentle fuss when she’s in her bed but will not willingly come up and ask for one yet. I think maybe in a calm home she will start to feel more comfortable, kennel life isn’t for everyone, and learn to trust humans.

She is a beautiful girl and I hope she starts to trust soon so we can see that amazing and sweet personality that I’m sure is hiding in her somewhere just bursting to come out.

Grape has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. She is a scared girl who is quite overwhelmed to find herself here at the moment and clearly isn't used to much human interaction, so finds this quite worrying at the moment. Despite her fears she will let you gently stroke her and is trying so hard to be brave.

She will be looking for a calm and quiet home where she can settle in at her own pace and would benefit from adopters with experience of ex-breeding dogs. She gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends and relies on their company for comfort, so she will need a kind resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in and finds her paws.

As Grape has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training, and the other basics of home life. Everything will be new to her, so a calm and consistent routine will be important.

Grape has arrived a little overweight, but with a good diet and gentle exercise, she should soon start to shed the excess. She has some hormonal alopecia, but this should start to grow back now she has been spayed. She has had 2 teeth extracted as well as a hernia repair and our vets have noted she has a small cyst, which was removed at the time of her spay. She is also being treated for a ear infection.

Grape is a very worried little girl at the moment, but with time, patience, and the support of another dog, she has the potential to slowly gain confidence and begin to show more of her true character.

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Buck
description:
I would like an active home filled with love and kindness!

I can be an only dog or live with a calm female dog.

I would love a garden to run and play in!

I can walk well on a harness and would love an active home.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have no tail, but this doesn't bother me!

Please meet the very handsome Buck, who has travelled all the way from Romania in the hope of finding his forever home. Since arriving here a few months ago, Buck has truly blossomed! Initially a little shy with new people, he now settles quickly and happily shows off his affectionate, gentle nature. He loves attention, enjoys fuss, and is more than happy to make new friends once he feels comfortable.

Buck is such a comical boy, always finding little ways to make you smile, but he is also incredibly affectionate. He has that spark of energy that brightens even the hardest of days.

Buck absolutely loves his food. You’ll hear his excited bark echo around the rescue at mealtimes without fail. He also really enjoys his walks and having a good run around the big yard, where he can let out all that happy energy. Buck also has the most cuddly side to him; he loves nothing more than resting his head on your lap while he slowly dozes off to sleep.

Buck was briefly adopted but was sadly returned as he didn't get along with the resident dog. Buck enjoys the company of well mannered female does and does enjoy sharing his kennel with another dog, so we would consider homing him with a laid back female dog if they were the right match. He can get a little jealous of sharing attention with another dog, but in the right home with experienced adopters this could be managed. That said, Buck would be equally happy to be homed as the only dog and get all the love and attention for himself.

Buck will be looking for an adult only home and would be best suited to adopters who have experience of owning dogs from a similar background before and who are around most of the time, so they can spend lots of time with him. He would love to find an active home where he can be kept both physically and mentally stimulated and enjoy plenty of walks and adventures with his new family.

Although Buck had never lived in a home before being adopted, he settled in wonderfully and was clean in the house. He wasn’t phased by the TV or radio and quickly found the sofas and beds! He can still be a little shy when first meeting men, but it doesn’t take him long to warm up. Buck also isn’t keen on sudden loud noises or sticks and brooms, so this is something his adopters will need to work on desensitising him to. He doesn’t like having his front paws touched, but he will politely let you know by gently pulling them away.

Buck is a truly special boy with so much love to give. He is absolutely wasted in kennels and will make a loyal, devoted companion for a very lucky family. He arrived with no tail, but this doesn’t bother him in the slightest and only adds to his charm. Please don’t overlook this wonderful lad, as Buck is more than ready to find his forever home.

Buck has received negative test results for Brucellosis, Leishmania, Giardia, Heartworm, Ehrlichia canis, Borrelia burgdorferi and Anaplasma.

Buck will need more than one meet and greet with his prospective adopters to allow him time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

Buck has now been with us for 7 months and is still patiently waiting for his forever home.

Buck absolutely loves the people he knows and trusts. If Buck is unsure of someone, it will take him awhile to come out of his shell and get to know them, but once they've built a bond with him, he is the most loving gentle boy, who loves attention!

Buck has plenty of doggy friends and enjoys socialising outside of his kennel environment, although he definitely has a preference for the ladies and gets on best with female dogs.

Buck can potentially live with another calm female dog who will respect his space when he needs it.

Buck is looking for an adopters who will give him the time he needs to settle and understand that he can be a very worried boy at first.

I do genuinely love Buck with my entire heart. I would love nothing more than seeing him finally settling into home life, with people who will cherish him just as much as I do!

For the past few weeks, Buck has been front and centre in our big yard play group! This is a great chance for our people-shy new dogs to meet and play with more confident long-stayers like Buck, and he's met a lot of new dogs this way, which suggests that once he's settled into his new home, he might benefit from a dog park or opportunities to meet up with friends.

Buck's best friend is another Romanian dog called Olive. You rarely see one without the other, in their yard, the big yard, or on walks! Sometimes in big yard play group, Bucky and Olive will separate from the other dogs and chase and wrestle each other for a while, and it's lovely to see. Unfortunately, Buck and Olive don't like to be kenneled together as they prefer their own space to unwind after all that time spent playing.

However, Buck has really come out of his shell with people around the rescue. He has a few people he's very close to, and is always up for cwtches with them. How can you say no that handsome face? He's also happier now to meet new people than he used to be, and now goes on walks with volunteers (accompanied, of course, by Olive) most days.

Buck can still get possessive over his favourite people, which is something we have to be aware of in big yard play group and that his adopters will need to bear in mind. He may grumble at other dogs in warning if they get too close when he's having his cuddles, though this does not usually escalate beyond a warning snap. It's likely that our sweet Bucky may not have had stable affection in his past, so he feels the need to guard that love from other dogs.

Luckily for Buck, we have plenty of love to go around at Many Tears! Hopefully, as he settles, he'll realise he is safe and loved and doesn't have to guard anyone anymore.

I’ve had the absolute pleasure of working with Buck, or “Buckaroo” as I like to call him, since the very day he arrived with us. I know you’re not supposed to have favourites, but if I’m honest, Buck has completely stolen a place in my heart.

Buck is such a comical boy, always finding little ways to make you smile, but he is also incredibly affectionate. He has that spark of energy that can turn even the hardest days into better ones.

Buck’s kennel friend, who he came over from Romania with, has recently been adopted. He adored her so much, and since she left, there’s been a little piece of him missing. Now he is the one still waiting, and it is heartbreaking knowing he doesn’t understand why it is not his turn yet.

Although Buck has shared his kennel and enjoys playdates with other dogs, always greeting them nicely out on walks, he would also thrive as the only dog in a home. He loves human attention so deeply and would really benefit from having people around most of the time to give him the love, comfort, and reassurance he deserves.

I recently took Buck out for a day to a local beach. From the moment we arrived, he was in his absolute element and enjoyed every second of it. Buck spent the majority of the time on a long line; although he ran around and explored, he also came back to me when called and always turned to make sure I was still close. This just shows how much of a loyal companion he can be.

I honestly love Buck with my whole heart, and it breaks me a little every single day knowing he is still waiting for his people to come for him. He has so much love, loyalty, and joy to give; he just needs someone to give him that chance.

It’s been a few weeks since Bucks arrival, and oh my has he made his presence known. Every single staff member who has had the pleasure of meeting this boy is utterly obsessed, and it’s very clear as to why!

Buck’s energy is infectious, he is the happiest, bounciest, most adoring little man and whoever adopts him will be truly lucky!!! When you meet him you’d never assume he is 6 years old - he exudes puppy energy.

Buck loves to play with his fellow Romanian buddy Jenny and they get along great. He also goes for play dates with the lovely Orietta, and he thoroughly enjoys it. He would like adopters who have experience with owning dogs before and who are around most of the time.

This sweet sweet boy is absolutely wasted in kennels, he is bursting with love to give and he’ll make a very lucky someone the happiest person in the world. Our foreign dogs are often overlooked and tend to hang around in kennels much longer than needed - please don’t let this be the case for our lovely Buck.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Rachel
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

i have never been on walks, but may be too scared and will need some time.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have had a pea size cyst removed from my right shoulder at the time of spay.

Rachel is a very scared girl who has come to us from a breeder. She is understandably overwhelmed by her new surroundings and clearly hasn’t had much socialisation before. However, since being with us, she has slowly started to show small signs of progress as she begins to realise she is safe. Although she still finds being handled very frightening, we are beginning to see small but meaningful improvements in her trust, and she is looking for a home with adopters experienced with traumatised ex-breeding dogs who can provide the reassurance and stability she needs to continue building her confidence and learning about trust and kindness.

She will need an adult-only home that can offer a calm and predictable environment where she can take things at her own pace. Rachel will also need at least one kind and confident resident dog to help guide her and provide comfort, as she can still become easily overwhelmed, but she takes great reassurance from the presence of other dogs and shares everything beautifully with her kennel companions.

Rachel has never lived in a home before, so she will need very patient and understanding adopters while she learns about house training, walking on a lead and accepting gentle handling. The big wide world still feels quite scary for her, but she is beginning to show curiosity in safe environments, and gentle time in the garden will be a great way to help her slowly explore and build confidence. She follows a daily routine beautifully, happily running out to the exercise yards and returning to her kennel when it's time to come back in. She also tries her best to keep her kennel clean, and we feel she is likely to pick up house training very quickly once she has regular access to a garden.

Rachel is only acting out of fear, but we are continuing to see glimpses of a softer side as she begins to relax in familiar surroundings. Although she still tries her best to avoid being touched and may attempt to bite when she feels frightened, her reactions are already less severe than when she first arrived. Recently, Rachel needed to have her thick coat clipped during the warm weather, which unfortunately had to be done under sedation as she is not yet ready to be groomed. Despite how frightening this experience must have been for her, she coped far better than we ever expected, allowing herself to be carried to the vets and held for her injection once she was safely in our arms. We couldn't have been prouder of how brave she was. As her coat grows back, we will continue gently introducing her to grooming so she can slowly learn that being brushed doesn't have to be scary.

However, she still has the potential and will act on it to bite if she is backed into a corner, specifically when she is being picked up and handled. It is imperative her adopters understand these behaviours.

Rachel has so much potential and, with time, patience and kindness, we truly believe she will continue to make progress and learn that she is safe and loved. She really is an easy dog to care for in every other aspect – she is wonderful with other dogs, thrives on routine and never puts a paw wrong. She just needs a truly understanding home where she can continue building on the trust she has started to develop and finally blossom into the dog she is meant to be.

Rachel came to us with a pea-sized cyst on her shoulder, which was removed at the time of her spay.

Rachel has been given the Gift of Life by Tracy Davidson

Rachel’s progress continues slowly and steadily and even though she still doesn’t like to be touched, she is so much more content and calm in general. She’s now more than happy to hang out with me and lay down near me, and just this week she actually went to sleep next to me with her tummy exposed!!! I know that may not sound like a lot, but it’s HUGE for a dog like Rachel with such severe trust issues.

The past couple of weeks at the rescue have been extremely warm and Rachel started to struggle a little bit with having such thick fur, so I decided to get it shaved off. Rachel is still not ready to be groomed, so I did have to take her into the vets to be sedated. This is the first time I’ve had to actually pick her up since I started going the crate and touch work with her, but it had to be done. She does still try her very best to get away and she does still try to bite, but it is less severe than what it was when she first came in. Getting her into my arms was the most difficult part, but after I had hold of her I was able to walk over to the vets carrying her, and hold her while she had her injection without a fuss. I was so, so proud of her. She’s now a bit bald, but so much more comfortable and cooler. When her fur starts to grow back I am going to start introducing her to a brush so she can get used to it, as her coat does grow quite fast and it’s very dense which means it gets matted easily. It’s not ideal for a dog like Rachel needing to be groomed regularly, but I’ll try my very best to ease her into it.

Looking after Rachel on a daily basis is very easy. She follows routine beautifully - running to the play yards and back into her kennel when it’s time to come in. She tries her best to be clean with her toileting and I think if she had access to a garden regularly, she would pick it up really quickly. She also shares everything with her kennel friends perfectly and she never puts a paw wrong with other dogs. Aside from hating being touched, she really isn’t a problem at all. I really am hoping that she’ll start to get used to it soon, and I think she will … but being in a home would help massively. So I hope she doesn’t have to wait too much longer for that to happen.

For the past month, Rachel has officially been my “project dog”. This means I’ve been spending a lot more time working directly with her, and I set a goal for both of us when I started. Because Rachel’s biggest fear is human hands, that became my main focus — helping her feel more comfortable with being touched and gently stroked.

In the first week, I wanted to get her used to my touch without her panicking. When Rachel thinks she’s about to be handled, she’ll run around the kennel, jumping from bed to bed to avoid me, and will bite to protect herself if I get too close. I felt that all the running and panic was only reinforcing her fear, making things harder for both of us. So, I introduced a crate to safely contain her in a smaller space, allowing me to begin gentle handling in a more controlled way.

My hope was that she would start to realise that a soft fuss on her head or body isn’t actually that scary — that the anticipation was worse than the reality. Each day for that first week, I set up a crate at the back of her kennel and spent a short session gently touching her, just once a day to ease her into it.

On the first day, it took a little while for her to go into the crate, but she eventually went in with her friend. She was actually very good and allowed me to gently stroke her face for a few minutes, before becoming a little unsettled and starting to nibble my hand. By the second day, she went into the crate much more quickly and again allowed strokes around her head and under her ears. As I carefully moved further down her body, she became uncomfortable and nibbled a bit harder to let me know she’d had enough.

By the third day, she went straight into the crate, and I focused more on her body. She allowed longer strokes before becoming unsettled. The fourth day was very similar, but on the fifth day there was a real breakthrough — she let me stroke her tummy and chest without any nibbles at all.

After every session, I made sure to sit at the front of her kennel for a few minutes and give her treats so we always ended on a positive note (and to make sure she was still my friend!). Rachel is known to hold a grudge, so maintaining that trust was really important, and thankfully this work hasn’t damaged our relationship at all.

In week two, my goal was to remove the crate and see if she would choose to stay settled in a bed while I handled her. I wasn’t sure how it would go, but she absolutely amazed me. On the first day, she settled into a bed at the back of the kennel while I sat on the floor and gently shuffled towards her — and she stayed still, allowing me to stroke her. I kept things consistent over the next few days without pushing her too far.

By the fifth day, I introduced something new: scissors around her head. She needs a fringe trim, so I wanted to begin desensitising her to the sensation and presence of them. She did incredibly well — so well, in fact, that I managed to snip a tiny bit, which I hadn’t even planned to do. Because she was coping so calmly, I took the opportunity, and it paid off.

In week three, I continued trimming her fringe gradually, little by little. After a few days, I was able to clear the hair from around her eyes.

That’s where we are now. There’s still a long way to go, and Rachel will need plenty more time, patience and love, but I’m so pleased with how far she’s come. We’ve definitely made real progress, and I’m excited to keep building on it with her.

Rachel has been at the rescue for just over a month now and in that time she’s gained a lot of inner confidence, and has blossomed into a very cheeky and happy girl who always seems to be up to mischief!! She absolutely loves toys and gets very excited when I put them in her kennel every morning, and she also loves playing with them in the yards. She’s also very partial to starting ‘parties’ AKA getting all the dogs to have a massive game of chase with her, which she finds very amusing. Her favourite thing in the world though … food!!! She is one of the foodiest dogs I’ve ever met and is always at the front of the queue for breakfast, dinner, and treats.Even though Rachel has made progress in many areas, one thing she still simply can’t handle is being touched by us humans in any way. Her fear of our hands is so strong and she will try to bite to protect herself. This doesn’t mean she’s a nasty dog in any way, it’s just complete panic and fear. It’s something I’m trying to de-sensitise her to and I’m working with her as much as I can, but I do think it’s going to take a long time and a lot of consistency. We don’t know what she’s been through in her life that’s made her the way she is, so all we can do now is prove to her that humans can be kind, and hope that one day she’s able to put her past behind her.Rachel will need a very experienced home with people who will be extremely patient with her, understand her, and work with her through her worries and fears. She’ll need at least 1 resident dog to learn from, and absolutely no children. Things that are normal to most dogs such as going for a walk, being brushed/groomed, or even just having a little fuss, are alien to Rachel, so it’s important her adopters take all of this into consideration and be okay with it.

It may be a long and slow road to get Rachel to where she needs to be, but I promise it will be so worth it. There is no better feeling than a dog like her showing you love and trust for the first time!

Rachel is a very scared girl who has come to us from a breeder. She is a very scared girl at the moment who is quite overwhelmed to find herself here and clearly hasn't had much socialisation before. She is looking for a home with adopters with experience of scared ex-breeding dogs who can provide the reassurance and stability she needs to help build her confidence as she learns about safety, trust, and our intentions.

She will need an adult-only home that can offer a calm and predictable environment where she can take things at her own pace. Rachel will also need at least one kind and confident resident dog to help her settle in and take her under their wing, as she can be easily overwhelmed at the moment.

Rachel has never lived in a home before, so she will need patient and understanding adopters while she learns about house training and how to walk on a lead. Right now, the big wide world may feel too overwhelming for her, so gentle sniffs in the garden would be a good place to start.

Rachel is only acting out of fear, and we have not yet been able to see the girl she will become once she feels safe. She deserves so much love, she just isn’t sure how to accept it yet and will need a truly understanding home to help her blossom.

Rachel has come to us with a pea sized cyst on her shoulder that has been removed at the time of her spay.
